summary: The Board must deny an award if it finds the victim or claimant did not fully cooperate with law enforcement, unless a substantial medical, mental health, or safety risk was the reason. To decide, the Board looks at things like whether the victim or claimant failed to help the prosecution or failed to appear as a witness for it.
quote: The Board shall deny a compensation award to a claimant if: 1. The Board determines that the victim or claimant did not cooperate fully with the appropriate law enforcement agency and the failure to cooperate fully was not due to a substantial medical, mental health, or safety risk. The Board shall use the following criteria to determine whether failure to cooperate fully with law enforcement warrants that a claim be denied: a. The victim or claimant failed to assist in the prosecution of a person who engaged in the criminally injurious conduct or failed to appear as a witness for the prosecution;
source_title: A.A.C. Title 10, Chapter 4 (Arizona Criminal Justice Commission), Article 1 Crime Victim Compensation Program, Supp. 26-1

summary: The award is denied or reduced when the loss was or can be recovered from insurance, a government benefit, or another collateral source.

summary: An award may be denied or reduced in proportion to how much the Board finds the victim responsible for the incident.

summary: By statute, any records, claims, or information a district board or district attorney receives, makes, or keeps to process a crime victim compensation claim are confidential.
quote: Any materials received, made, or kept by a board or a district attorney to process a claim on behalf of a crime victim under this article are confidential.
source_title: C.R.S. 24-4.1-107.5 (Confidentiality of materials), via Justia

summary: No cost of a sexual assault evidence collection exam, including pregnancy and STI testing and preventive treatment under the state protocol, may be charged directly or indirectly to the survivor.
quote: No costs incurred by a health care facility for the examination of a victim of sexual assault, when such examination is performed for the purpose of gathering evidence as prescribed in the protocol, including the costs of testing for pregnancy and sexually transmitted diseases and the costs of prophylactic treatment as provided in the protocol, and no costs incurred for a medical forensic assessment interview conducted by a health care facility or provider or by an examiner working in conjunction with a multidisciplinary team established pursuant to section 17a-106a or with a child advocacy center, shall be charged directly or indirectly to such victim.
source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 368a, including sec. 19a-112a (sexual assault evidence collection costs)

params: {"payer":"Forensic Sex Evidence Exams account, Connecticut Judicial Department"}
summary: Exam costs are charged to the Forensic Sex Evidence Exams account in the Judicial Department.
quote: Any such costs shall be charged to the Forensic Sex Evidence Exams account in the Judicial Department.
source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 368a, including sec. 19a-112a (sexual assault evidence collection costs)

summary: Toxicology screening done under the protocol may not be charged to the survivor; the state Division of Scientific Services pays.
quote: No costs incurred by a health care facility for any toxicology screening of a victim of sexual assault, when such screening is performed as prescribed in the protocol, shall be charged directly or indirectly to such victim. Any such costs shall be charged to the Division of Scientific Services within the Department of Emergency Services and Public Protection.
source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 368a, including sec. 19a-112a (sexual assault evidence collection costs)

summary: Compensation for a personal injury is capped at $15,000.
quote: Compensation for personal injury shall be in an amount not to exceed fifteen thousand dollars
source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

summary: When the only injury is emotional harm (a mental or emotional impairment caused by a threat of physical injury or death), compensation for medical care, mental health care and security measures is capped at $5,000. Claims involving actual bodily harm fall under the higher personal injury cap above instead.
quote: in cases of emotional harm only, compensation for medical and mental health care and security measures shall be in an amount not to exceed five thousand dollars
source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

summary: Crime scene cleanup and security system expenses share one maximum benefit of $1,000 (not $1,000 each).
quote: CRIME SCENE CLEANUP AND SECURITY SYSTEM EXPENSES (maximum benefit $1,000)
source_title: Personal Injury Application, JD-VS-8PI (Rev. 7/21)

summary: Replacing clothes and bedding held as evidence falls under the same single up-to-$1,000 benefit as crime scene cleanup and security systems, not a separate $1,000.
quote: Up to $1,000 for crime scene cleanup, security systems, or replacement of clothes and bedding held as evidence
pinpoint: JDP-VS-10 brochure, Examples of Eligible Expenses
source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Program brochure, JDP-VS-10 (Rev. 9/26)

summary: Crime scene cleanup shares the single $1,000 maximum benefit with security system expenses.
quote: CRIME SCENE CLEANUP AND SECURITY SYSTEM EXPENSES (maximum benefit $1,000)
source_title: Personal Injury Application, JD-VS-8PI (Rev. 7/21)

summary: The program can award up to $5,000 more than the limits above to a victim who is a minor when the application is filed and has extra medical or counseling needs.
quote: the Office of Victim Services or a victim compensation commissioner may award additional compensation in an amount not to exceed five thousand dollars above the maximum amounts set forth in said subdivision to a personal injury victim, who is a minor at the time the application for compensation or restitution services is filed, when such victim has additional medical needs or mental health counseling needs
source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

summary: The program can also award more than the limits above for good cause, when it finds compelling reasons of fairness.
quote: the Office of Victim Services or a victim compensation commissioner may, for good cause shown and upon a finding of compelling equitable circumstances, award compensation in an amount in excess of the maximum amounts set forth in said subdivision
source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

summary: The program may pay expenses actually and reasonably incurred because of the injury, and must cover medical care for a victim with no insurance or whose coverage is used up.
quote: (1) Expenses actually and reasonably incurred as a result of the personal injury or death of the victim, provided coverage for the cost of medical care and treatment of a crime victim who does not have medical insurance or who has exhausted coverage under applicable health insurance policies or Medicaid shall be ordered
source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

summary: Mental health therapy prescribed by a licensed medical or mental health professional is a covered benefit, including individual, family and group therapy.
quote: Mental health therapy including individual, family, group, medication management, music therapy, art therapy, horse assisted therapy, psychotherapy, tutoring, personal trainer, gym membership, and summer camp prescribed by a licensed medical or mental health professional
source_title: Victim Compensation Program Benefits chart, JD-VS-47 (Rev. 7-24)

summary: Dental fees and dentures are listed as covered medical expenses.
quote: Hospital, doctor, cosmetic, and dental fees; co-pays and other medical related expenses, such as physical therapy, ambulance, prescription expenses, medical equipment, eyeglasses, dentures, and supplies
source_title: Victim Compensation Program Benefits chart, JD-VS-47 (Rev. 7-24)

summary: Prescription expenses are listed as covered medical expenses.
quote: Hospital, doctor, cosmetic, and dental fees; co-pays and other medical related expenses, such as physical therapy, ambulance, prescription expenses, medical equipment, eyeglasses, dentures, and supplies
source_title: Victim Compensation Program Benefits chart, JD-VS-47 (Rev. 7-24)

summary: The program may pay for loss of earning power caused by the victim's total or partial incapacity.
quote: (2) loss of earning power as a result of total or partial incapacity of such victim
source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

summary: In physical injury cases, travel expenses to attend court, Psychiatric Security Review Board, and Board of Pardons and Paroles proceedings are covered.
quote: For physical injury and homicide cases, lost wages and travel expenses for the victim and/or relatives to attend proceedings at court, the Psychiatric Security Review Board, and the Board of Pardons and Paroles
source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Program brochure, JDP-VS-10 (Rev. 9/26)

summary: Security systems, lock, door and window repair, and clothes and bedding held as evidence are covered, subject to the program maximum for this benefit.
quote: Costs for replacement or repair of damaged locks, doors, and windows; clothes and bedding held as evidence; biohazard clean-up; and the cost and installation of security systems
pinpoint: JD-VS-47, Crime Scene Clean-up and Security Systems
source_title: Victim Compensation Program Benefits chart, JD-VS-47 (Rev. 7-24)

params: {"expense":"clothing_bedding","scope":"replacing clothes and bedding held as evidence"}
summary: Replacing clothes and bedding held as evidence is a covered benefit, inside the shared crime scene cleanup and security maximum.
quote: Costs for replacement or repair of damaged locks, doors, and windows; clothes and bedding held as evidence; biohazard clean-up; and the cost and installation of security systems
pinpoint: JD-VS-47, Crime Scene Clean-up and Security Systems
source_title: Victim Compensation Program Benefits chart, JD-VS-47 (Rev. 7-24)

summary: Biohazard cleanup of a crime scene is a covered benefit, inside the shared crime scene cleanup and security maximum.
quote: Costs for replacement or repair of damaged locks, doors, and windows; clothes and bedding held as evidence; biohazard clean-up; and the cost and installation of security systems
pinpoint: JD-VS-47, Crime Scene Clean-up and Security Systems
source_title: Victim Compensation Program Benefits chart, JD-VS-47 (Rev. 7-24)

summary: Property loss and damage is not an eligible expense, so a lost or damaged phone or other belongings would not be paid. The narrow exceptions are the shared crime scene cleanup, security and evidence clothing and bedding benefit.
quote: Property loss and damage, pain and suffering, and travel to and from medical appointments are not eligible expenses.
source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Program brochure, JDP-VS-10 (Rev. 9/26)

summary: Travel to and from medical appointments is not an eligible expense.
quote: Property loss and damage, pain and suffering, and travel to and from medical appointments are not eligible expenses.
source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Program brochure, JDP-VS-10 (Rev. 9/26)

summary: The statute bars compensation for property crime losses and for pain and suffering.
quote: no compensation shall be awarded for losses sustained for crimes against property or for noneconomic detriment such as pain and suffering
source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

summary: The application must be made within 3 years after the date of the injury.
quote: the application has been made within three years after the date of the personal injury or death
source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

params: {"years":3,"from":"crime","extension":"waiver for physical, emotional or psychological injury"}
summary: A person who missed the 3-year deadline because of physical, emotional or psychological injuries caused by the crime may apply for a waiver.
quote: fails to make application for compensation within three years after the date of the personal injury or death as a result of physical, emotional or psychological injuries caused by such personal injury or death may apply for a waiver of such time limitation
source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

summary: If you were a minor and, through no fault of your own, did not apply within 3 years, you may ask for a waiver. The Office of Victim Services may grant it if it finds you were not at fault.
quote: any minor, including, but not limited to, a minor who is a victim of conduct by another person that constitutes a violation of section 53a-192a or a criminal violation of 18 USC Chapter 77, who, before, on or after October 1, 2005, fails to make application for compensation within three years after the date of the personal injury or death through no fault of the minor, may apply for a waiver of such time limitation. The Office of Victim Services, upon a finding that such minor is not at fault, may grant such waiver.
source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

summary: The Office of Victim Services may also waive the time limit for good cause, if it finds compelling reasons that make this fair.
quote: Notwithstanding the provisions of subdivision (1), (2) or (3) of this subsection, the Office of Victim Services may, for good cause shown and upon a finding of compelling equitable circumstances, waive the time limitations of subdivision (1) of this subsection.
source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

summary: The crime must be reported to police, but a sexual assault survivor does not lose eligibility for skipping the report if they went to a health care facility within 120 hours of the assault for an evidence collection exam, or met the disclosure or protective order rules of section 54-209(d).
quote: (C) such incident or offense has been reported to the police, except that a victim of a sexual assault shall not be ineligible for the payment of compensation by reason of failing to make a report pursuant to this subparagraph if such victim presented himself or herself to a health care facility within one hundred twenty hours of such sexual assault for examination and collection of evidence of such sexual assault in accordance with the provisions of section 19a-112a , or if such victim complied with subsection (d) of section 54-209 .
source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

summary: A police report is still the default, but for sexual assault offenses, disclosing the injury to a listed professional, such as a sexual assault counselor, a nurse or physician, or a mental health professional, can stand in for it if the office reasonably concludes the offense occurred.
quote: (K) a domestic violence counselor or a sexual assault counselor, as defined in section 52-146k
source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

summary: A police report is still the default, but reporting the injury in a restraining order or civil protection order application, where the order was granted after a hearing, can stand in for it if the office reasonably concludes the offense occurred.
quote: the personal injury is reported in an application for a restraining order under section 46b-15 or an application for a civil protection order under section 46b-16a or on the record to the court, provided such restraining order or civil protection order was granted in the Superior Court following a hearing
source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

summary: The award takes into account money the applicant received or can receive from other sources, such as insurance and workers' compensation; life insurance is not counted.
quote: shall take into consideration any amounts that the applicant has received or is eligible to receive from any other source or sources, including, but not limited to, payments from state and municipal agencies, insurance benefits, and workers' compensation awards
source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

summary: If a sexual assault survivor believes a health insurance claim would cause undue harm by spreading treatment information, the office may waive counting health insurance as a collateral source.
quote: In a case involving circumstances under which a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault or child abuse, or a claimant in such a case, believes that the dissemination of treatment information associated with a health insurance claim would cause undue harm, the Office of Victim Services may waive the consideration of health insurance as a collateral source.
source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

summary: To decide on an award, the office looks at what matters in the case. This includes anything the victim did that helped cause the injury, how much the victim helped the office check the claim, and how much the victim helped police catch and prosecute the offender.
quote: shall consider all circumstances determined to be relevant, including, but not limited to, provocation, consent or any other behavior of the victim which directly or indirectly contributed to such victim's injury or death, the extent of the victim's cooperation in investigating the application and the extent of the victim's cooperation with law enforcement agencies in their efforts to apprehend and prosecute the offender
source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

summary: No award is made if the offender would be unjustly enriched, or if the victim broke a state penal law that caused or contributed to the injury.
quote: No compensation shall be awarded if: (1) The offender is unjustly enriched by the award, provided compensation awarded to a victim which would benefit the offender in a minimal or inconsequential manner shall not be considered unjust enrichment; (2) the victim violated a penal law of this state, which violation caused or contributed to such victim's injuries or death.
source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

summary: Connecticut's sexual assault offenses are named in the compensation statute as crimes the program can pay for, with alternative proof rules.
quote: In instances where a violation of section 53a-70b of the general statutes, revision of 1958, revised to January 1, 2019, or section 53-21 , 53a-70 , 53a-70a , 53a-70c , 53a-71 , 53a-72a , 53a-72b , 53a-73a
source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

params: {"rule":"Crimes in Connecticut are covered regardless of the applicant's residency; Connecticut residents hurt elsewhere may qualify only if that state or country has no program they are eligible for."}
summary: A crime that happens in Connecticut is covered no matter where the applicant lives.
quote: Compensation shall be awarded pursuant to sections 54-201 to 54-218 , inclusive, for personal injury or death resulting from a crime which occurs (1) within this state, regardless of the residency of the applicant
source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

source_title: Personal Injury Application, JD-VS-8PI (Rev. 7/21)

pinpoint: JD-VS-47, Lost Wages and Travel Expenses to Attend Proceedings, Requirements
source_title: Victim Compensation Program Benefits chart, JD-VS-47 (Rev. 7-24)

quote: judge (attach a copy of the signed civil protection order or restraining order)
source_title: Personal Injury Application, JD-VS-8PI (Rev. 7/21)

params: {"document":"other","note":"Documentation that relates the injury and each expense to the crime."}
summary: The program requires documentation that ties the injury and each expense to the crime.
quote: Documentation that relates the injury and expense to the crime is required.
source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Program brochure, JDP-VS-10 (Rev. 9/26)

summary: Sign the application by hand; unsigned applications are sent back for signature.
quote: Applications that are not signed will be returned for signature.
source_title: Personal Injury Application, JD-VS-8PI (Rev. 7/21)

params: {"program_name":"Address Confidentiality Program (ACP), Connecticut Safe at Home","agency":"Office of the Secretary of the State","covers_sexual_assault":true,"enroll":"Participants complete applications through a community-based domestic violence or sexual assault crisis program. These programs are located throughout the state. The application process involves meeting with an application assistant and receiving orientation information about the program. Application Assistants send the completed applications to the ACP office."}
summary: Connecticut's Address Confidentiality Program is run by the Secretary of the State. It gives a substitute mailing address to victims of sexual assault, family violence, stalking and some other crimes who want to keep their home address private because of safety concerns.
quote: There shall be an address confidentiality program established in the office of the Secretary of the State to provide a substitute mailing address for any person who wishes to keep such person's residential address confidential because of safety concerns and (1) has been a victim of (A) family violence, (B) injury or risk of injury to a child, (C) kidnapping, (D) sexual assault, (E) stalking
source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968a, Address Confidentiality Program (secs. 54-240 to 54-240o)

summary: Information the Office of Victim Services or a compensation commissioner receives that is already confidential under another Connecticut law stays confidential while they hold it. The statute does not make the whole claim file confidential.
quote: Any information received which is confidential in accordance with any provision of the general statutes shall remain confidential while in the custody of the Office of Victim Services or a victim compensation commissioner.
source_title: Conn. Gen. Stat. Chapter 968 (Victim Services), secs. 54-201 to 54-235

summary: The hospital may not bill a sexual assault survivor for the evidence kit (PERK), including the kit itself, its administration, and processing of the kit or any biological specimens. The statute does not say whether the survivor's insurance may be billed.
quote: The hospital shall not bill a sexual assault victim for costs associated with a PERK, including the costs of the PERK, its administration, and the processing of the PERK or any biological specimens.
source_title: D.C. Code § 4-561.03, Payment for PERKs

summary: A sexual assault survivor has the right to have a PERK (evidence kit) performed at no cost.
quote: a sexual assault victim shall have the right to have: (1) A PERK performed at no cost;
source_title: D.C. Code § 23-1908, Sexual assault victims' rights

params: {"amount_cents":2500000,"exception":"or more if you care for more than 2 children who live with you"}
summary: The program may not award more than $25,000 per victimization. If the victim is or was the parent, guardian, custodian, or main caregiver of more than 2 children who live or lived with them, the program may award up to $5,000 more for each child living with the claimant, starting with the third child.
quote: The Court shall not award compensation in an amount exceeding $25,000 per victimization; except, that: (1) If the victim is or was the parent, guardian, custodian, or primary caregiver to more than 2 children who reside or resided with the victim, the Court may award additional compensation to the claimant of up to $5,000 for each child who resides with the claimant, beginning with the third child
source_title: D.C. Code § 4-507, Awards of compensation

summary: Mental health counseling is capped at $3,000 for adults and $6,000 for minor children.
quote: Compensation for mental health expenses shall not exceed $ 3,000 for adults and $ 6,000 for minor children.
source_title: D.C. Superior Court Rules for the Crime Victims Compensation Program

summary: Lost earnings can be paid for up to 52 weeks after the crime, capped at the lesser of 80% of the victim's net pay or $10,000.
quote: Loss of earnings may be compensated for a total period of up to 52 weeks after the date of the crime, in an amount not to exceed the lesser of 80 % of the victim's net pay or $10,000.
source_title: D.C. Superior Court Rules for the Crime Victims Compensation Program

summary: Moving expenses of up to $1,500 may be paid when needed for health or safety, on referral from a prosecutor, police officer, judicial officer, medical or mental health provider, or victim advocate.
quote: Upon referral by a prosecutor, law enforcement officer, judicial officer, medical or mental health services provider, or victims advocate, compensation of up to $1,500 may be awarded for reasonable moving expenses where necessary for health or safety.
source_title: D.C. Superior Court Rules for the Crime Victims Compensation Program

summary: Temporary emergency housing is capped at $3,000, for a period of up to 120 days, on referral from a prosecutor, police officer, judicial officer, or victim advocate.
quote: Upon referral by a prosecutor, law enforcement officer, judicial officer, or victims advocate, the cost of temporary emergency food and housing for a period of up to 120 days may be awarded. The maximum award for temporary emergency housing shall be $3,000.
source_title: D.C. Superior Court Rules for the Crime Victims Compensation Program

summary: Transportation is capped at $500 for necessary out-of-state travel and $100 for local transportation, with a $600 total per claim. It covers trips to court, to take part in the investigation or prosecution, to get medical care, and to get other services needed because of the crime.
quote: Up to $500 for necessary out of state travel and up to $100 for all local transportation, not to exceed a total of $600 per claim, may be awarded for reasonable transportation expenses incurred by the victim or secondary victim
source_title: D.C. Superior Court Rules for the Crime Victims Compensation Program

summary: Up to $1,000 may be paid to replace doors, windows, locks, or other items needed to secure the victim's home. Guard dogs, other animals, and guns or other weapons are not covered.
quote: Compensation of up to $1,000 may be awarded for the reasonable cost of replacement of doors, windows, locks or other items necessary to secure the victim's home or other place of residence, except that the costs of guard dogs, other animals, guns or other weapons shall not be awarded.
source_title: D.C. Superior Court Rules for the Crime Victims Compensation Program

summary: Up to $100 may be paid to replace a living victim's clothing held by police as evidence.
quote: Reasonable compensation up to $100 may be awarded for the replacement value of clothing of a living victim which is held by law enforcement officials for evidentiary purposes.
source_title: D.C. Superior Court Rules for the Crime Victims Compensation Program

summary: Up to $1,000 may be paid for reasonable crime scene clean-up costs.
quote: Compensation of up to $1000 may be awarded to claimants for reasonable costs associated with cleaning up the crime scene.
source_title: D.C. Superior Court Rules for the Crime Victims Compensation Program

summary: Loss of services, meaning replacement services such as child care or housekeeping the victim can no longer provide because of the injury or death, is paid at no more than the D.C. minimum hourly wage, up to $200 per week and $2,500 per victimization.
quote: Compensation for loss of services shall be limited to the minimum hourly wage for the District of Columbia, and shall not exceed $ 200 per week and $ 2,500 per victimization.
source_title: D.C. Superior Court Rules for the Crime Victims Compensation Program

summary: Up to $2,000 may be paid for a rental car while the victim's car is held by police as evidence. The current statute describes this cost as alternate transportation, including a rental car or rideshare.
quote: Compensation of up to $2,000 may be awarded for the reasonable cost of a rental car for the period of time that a victim or secondary victim's automobile is being held by the police as evidence or to collect evidence.
source_title: D.C. Superior Court Rules for the Crime Victims Compensation Program

summary: Loss of services (replacement child care, housekeeping, and similar services the victim can no longer provide) is capped at $2,500 per victimization, on top of the $200 weekly limit.
quote: Compensation for loss of services shall be limited to the minimum hourly wage for the District of Columbia, and shall not exceed $ 200 per week and $ 2,500 per victimization.
source_title: D.C. Superior Court Rules for the Crime Victims Compensation Program

summary: Funeral and burial expenses are capped at $10,000. An older court rule gives a lower figure, but the statute controls.
quote: Reasonable funeral and burial expenses, including the reasonable cost of embalming, burial containers, cremation, and the chosen method of interment; provided, that a claimant's economic loss under this sub-subparagraph shall not exceed $10,000
source_title: D.C. Code § 4-501, Definitions

summary: Reasonable medical expenses are covered, whether the care was provided in D.C. or elsewhere.
quote: Reasonable medical expenses incurred, whether provided in the District or elsewhere;
source_title: D.C. Code § 4-501, Definitions

summary: Costs from a pregnancy resulting from a sexual assault are covered, including an abortion or prenatal care and delivery, but not the cost of raising the child.
quote: Compensation may be awarded for costs incurred for pregnancy resulting from a sexual assault. This includes the cost of an abortion, or prenatal care and delivery, but not the cost of raising a child conceived through sexual assault.
source_title: D.C. Superior Court Rules for the Crime Victims Compensation Program

summary: Out-patient mental health counseling needed because of the crime is covered when provided by a licensed psychiatrist, psychologist, social worker, marriage, family, or child counselor, or a counselor licensed by the Board of Professional Counseling.
quote: Out-patient mental health counseling expenses which became necessary as a direct result of the crime and which are provided by a: (i) Licensed psychiatrist or psychologist; (ii) Licensed social worker; (iii) Licensed marriage, family, or child counselor practicing within the scope of licensure; or (iv) Individual licensed by the Board of Professional Counseling
source_title: D.C. Code § 4-501, Definitions

summary: Lost income incurred as a direct or indirect result of the injury is covered.
quote: Loss of income or support incurred as a direct or indirect result of an injury or death;
source_title: D.C. Code § 4-501, Definitions

summary: Reasonable moving expenses are covered when needed for health or safety.
quote: Reasonable moving expenses where necessary for health or safety;
source_title: D.C. Code § 4-501, Definitions

summary: Dental care is part of covered medical expenses.
quote: Ambulance, hospital, surgical, medical, nursing, dental, optometric, ophthalmologic, chiropractic, podiatric, in-patient mental health, and pregnancy-related care;
source_title: D.C. Code § 4-501, Definitions

summary: Pain and suffering are not paid, and neither is the value of property damaged or taken during the crime.
quote: “Economic loss” does not mean: (i) Pain and suffering; (ii) The value of any property damaged or taken during the crime;
source_title: D.C. Code § 4-501, Definitions

summary: The program cannot pay attorney's fees for help filing an application. A fee may be awarded only for an appeal.
quote: The Crime Victims Compensation Program cannot pay attorney's fees for assisting a victim with the filing of a compensation application.
pinpoint: CVCP Application page, Information on Attorneys
source_title: D.C. Superior Court, CVCP Application page

params: {"years":1,"from":"crime","extension":"If you learned of the program later, you may have 1 year from then if the delay was reasonable."}
summary: A claim must be filed within one year after the crime. If you learned of the program later and the delay was reasonable, you have one year from when you learned of it.
quote: The claimant filed a claim under this subchapter within one year after: (A) The crime occurred; (B) Learning of the Program, with an adequate showing that the delay in learning of the Program was reasonable;
source_title: D.C. Code § 4-506, Eligibility for compensation

summary: The program may waive the time limits to apply and to report to police for good cause. Serious health or safety concerns can count.
quote: The time limit requirements of this section may be waived for good cause shown, including compelling health or safety concerns.
source_title: D.C. Code § 4-506, Eligibility for compensation

summary: A new 1-year window opens if a request to change the offender's sentence is filed or decided. The same is true for any other motion after conviction in a case where you were the victim.
quote: (C) The filing or resolution of a first application, or any subsequent application entertained by the court, for a sentence modification as described in § 24-403.03 ; (D) The filing or resolution of a motion to modify a term of imprisonment as described in § 24-403.04 ; or (E) The filing or resolution of any other post-conviction motion in which the claimant was a victim or secondary victim
source_title: D.C. Code § 4-506, Eligibility for compensation

summary: Generally the crime must be reported to law enforcement within 7 days, or within 7 days of when a report could reasonably be made.
quote: The crime was reported to a law enforcement office within 7 days after its occurrence or, if the crime could not be reasonably reported within that time period, within 7 days from the time a report can reasonably be made.
source_title: D.C. Code § 4-506, Eligibility for compensation

summary: A sexual assault survivor can meet the reporting requirement without a police report by getting a temporary or final civil protection order or a forensic medical exam, or by reporting to law enforcement any time before the statute of limitations runs out.
quote: In the case of a sexual assault victim: (A) Obtaining a: (i) Temporary civil protection order or civil protection order from the Court; or (ii) Forensic medical examination; or (B) Reporting the offense to a law enforcement office before expiration of the applicable statute of limitations for that offense
source_title: D.C. Code § 4-506, Eligibility for compensation

summary: If the program finds a victim's ability to report was affected by age, physical condition, psychological state, cultural or language barriers, or a health or safety concern, the victim can instead submit a court order, law enforcement records, or records from a medical professional.
quote: if the Program determines that the claimant's ability to report the crime may be impacted due to the claimant's age, physical condition, psychological state, cultural or linguistic barriers, or any other health or safety concern that jeopardizes the claimant's well-being
source_title: D.C. Code § 4-506, Eligibility for compensation

summary: The award equals the claimant's economic loss minus the amount available from collateral sources.
quote: The Court shall award compensation in an amount equal to the claimant’s economic loss, decreased by the amount available to the claimant from collateral sources.
source_title: D.C. Code § 4-507, Awards of compensation

summary: If the victim is a dependent on someone else's insurance policy, that policy does not count as a collateral source unless the victim chooses to use it.
quote: if a victim or secondary victim is a dependent on a primary insurance holder's insurance policy, the primary insurance holder's insurance policy shall not constitute a collateral source for the purposes of subsection (a) of this section, unless the victim or secondary victim chooses to avail themselves of the benefits or compensation from the primary insurance holder's insurance policy.
source_title: D.C. Code § 4-507, Awards of compensation

summary: An application may be denied in whole or in part because of the nature of the victim's involvement in the events leading to the crime.
quote: An application for assistance may be denied, in whole or in part, if the Court finds: (1) Denial is appropriate due to the nature of the victim’s or secondary victim’s involvement in the events leading to the relevant crime;
source_title: D.C. Code § 4-508, Disqualifications and reductions

summary: An application may be denied in whole or in part if the victim did not reasonably cooperate with law enforcement, unless the cooperation was affected by the factors in 4-506(c) (for example the sexual assault reporting alternatives, or age, condition, trauma, language, or safety concerns).
quote: (A) The victim failed to reasonably cooperate with law enforcement; and (B) The victim's cooperation was not impacted by the factors described in § 4-506(c)
source_title: D.C. Code § 4-508, Disqualifications and reductions

summary: An emergency award of up to $1,000 may be made before the final decision if an award is likely and the claimant would face undue financial or emotional hardship without immediate help. It is deducted from the final award.
quote: If it appears likely that a final award will be made and that the claimant will suffer undue financial or emotional hardship if immediate financial assistance is not granted, an emergency award not exceeding $1,000 may be made prior to the final determination.
source_title: D.C. Code § 4-510, Emergency awards

summary: First degree sexual abuse is a covered crime. The same statutory list also covers second, third, and fourth degree sexual abuse, misdemeanor sexual abuse, and child sexual abuse offenses.
quote: First degree sexual abuse, as described in section 201 of the Anti-Sexual Abuse Act of 1994
source_title: D.C. Code § 4-501, Definitions

params: {"rule":"Anyone injured in D.C.; D.C. residents injured abroad by terrorism or mass violence, or in a state without a VOCA-eligible compensation program"}
summary: Anyone injured by a crime in D.C. can apply. D.C. residents injured outside D.C. qualify only for terrorism or mass violence abroad, or when the state where it happened has no federally funded compensation program.
quote: “Victim” means a person who suffers personal injury or death in the District, a person who is a resident of the District and suffers personal injury or death as a result of a terrorist act or act of mass violence committed outside of the United States, or a person who is a resident of the District and who suffers personal injury or death outside the District in a state that does not have a crime victims compensation program
source_title: D.C. Code § 4-501, Definitions

summary: Email the completed application and supporting documents to CVCPapplications@dcsc.gov.
quote: Please submit completed application by email to CVCPapplications@dcsc.gov or by mail or in person to 515 5th Street, NW #109, Washington, D.C. 20001; or see remote sites.
source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

quote: Please submit completed application by email to CVCPapplications@dcsc.gov or by mail or in person to 515 5th Street, NW #109, Washington, D.C. 20001; or see remote sites.

summary: Include a copy of the DC police report or DC civil protection order, plus any bills or receipts you want reimbursed.
quote: submit it along with a copy of your DC police report or DC civil protection order (the program does not accept temporary restraining orders), any bills or receipts that you would like to have reimbursed by the program.
source_title: D.C. Superior Court, CVCP Application page

params: {"document":"exam_record","note":"Listed on the application as one accepted form of crime documentation (at least one must be selected)."}
summary: A forensic medical examination is one of the crime documentation options on the application.
quote: Forensic medical examination
pinpoint: CVCP Application (rev. 4/21/23), p.2, Documentation of Crime
source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

summary: Send any bills or receipts you want the program to reimburse.
quote: any bills or receipts that you would like to have reimbursed by the program.
source_title: D.C. Superior Court, CVCP Application page

summary: Submit copies of all medical, dental, or mental health bills received so far.
quote: Submit copies of all available bills received to date.
source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

summary: Attach all insurance payment statements and denials for treatment costs.
quote: Attach all insurance payment statements and rejections.
source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

summary: For lost wages, submit a disability statement from the doctor who can verify how long you could not work.
quote: (Please submit disability statement from the verifying doctor)
source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

params: {"document":"wage_verification","note":"Only if self-employed: federal income tax returns."}
summary: If you are self-employed and claiming lost wages, attach your federal income tax returns for the 12 months before the crime.
quote: If yes, you must attach a copy of your Federal Income Tax Returns for the last 12 months preceding crime.
source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

params: {"document":"other","note":"Copy of the lease and a referral form, only if requesting temporary housing or moving expenses."}
summary: For temporary housing or moving expenses, submit a copy of the lease and a referral form.
quote: If yes, submit a copy of lease. A referral form must also be submitted.
source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

params: {"document":"receipts","note":"Transportation receipts, only if your car was held as evidence."}
summary: If your car was held as evidence, submit copies of your alternate transportation receipts.
quote: Please submit copy of transportation receipts.
source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

params: {"document":"other","note":"Birth certificates for children, only when listing secondary victims or dependents."}
summary: When listing dependents or secondary victims, submit copies of the children's birth certificates.
quote: Submit copies of birth certificates for children.
source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

quote: Please click here to complete a Confidential Information form. Once completed, you can attach it at the end of the online interactive interview that you are completing, such as the Crime Victims Compensation Form.
pinpoint: D.C. Courts Forms Help Online, Crime Victims
source_title: D.C. Courts Forms Help Online, Crime Victims (guided online CVCP application)

quote: Please allow 5 business days for a CVCP team member to review your compensation application.
source_title: CVCP Application (revised 4/21/23)

params: {"program_name":"Address Confidentiality Program (ACP)","agency":"Office of Victim Services and Justice Grants (OVSJG)","covers_sexual_assault":true,"enroll":"Application assistants are available in several agencies across the District to answer questions, verify eligibility, and accept applications. To learn more about the ACP or submit an application, reach out to an application assistant on the list below."}
summary: D.C.'s Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Office of Victim Services and Justice Grants, gives eligible D.C. residents who fear for their safety and have experienced sexual assault, domestic violence, stalking, or human trafficking a legal substitute address that District agencies must accept, plus forwarding of first-class, certified, and registered mail. Applicants must also have moved recently, plan to move soon, or have kept their current address off public records, and apply through an application assistant.
quote: The District’s Address Confidentiality Program (ACP), administered by the Office of Victim Services and Justice Grants (OVSJG), provides a legal substitute address for eligible DC residents to maintain the confidentiality of her or his actual address.
pinpoint: OVSJG Address Confidentiality Program page, program description
source_title: Office of Victim Services and Justice Grants, Address Confidentiality Program page

summary: Information, records, and hearing transcripts in compensation claim files are confidential and not open to public inspection. The law lists exceptions.
quote: Information, records, and transcripts of hearings contained in the claims files under the provisions of this chapter are confidential and not open to public inspection
source_title: D.C. Code § 4-511, Confidentiality

summary: A survivor of a sexual offense pays nothing out of pocket for the forensic medical exam and does not have to file an application with the program for it.
quote: The victim of the sexual offense shall not pay any out-of-pocket costs associated with the forensic medical examination and shall not be required to file an application with the Agency.
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

summary: Hospitals and health care professionals must provide forensic medical exams free of charge to sexual offense victims.
quote: Hospitals and health-care professionals shall provide forensic medical examinations free of charge to the victims of sexual offenses.
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

params: {"payer":"Patient's insurance first (including Medicaid and Medicare), then the Victims' Compensation Fund for any uncovered cost"}
summary: The provider must first seek payment from the patient's insurance, including Medicaid and Medicare, if available. If there is no insurance, or it does not cover the full cost, the provider may seek payment from the Victims' Compensation Fund.
quote: Any hospital or health-care professional performing a forensic medical examination shall seek reimbursement for the examination from the patient's insurance carrier, including Medicaid and Medicare, if available. If insurance is unavailable, or does not cover the full costs of the forensic medical examination, the service provider may seek reimbursement from the Victims' Compensation Fund.
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

params: {"payer":"Victims' Compensation Fund, for crimes committed in Delaware","condition":"if the crime was in Delaware"}
summary: Delaware's victim compensation law applies to victims of crimes committed in Delaware, including people who do not live there. That law includes the free forensic exam rule.
quote: This chapter shall apply to: (1) All persons, including nonresidents of Delaware, who are victims of crimes committed on January 1, 1975, or thereafter within this State
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

params: {"amount_cents":2500000,"exception":"or up to $50,000 if you are left fully and permanently disabled"}
summary: Total compensation is capped at $25,000, or up to $50,000 for victims who are permanently and totally disabled.
quote: Compensation may not be awarded under the chapter to a claimant in a total amount in excess of $25,000; provided, however, that the Agency may award compensation to victims who are permanently and totally disabled in an amount not to exceed $50,000.
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

summary: Temporary housing is capped at $1,500.
quote: b. Temporary housing not to exceed $1,500.
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

summary: Moving expenses are capped at $1,000.
quote: c. Moving expenses not to exceed $1,000.
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

summary: Essential personal safety property is capped at $1,500.
quote: d. Essential personal safety property not to exceed $1,500.
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

summary: Crime scene cleanup is capped at $1,000.
quote: a. Crime scene cleanup not to exceed $1,000.
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

summary: If the claimant has a lawyer before the Appeals Board, the Board may award attorney fees of up to $1,000 or 15% of the award, whichever is less, paid on top of the compensation. The lawyer may not charge the claimant anything beyond that award.
quote: Such fees shall not exceed $1,000 or 15% of the amount awarded, whichever sum is less, and shall be in addition to the amount of compensation awarded to the claimant.
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

summary: Loss of support is capped at $3,000 for a victim who depended on the offender's income and lost it because of the crime (the offender must have had income at the time).
quote: i. Loss of support for victims of violence, not to exceed $3,000, when all of the following are established
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

summary: Medical expenses are a covered loss.
quote: n. Medical expenses.
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

summary: Psychiatric care and mental health counseling are covered losses.
quote: o. Psychiatric care and mental health counseling.
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

summary: Lost past or future earnings caused by a disability from the injury are covered, including vacation, sick, and compensatory time.
quote: r. Loss of past or future earnings, including reimbursement for vacation, sick, and compensatory time, because of a disability resulting from personal injury.
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

summary: The cost to change locks is covered, along with replacing items seized as evidence.
quote: k. The cost to change locks and replace items seized as evidence.
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

summary: Replacing items seized as evidence is covered; this is separate from the general bar on property loss.
quote: k. The cost to change locks and replace items seized as evidence.
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

params: {"expense":"childcare","scope":"the deposit plus up to 2 months of care by a state-approved or licensed day care provider"}
summary: Child care is covered, limited to the deposit plus 2 months of care by a state-approved or licensed provider.
quote: l. Child care not to exceed the deposit plus 2 months of care by a state-approved or licensed day care provider.
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

summary: Hospital expenses are a covered loss.
quote: q. Hospital expenses.
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

summary: The program page lists dental expenses and prescription medication among covered costs.
quote: Compensation is available for payment of medical and dental expenses, mental health counseling, prescription medication, lost wages, funeral/burial support, temporary housing and moving or relocation services, crime related expenses and other costs approved by the Agency.
pinpoint: VCAP page, FAQs: Who can get help?
source_title: Delaware DOJ, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program page and FAQs

summary: The program page lists prescription medication among covered costs.
quote: Compensation is available for payment of medical and dental expenses, mental health counseling, prescription medication, lost wages, funeral/burial support, temporary housing and moving or relocation services, crime related expenses and other costs approved by the Agency.
pinpoint: VCAP page, FAQs: Who can get help?
source_title: Delaware DOJ, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program page and FAQs

summary: Reasonable expenses for attending criminal proceedings as a prosecution witness are covered.
quote: m. Reimbursement for reasonable expenses incurred due to attendance at criminal proceedings as a witness for the prosecution.
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

params: {"expense":"legal","scope":"fees for a lawyer who represents you before the Appeals Board"}
summary: You do not need a lawyer before the Appeals Board, but if you have one, the Board may award an amount for the lawyer's services.
quote: A claimant need not be represented by an attorney before the Appeals Board, but if such person is represented the Appeals Board may award an amount for services rendered.
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

summary: Pecuniary loss does not include property damage, so damaged personal property (for example a phone) is generally not paid. The cost to replace items seized as evidence is the exception.
quote: “Pecuniary loss” means any expenses actually and necessarily incurred as a result of personal injury or death resulting from a crime, but does not include property damage.
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

params: {"item":"lost, damaged, or stolen property; pain and suffering"}
summary: The program will not pay for lost, damaged, or stolen property, or for pain and suffering.
quote: You cannot be paid for lost, damaged, or stolen property, or for pain and suffering.
pinpoint: VCAP page, FAQs: Are there any limits?
source_title: Delaware DOJ, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program page and FAQs

params: {"years":1,"from":"crime","extension":"unless the program gives you more time"}
summary: The claim must be filed within 1 year after the injury, unless the Agency grants an extension or finds the deadline unreasonable in the circumstances.
quote: Where the claim has not been filed within 1 year after the personal injury on which the claim in based, unless an extension is granted by the Agency or the Agency, in its discretion, determines that the circumstances render this requirement unreasonable.
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

summary: The program may not turn away a claim from sexual assault or abuse of a child because it was filed late.
quote: Notwithstanding any provision to the contrary, the Agency may not limit acceptance or consideration of any applications arising from sexual assault or abuse of a child which may have otherwise been barred from consideration by a statute of limitations.
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

summary: If the crime happened before your eighteenth birthday, the program may pay for mental health counseling. This holds even if you applied late, did not report to police in time, or did not cooperate with police. The crime must be properly documented, and you must apply before your twentieth birthday.
quote: Notwithstanding the provision of paragraph (10) of this section and § 9010(a)(3), (4), and (5) of this title to the contrary, the Agency may make an award for the payment of mental health counseling services under this chapter on a claim made by the victim of a crime that occurred before the victim’s eighteenth birthday so long as the occurrence of the crime is appropriately documented, and the claim is filed before the victim’s twentieth birthday.
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

summary: For sexual assault or abuse, that twentieth-birthday limit does not apply.
quote: However, the foregoing limitations in this paragraph (11) regarding the victim’s twentieth birthday do not apply in cases of crimes involving sexual assault or abuse.
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

summary: The crime must be reported to law enforcement within 72 hours, but this is waived if it was reported to protective services or Family Court, the victim has a protection from abuse order, the victim cooperated with law enforcement or an appropriate government agency in a sexual assault case, or the Agency finds the requirement unreasonable.
quote: Where the victim has failed to report the crime to a law-enforcement agency within 72 hours of its occurrence. This requirement is waived in any of the following circumstances: a. The crime has been reported to an appropriate governmental agency, such as child or adult protective services or the Family Court. b. The victim can provide a protection from abuse order. c. The victim has cooperated with law enforcement or an appropriate government agency in cases of crimes involving domestic violence, sexual assault or abuse. d. Where the Agency, in its discretion, determines that the circumstances of the crime or the victim render this requirement unreasonable.
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

summary: A claim is denied if the victim refused reasonable cooperation with law enforcement.
quote: Where the victim refused to give reasonable cooperation to state or local law-enforcement agencies in their efforts to apprehend or convict the perpetrator of the crime in question.
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

params: {"required":false,"scope":"child victims of sexual assault or abuse"}
summary: If you were a child when the sexual assault or abuse happened, the program cannot deny your claim just because you waited to report or to apply.
quote: In no event may the Agency deny any claim solely because the victim was a child victim of sexual assault or abuse, and the victim either delayed reporting the abuse or assault to authorities or the victim delayed an application for services to mitigate the effects of the impact of sexual assault or abuse.
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

params: {"amount_cents":2500,"waived_for":"dire hardship, as determined by the Agency"}
summary: Claims for less than $25 are not paid, except in cases of dire hardship.
quote: Except in cases of dire hardship, as determined by the Agency, there may not be payment of compensation where the claim is for less than $25.
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

summary: The award is the loss minus anything the claimant has received or will receive from other sources, including insurance.
quote: If a claim is approved, the award must be the amount of pecuniary loss minus the amount the claimant has received or will receive as indemnification from any other source, including any applicable insurance.
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

summary: If the victim bears a share of responsibility for the injury, the Agency reduces the award by that share.
quote: If the victim bears any share of responsibility that caused injury or death, the Agency shall reduce the amount of compensation in accordance with its assessment of the degree of such responsibility attributable to the victim.
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

summary: An emergency award is possible only on a showing of dire necessity, requested in writing with the claim form, and not until a police report or other official law enforcement documentation is obtained.
quote: The Agency will make an emergency award only upon a showing of dire necessity. The claimant, must, in writing, request an emergency award when submitting his claim form and show just cause as to why such an award should be considered. No such award will be made until the police report or other official documentation from the appropriate law enforcement agency is acquired.
source_title: 1 Del. Admin. Code 301, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program Rules and Regulations

summary: Covered crimes include offenses with the characteristics of rape, unlawful sexual intercourse, unlawful sexual penetration, or unlawful sexual contact.
quote: Any specific offense set forth in Chapter 5 of this title, if the offense was committed after July 1, 1973, and contains the characteristics of murder, rape, unlawful sexual intercourse, unlawful sexual penetration or unlawful sexual contact
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

summary: Personal injury includes mental, emotional, or psychological harm and pregnancy resulting from the crime, not only bodily harm.
quote: “Personal injury” means bodily harm, mental, emotional or psychological harm, or includes pregnancy resulting from the crime.
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

params: {"rule":"Crimes committed in Delaware, regardless of the victim's residency"}
summary: The program covers everyone, including nonresidents, who is a victim of a crime committed in Delaware.
quote: All persons, including nonresidents of Delaware, who are victims of crimes committed on January 1, 1975, or thereafter within this State
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

params: {"rule":"Delaware domiciliaries victimized out of state, only where that state lacks an eligible program with equal benefits"}
summary: A Delaware domiciliary hurt by a crime in another state may apply if the crime would be compensable in Delaware and that state has no eligible program with equal benefits.
quote: A person whose domicile is in Delaware and who is the victim or secondary victim of a crime that occurs in another state, possession, or territory of the United States may make an application for compensation if both of the following are true: a. The crimes would be compensable had they occurred in Delaware. b. The placement of the crime occurred in states, possessions, or territories of the United States not having eligible crime victim compensation programs that provide benefits equal to the benefits provided under this chapter.
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 90, Compensation for Innocent Victims of Crime (sections 9001 to 9025)

params: {"document":"other","note":"documentation of temporary housing, rent, security deposit, furniture, or moving costs, within 45 days of VCAP's request"}

quote: A victim who seeks compensation for temporary housing, rent, security deposit, furniture and/or moving expenses must submit documentation within 45 days of VCAP's request therefor, unless an extension is granted by the Agency.
source_title: 1 Del. Admin. Code 301, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program Rules and Regulations

quote: If the victim seeks compensation for an injury sustained while in the course and scope of employment, the victim must submit a claim for worker's compensation, and provide documentation thereof, before making application to VCAP for compensation.
source_title: 1 Del. Admin. Code 301, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program Rules and Regulations

params: {"document":"other","note":"a written request showing just cause, only if asking for an emergency award"}

quote: The claimant, must, in writing, request an emergency award when submitting his claim form and show just cause as to why such an award should be considered.
source_title: 1 Del. Admin. Code 301, Victims' Compensation Assistance Program Rules and Regulations

summary: A decision on a claim can take up to 60 days, and longer in rare cases.

summary: Delaware's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Department of Justice, gives certified participants a substitute address and forwards their mail. Victims of sexual assault can apply if they have filed for a protection from abuse order or are named as a victim in a criminal or delinquency case, and they state that they fear future violence from the perpetrator.
quote: All of the following persons are eligible to apply to become program participants: (1) A victim of domestic violence, sexual assault, human trafficking, kidnapping, or stalking who has filed for a protection from abuse order or who is or was named as a victim in any criminal or delinquency proceeding
source_title: 11 Del. C. ch. 96, subch. II, Address Confidentiality Act (sections 9611 to 9619)

quote: (14) Investigative files compiled or maintained by the Victims’ Compensation Assistance Program
source_title: 29 Del. C. ch. 100, Freedom of Information Act

summary: A medical provider who performs the initial forensic exam may not bill the victim (or a minor victim's parent or guardian), directly or indirectly, for that exam.
quote: (1) A medical provider who performs an initial forensic physical examination may not bill a victim or the victim’s parent or guardian if the victim is a minor directly or indirectly for that examination.
source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.28 (Payment for victims' initial forensic physical examinations)

summary: The state's payment is payment in full for the initial forensic exam, and the victim may not be required to pay any of its cost.
quote: Payment made to the medical provider by the department shall be considered by the provider as payment in full for the initial forensic physical examination associated with the collection of evidence. The victim may not be required to pay, directly or indirectly, the cost of an initial forensic physical examination performed in accordance with this section.
source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.28 (Payment for victims' initial forensic physical examinations)

params: {"payer":"Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Office of the Attorney General), Crime Victims' Services Office"}
summary: The Attorney General's Crime Victims' Services Office pays for the initial forensic exam after sexual battery or a lewd or lascivious offense, whether or not the victim has insurance, takes part in the criminal case, or cooperates with police.
quote: The Crime Victims’ Services Office of the department shall pay for medical expenses connected with an initial forensic physical examination of a victim of sexual battery as defined in chapter 794 or a lewd or lascivious offense as defined in chapter 800. Such payment shall be made regardless of whether the victim is covered by health or disability insurance and whether the victim participates in the criminal justice system or cooperates with law enforcement.
source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.28 (Payment for victims' initial forensic physical examinations)

summary: State payment for the initial forensic exam may not exceed $1,000 per violation and covers only the medical expenses connected with that exam.
quote: The payment shall be made only out of moneys allocated to the Crime Victims’ Services Office for the purposes of this section, and the payment may not exceed $1,000 with respect to any violation. The department shall develop and maintain separate protocols for the initial forensic physical examination of adults and children. Payment under this section is limited to medical expenses connected with the initial forensic physical examination
source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.28 (Payment for victims' initial forensic physical examinations)

summary: Total benefits on one claim cannot exceed $15,000 when the victim is living and not catastrophically injured.
quote: Total benefits paid on a single claim cannot exceed $15,000 when the victim is not deceased, or catastrophically injured
pinpoint: Schedule of Benefits (Fla. Admin. Code R. 2A-2.2003(2)(c))
source_title: Bureau of Victim Compensation Schedule of Benefits (effective January 6, 2022)

summary: Medical and dental treatment is capped at $10,000, paid at a rate of 50%.
quote: Medical/Dental Treatment $10,000 at a rate of 50%
pinpoint: Schedule of Benefits (Fla. Admin. Code R. 2A-2.2003(2))
source_title: Bureau of Victim Compensation Schedule of Benefits (effective January 6, 2022)

summary: Mental health care for an injured adult victim is capped at $5,000, paid at a rate of 50%.
quote: Mental Health Injured Adult Victim $5,000 at a rate of 50%
pinpoint: Schedule of Benefits (Fla. Admin. Code R. 2A-2.2003(2))
source_title: Bureau of Victim Compensation Schedule of Benefits (effective January 6, 2022)

summary: Mental health care for an injured minor (until age 18) is capped at $10,000, paid at a rate of 50%.
quote: Mental Health Injured Minor (until age 18) $10,000 at a rate of 50%
pinpoint: Schedule of Benefits (Fla. Admin. Code R. 2A-2.2003(2))
source_title: Bureau of Victim Compensation Schedule of Benefits (effective January 6, 2022)

summary: Wage loss is capped at $15,000, paid at a rate of 50% or the gross average weekly wage (GAWW).
quote: Wage Loss $15,000 at a rate of 50% or GAWW
pinpoint: Schedule of Benefits (Fla. Admin. Code R. 2A-2.2003(2))
source_title: Bureau of Victim Compensation Schedule of Benefits (effective January 6, 2022)

summary: Sexual battery relocation assistance is a one-time payment of up to $1,500 per claim, with a lifetime maximum of $3,000.
quote: The department may award a one-time payment of up to $1,500 on any one claim and a lifetime maximum of $3,000 to a victim of sexual battery, as defined in s. 794.011 , who needs relocation assistance.
source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.199 (Relocation assistance for victims of sexual battery)

params: {"expense":"property_replacement","amount_cents":50000,"per":"claim","item":"property loss for elderly persons or disabled adults"}
summary: Property loss awards are only for elderly persons or disabled adults whose loss seriously lowers their quality of life: up to $500 per claim and $1,000 lifetime.
quote: the department may award a maximum of $500 on any one claim and a lifetime maximum of $1,000 on all claims to elderly persons or disabled adults who suffer a property loss that causes a substantial diminution in their quality of life
source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.195 (Awards to elderly persons or disabled adults for property loss)

summary: Mental health care for an adult or minor victim of a forcible felony who was not physically injured is capped at $5,000, paid at a rate of 50%, for care within one year of the crime.
quote: Mental Health Minor Victim Mental Injury (until age 18) Mental Health Adult or Minor Victim of Forcible Felony (non injury) $10,000 at a rate of 50% n/a $5,000 at a rate of 50% one year
pinpoint: Schedule of Benefits (Fla. Admin. Code R. 2A-2.2003(2))
source_title: Bureau of Victim Compensation Schedule of Benefits (effective January 6, 2022)

summary: Medical and dental costs are paid only for care within one year of the crime.
quote: Medical/Dental Treatment $10,000 at a rate of 50% one year
pinpoint: Bureau of Victim Compensation Schedule of Benefits (Jan. 6, 2022), Medical/Dental Treatment
source_title: Bureau of Victim Compensation Schedule of Benefits (effective January 6, 2022)

summary: For an injured adult, mental health care is paid only within one year of the crime.
quote: Mental Health Injured Adult Victim $5,000 at a rate of 50% one year
pinpoint: Bureau of Victim Compensation Schedule of Benefits (Jan. 6, 2022), Mental Health Injured Adult Victim
source_title: Bureau of Victim Compensation Schedule of Benefits (effective January 6, 2022)

summary: Wage loss is paid only for loss within one year of the crime.
quote: Wage Loss $15,000 at a rate of 50% or GAWW Timeframe Within Which Loss Must Be Incurred From Date of Crime (up to) one year
pinpoint: Bureau of Victim Compensation Schedule of Benefits (Jan. 6, 2022), Wage Loss
source_title: Bureau of Victim Compensation Schedule of Benefits (effective January 6, 2022)
