summary: People who suffered a psychological injury as a direct result of a forcible felony may get mental health care if the law enforcement report names them as a victim of the crime. For adults who were not physically hurt, this is the only benefit.
quote: Persons who suffered a psychological or psychiatric injury as a direct result of a forcible felony may receive mental health care, when the law enforcement report identifies the individual as a victim of the crime. This is the only benefit available to adult victims who did not suffer a physical injury or death.
source_title: Fla. Admin. Code R. 2A-2.2002 (Compensation Eligibility Requirements), via Cornell LII

params: {"expense":"lost_wages","scope":"pay you lost because physical injuries from the crime kept you from working"}
summary: Wage loss is paid when the victim could not work because of physical injuries from the crime.
quote: Who missed time from work because they were unable to work as a result of the physical injuries sustained as a result of the crime;
source_title: Fla. Admin. Code R. 2A-2.2002 (Compensation Eligibility Requirements), via Cornell LII

summary: Travel to medical or dental treatment can be reimbursed with an itemized bill from the provider and a reasonable mileage estimate.
quote: Reimbursement for transportation costs to medical/dental treatment appointments requires the submission of an itemized bill by the treating provider and a reasonable estimate of the mileage between the victim/applicant's residence.
source_title: Fla. Admin. Code R. 2A-2.2002 (Compensation Eligibility Requirements), via Cornell LII

summary: Travel to mental health treatment can be reimbursed with an itemized bill from the provider and a reasonable mileage estimate.
quote: Reimbursement for transportation costs to mental health treatment appointments requires the submission of an itemized bill by the treating provider and a reasonable estimate of the mileage between the victim/applicant's residence.
source_title: Fla. Admin. Code R. 2A-2.2002 (Compensation Eligibility Requirements), via Cornell LII

summary: Medical, dental, and mental health costs the victim paid out of pocket are reimbursed at 100 percent, within the time limits and caps.
quote: Out-of-pocket reimbursement to the victim/applicant for qualified funeral/burial, mental health (includes grief counseling), medical/dental expenses, and crime scene cleanup shall be compensated at 100 percent, when services or treatment was rendered within the timeframes established and up to the maximum benefit amount on the Schedule of Benefits.
source_title: Fla. Admin. Code R. 2A-2.2002 (Compensation Eligibility Requirements), via Cornell LII

summary: For sexual battery relocation help, a certified rape crisis center in Florida must certify your need, state that you are cooperating with law enforcement (if that applies), and include your safety plan. The assault must have happened in your home, or somewhere that makes you reasonably fear for your safety at home.
quote: (c) The victim’s need for assistance must be certified by a certified rape crisis center in this state. (d) The center’s certification must assert that the victim is cooperating with law enforcement officials, if applicable, and must include documentation that the victim has developed a safety plan. (e) The act of sexual battery must be committed in the victim’s place of residence or in a location that would lead the victim to reasonably fear for his or her continued safety in the place of residence.
source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.199 (Relocation assistance for victims of sexual battery)

params: {"expense":"relocation","scope":"housing only: short-term shelter, rent, or a lease"}
summary: Relocation money pays only for housing: short-term shelter, rent, or a lease, which can include a security deposit, application fees, and the first month's payment.
quote: "Relocation assistance" compensation is defined as compensable housing expenses limited to short-term interim shelter, rental agreements, or long-term leases, and may include security deposits, application fees, and/or the first month's contractual payment.
source_title: Fla. Admin. Code R. 2A-2.2001 (Definitions), via Cornell LII

params: {"item":"real property, cash or negotiable instruments, intangible items, cosmetic damage"}
summary: Under the property loss program, real property, cash, intangible items, and cosmetic damage are not compensable.
quote: Examples of property that is not compensable includes real property, abandoned property, cash or other negotiable instruments, contraband or other illicit items, exchange agreements, items that amount to a monetary loss, are intangible, or are cosmetic damage causing a devaluation of the property.
source_title: Fla. Admin. Code R. 2A-2.2002 (Compensation Eligibility Requirements), via Cornell LII

params: {"years":3,"from":"crime","condition":"for a crime on or after October 1, 2019"}
summary: For crimes on or after October 1, 2019, the claim must be filed within 3 years after the crime.
quote: (b)1. A claim arising from a crime occurring on or after October 1, 2019, must be filed within 3 years after the later of: a. The occurrence of the crime upon which the claim is based; b. The death of the victim or intervenor; or c. The death of the victim or intervenor is determined to be the result of the crime.
source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.07 (Filing of claims for compensation)

params: {"years":5,"from":"crime","extension":"Waived entirely when the delay came from sexual assault forensic kit testing or DNA profile matching."}
summary: For newer crimes, if you filed late because testing a sexual assault kit or matching DNA was delayed, the deadline can be waived. For other good cause, the department may allow up to 5 years after the crime.
quote: 2. Upon a showing that a delay in filing a claim under this paragraph occurred because of a delay in the testing of, or a delay in the DNA profile matching from, a sexual assault forensic examination kit or biological material collected as evidence related to a sexual offense, a person who is eligible for compensation under subsection (1) may receive a waiver of any claim filing deadline. 3. For good cause based on a reason other than a delay described in subparagraph 2., the department may extend the time for filing a claim under subparagraph 1. for a period not to exceed 5 years after such occurrence.
source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.07 (Filing of claims for compensation)

summary: For a crime before October 1, 2019, the claim must be filed within 1 year after the crime. If you filed late because testing a sexual assault kit or matching DNA was delayed, the deadline can be waived.
quote: (a)1. A claim arising from a crime occurring before October 1, 2019, must be filed within 1 year after: a. The occurrence of the crime upon which the claim is based. b. The death of the victim or intervenor. c. The death of the victim or intervenor is determined to be the result of a crime, and the crime occurred after June 30, 1994. 2. Upon a showing that a delay in filing a claim under this paragraph occurred because of a delay in the testing of, or a delay in the DNA profile matching from, a sexual assault forensic examination kit or biological material collected as evidence related to a sexual offense, a person who is eligible for compensation under subsection (1) may receive a waiver of any claim filing deadline.
source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.07 (Filing of claims for compensation)

summary: For an older crime, the department may also allow up to 2 years after the crime for other good cause.
quote: 3. For good cause based on reason other than a delay described in subparagraph 2., the department may extend the time for filing a claim under subparagraph 1. for a period not exceeding 2 years after such occurrence.
source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.07 (Filing of claims for compensation)

params: {"years":3,"from":"age_18","extension":"Good cause can extend it, and a delay in sexual assault kit testing or DNA profile matching can waive it (same subsection; see researcher_notes)."}
summary: If you were under 18 at the time of a crime on or after October 1, 2019, you have 3 years after turning 18 to file.
quote: (c) For a claim arising from a crime occurring on or after October 1, 2019, when a victim or intervenor who was under the age of 18 at the time the crime occurred reaches the age of 18, the victim or intervenor has 3 years to file a claim.
source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.07 (Filing of claims for compensation)

summary: If you were under 18 at the time of a crime before October 1, 2019, you have 1 year after turning 18 to file.
quote: (b) For a claim arising from a crime that occurred before October 1, 2019, when a victim or intervenor who was under the age of 18 at the time the crime occurred reaches the age of 18, the victim or intervenor has 1 year to file a claim
source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.07 (Filing of claims for compensation)

summary: If you were a minor when it happened and filed late because testing a sexual assault kit or matching DNA was delayed, the deadline can be waived. For other good cause, the department may add up to 1 more year for an older crime, or up to 2 more years for a newer one.
quote: Upon a showing that a delay in filing a claim occurred because of delay in the testing of, or a delay in the DNA profile matching from, a sexual assault forensic examination kit or biological material collected as evidence related to a sexual offense, a person who is eligible for compensation under this subsection may receive a waiver of any claim filing deadline. For good cause based on any other reason, the department may extend the time period allowed for filing a claim under paragraph (b) for an additional period not to exceed 1 year or under paragraph (c) for an additional period not to exceed 2 years.
source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.07 (Filing of claims for compensation)

params: {"required":true,"within_days":5,"alternatives":[],"exception":"for a crime on or after October 1, 2019, or later with good cause"}
summary: For crimes on or after October 1, 2019, the crime must be reported to the proper authorities within five days unless the department finds good cause for the delay.
quote: 2. Five days after the occurrence of such crime, if the crime occurred on or after October 1, 2019, unless the department, for good cause shown, finds the delay to have been justified.
source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.13 (Awards)

summary: The report must go to state or federal law enforcement or prosecutors.
quote: "Proper authorities" means state and federal law enforcement officials and prosecuting attorneys.
source_title: Fla. Admin. Code R. 2A-2.2001 (Definitions), via Cornell LII

summary: The program may deny, reduce, or take back an award if it finds you have not cooperated with the state attorney, law enforcement, and the program.
quote: The department, upon finding that any claimant or award recipient has not duly cooperated with the state attorney, all law enforcement agencies, and the department, may deny, reduce, or withdraw any award, as the case may be.
source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.13 (Awards)

summary: The program pays last, after insurance and every other source.
quote: Payment made in accordance with this section shall be considered payment of last resort that follows all other sources.
source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.13 (Awards)

summary: The program must deny an award if it finds you would not face serious financial hardship without it. It looks at all of your financial resources.
quote: If the department finds that the claimant, if not granted assistance pursuant to this chapter to meet the loss of earnings or support or out-of-pocket loss, will not suffer serious financial hardship as a result of the loss of earnings or support and the out-of-pocket loss incurred as a result of the injury, the department shall deny the award. In determining serious financial hardship, the department shall consider all the financial resources of the claimant.
source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.13 (Awards)

summary: The award can be reduced or denied if the department finds the victim's conduct contributed to the injury.
quote: In determining the amount of an award, the department shall determine whether, because of his or her conduct, the victim of such crime or the intervenor contributed to the infliction of his or her physical injury or psychiatric or psychological injury or to his or her death, and the department shall reduce the amount of the award or reject the claim altogether, in accordance with such determination.
source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.13 (Awards)

summary: A contribution penalty is 25 percent of payments made directly to the victim; more than 25 percent means denial.
quote: Penalty assessments, if imposed, based on contribution will be applied only to payments made directly to the victim or applicant at the rate of 25 percent of the amount otherwise payable. A penalty assessment of more than 25 percent will result in the denial of benefits.
source_title: Fla. Admin. Code R. 2A-2.2002 (Compensation Eligibility Requirements), via Cornell LII

summary: If the program thinks an award is likely, and you get Social Security benefits or waiting would cause you undue hardship, it may give you an emergency award of up to $1,000. That amount comes out of your final award.
quote: if it appears to the department that such claim is one with respect to which an award probably will be made, and that either the claimant is a recipient of benefits under the federal Social Security Act or undue hardship will result to the claimant if immediate payment is not made, the department may make an emergency award to the claimant, pending a final decision in the case, on the following conditions: (1) The amount of such emergency award may not exceed $1,000; (2) The amount of such emergency award shall be deducted from any final award made to the claimant;
source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.12 (Emergency awards)

summary: Covered crimes include any felony or misdemeanor causing physical injury and any forcible felony causing psychological injury.
quote: (a) A felony or misdemeanor offense committed by an adult or a juvenile which results in physical injury or death, a forcible felony committed by an adult or juvenile which directly results in psychiatric or psychological injury
source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.03 (Definitions)

summary: Sexual battery is a forcible felony under Florida law.
quote: “Forcible felony” means treason; murder; manslaughter; sexual battery;
source_title: Fla. Stat. 776.08 (Forcible felony)

params: {"rule":"Crimes committed in Florida are covered; Florida residents harmed out of state are covered only where that jurisdiction lacks an eligible VOCA compensation program."}
summary: A Florida resident hurt by a crime in another state is covered only if that state has no eligible crime victim compensation program.
quote: (d) A criminal act committed outside this state against a resident of this state which would have been compensable if it had occurred in this state and which occurred in a jurisdiction that does not have an eligible crime victim compensation program as the term is defined in the federal Victims of Crime Act of 1984.
source_title: Fla. Stat. 960.03 (Definitions)

params: {"rule":"A resident keeps a primary dwelling in Florida; students and military personnel stationed in Florida count as residents."}
summary: For this program a resident is someone whose primary home is in Florida, and students and military personnel stationed in Florida are treated as residents.
quote: "Resident" means one who maintains his or her primary dwelling in Florida. Residency is governed by a person's intent, as evidenced by all surrounding facts and circumstances. Military personnel stationed in Florida and students shall be deemed residents for purposes of this program.
source_title: Fla. Admin. Code R. 2A-2.2001 (Definitions), via Cornell LII

summary: Hawaii's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Department of Law Enforcement, is free and lets survivors of domestic abuse, sexual offenses, or stalking use a substitute address instead of their home, work, and school addresses with state and county agencies. It also forwards mail and accepts legal service for participants. Survivors apply through an application assistant at a certified victim services organization, not directly with the Department.
quote: The Hawaii Address Confidentiality Program is a free resource that helps to protect survivors of domestic abuse, sexual offenses, and stalking. The program enables participants to use a substitute address in place of their residential, work, and school addresses with state and county government agencies.

summary: Medical costs of a pregnancy resulting from sexual abuse can be paid, counted under the medical benefit.

source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

summary: Glasses, hearing aids, dentures, prosthetics, wheelchairs, and medication taken, lost, or destroyed in the crime can be replaced.
quote: Compensation may be paid for the replacement of a medical device including but not limited to a sight or hearing device, dentures, a prosthetic device, a wheelchair, and medication that was taken, lost or destroyed during the crime.
source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

summary: Mental health care for the victim is covered up to $5,000.
quote: Reasonable charges incurred for mental health care not to exceed five thousand dollars
source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

summary: Mental health care for a secondary victim (spouse, child, parent, sibling, or household member) is covered up to $2,000 each.
quote: The allowable charges under this subsection shall not exceed two thousand dollars per secondary victim.
source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

summary: Wages lost because of the injury are covered up to $6,000.
quote: Loss of income from work the victim would have performed and for which the victim would have received remuneration if the victim had not been injured, not to exceed six thousand dollars.
source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

summary: Wages lost to cooperate with the investigation or attend court are covered up to $1,000 per person.
quote: Loss of income from work that the victim, the victim's parent or caretaker, or the survivor of a deceased victim would have performed and for which that person would have received remuneration, where the loss of income is a direct result of cooperation with the investigation and prosecution of the crime or attendance at criminal justice proceedings including the trial and sentencing in the case, or due to the planning of or attendance at a funeral, memorial, or burial service, not to exceed one thousand dollars per person.
source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

summary: Lost wages are figured from gross pay for scheduled hours missed, then reduced by 25 percent.
quote: Lost wages are computed as the gross rate of pay multiplied by the number of scheduled hours of work missed, decreased by 25 percent
source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

summary: Wages lost in the first two weeks after the crime need no disability statement; longer periods need one from a licensed medical or mental health provider.
quote: Compensation for lost wages or income incurred within the first two weeks following the crime shall be paid to an eligible crime victim without an authorized disability statement.
source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

summary: Wages lost for up to 30 days because of health or safety concerns about going to work after the crime, stalking, or harassment can be paid.
quote: Compensation for lost wages or income shall be paid to an eligible crime victim for up to 30 days following an event that compromises the health or safety of the victim including but not limited to the approved crime, stalking, or harassment.
source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

summary: Travel to medical care, counseling, or court is covered up to $1,000 per person.
quote: Reasonable expenses incurred by the victim, a secondary victim, the parent or guardian of a victim, or a survivor of a deceased victim for transportation to medical or counseling services, criminal justice proceedings, or a funeral, memorial, or burial service, not to exceed one thousand dollars per person.
source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

summary: Driving your own car is paid at the state employee mileage rate.
quote: Use of a privately owned vehicle shall be paid at the per-mile rate established by the department of administrative services for state employees using a private vehicle for state business.
source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

summary: Emergency relocation is covered up to $1,000 per person, once in a lifetime.
quote: Reasonable charges incurred by a victim, a secondary victim, a survivor of a deceased victim, or by a victim service program on behalf of a victim, for emergency relocation expenses, not to exceed one thousand dollars per person per lifetime.
source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

summary: To count as emergency relocation, the move must happen within 30 days of the crime, its discovery, or when it could reasonably be reported, or within 30 days before or after the offender's release from incarceration.
quote: "Emergency relocation" means a relocation that takes place within thirty days of the date of a crime or the discovery of a crime, or within thirty days after a crime could reasonably be reported. "Emergency relocation" also includes a relocation that takes place within the thirty days before or after an offender related to the crime is released from incarceration.
source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

summary: The statute allows up to 3 months of housing assistance, up to $2,000 per person per lifetime, but the program's facts page lists this benefit as currently unavailable.
quote: Reasonable expenses incurred by a victim, or by a victim service program on behalf of a victim, for up to three months of housing assistance, not to exceed two thousand dollars per person per lifetime.
source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

summary: New or replacement locks, windows, and other home security items are covered up to $500 per residence.
quote: Reasonable crime-related expenses incurred by a victim, the victim's parent or caretaker, or a survivor of a deceased victim to replace inadequate or damaged locks, windows, and other residential security items or install new locks, windows, and other residential security items, not to exceed five hundred dollars per residence.
source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

summary: Doors, locks, windows, security cameras, and security systems can be paid under the security benefit.
quote: Compensation may be paid for doors, locks, windows, security cameras, security systems or devices, or other reasonable expenses that provide for the safety of the victim or the security of the residence.
source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

summary: Clothing kept as evidence is replaced up to $200.

source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

summary: Child or dependent care while attending court, medical, or counseling appointments is covered up to $1,000 per person.

source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

summary: Funeral and burial costs are covered up to $7,500.

source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

summary: The crime must be reported to police or the sheriff within 72 hours, or within 72 hours of when a report could reasonably be made. The program may waive this for good cause.
quote: A person is not eligible for compensation unless the crime was reported to the local police department or county sheriff department within seventy-two hours of its occurrence. If the crime cannot reasonably be reported within that time period, the crime shall have been reported within seventy-two hours of the time a report can reasonably be made. The department may waive this requirement if good cause is shown.
source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

quote: For a victim of sexual abuse, the 72-hour reporting requirement may be waived for good cause if a sexual abuse evidentiary examination was completed within 72 hours of the crime or if the crime was disclosed to another provider including but not limited to a licensed medical provider, a licensed mental health professional, or a designated victim service provider.
source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

quote: When immediate or short-term medical services to a victim are provided pursuant to section 915.35 by a professional licensed or certified by the state to provide such services, the professional shall file the claim for compensation, unless the department of health and human services is required to file the claim under this section. The requirement to report the crime to the local police department or county sheriff department under subsection 3 does not apply to this subsection.
source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

summary: The victim must cooperate with reasonable requests from law enforcement in the investigation or prosecution of the crime.

source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

From or on behalf of a person who committed the crime or who is otherwise responsible for damages resulting from the crime. b. From an insurance payment or program, including but not limited to workers' compensation or unemployment compensation. c. From public funds. d. As an emergency award under section 915.91.
source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

summary: The program pays only after insurance, other government programs, and other sources.

source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Facts (Iowa Attorney General FAQ page)

summary: No award is made when the injury was caused by the victim's consent, provocation, or incitement, or by the victim's own criminal act. The criminal-act bar does not apply to a minor involved in commercial sexual activity.
quote: Compensation shall not be made when the bodily injury or death for which a benefit is sought was caused by any of the following: a. Consent, provocation, or incitement by the victim. b. The victim assisting, attempting, or committing a criminal act. This paragraph shall not apply to a victim under the age of eighteen involved in commercial sexual activity as defined in section 710A.1.
source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

summary: The program may reduce or deny an award only when the victim's conduct had a causal relationship to the injury.
quote: The program shall reduce or disqualify compensation when there is a causal relationship between the contributory conduct on the part of the victim and the victim's injury or death.
source_title: Iowa Admin. Code 61, chapter 9 (Crime Victim Assistance Division), IAC 2/5/25

summary: An emergency payment of up to $500 is possible when waiting would cause undue hardship. It is later subtracted from the final award.

summary: Injury includes emotional harm, not only physical harm, and includes pregnancy resulting from the crime.
quote: "Personal injury" or "injury" means bodily harm or mental suffering and shall include a victim's pregnancy or miscarriage resulting from a crime.

source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

summary: Records that Iowa's public records law already keeps confidential, and information taken from them, stay confidential when the program gets them.

source_title: Iowa Code 2026, chapter 915 (Victim Rights), including 915.41 and 915.80 to 915.94

summary: By statute, the cost of a sexual assault forensic or medical exam is paid from the state crime victims compensation account rather than by the law enforcement agency.
quote: the cost of forensic and/or medical examinations of alleged victims of sexual assault shall be paid for from the crime victims compensation account
source_title: Idaho Code 19-5303 (Cost of medical exams)

params: {"payer":"Industrial Commission, after any federal or federally financed third party for adults; after any liable third party, including private insurance, for minors"}
summary: The commission pays for evidence-gathering sexual assault exams after any federal or federally financed payer (such as Medicaid or Medicare); for victims under 18 it pays after any liable third party.
quote: Payment for the costs of forensic and medical examinations of alleged victims of sexual assault performed for the purposes of gathering evidence for possible prosecution, after collections from any federal or federally financed third party who has liability, shall be made by the commission; provided however that payment for the costs of forensic and medical examinations of alleged victims under eighteen (18) years of age shall be made by the commission after collections from any third party who has liability.
source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

params: {"payer":"Idaho Crime Victims Compensation Program, instead of an adult's private insurance"}
summary: The program says an adult's (18 or older) private insurance should not be billed for a sexual assault forensic and medical exam.
quote: an adult victim's (18 years of age and older) private insurance should not be billed for a sexual assault forensic and medical examination.
pinpoint: CVCP Sexual Assault Forensics Examinations page
source_title: Idaho CVCP: Sexual Assault Forensics Examinations

summary: The program says it will pay for an adult survivor's sexual assault forensic and medical exam, and to call the program right away if the facility sends a bill for the exam.
quote: Please note that if you are an adult victim of a Sexual Assault, we will pay for the costs of your Sexual Assault Forensic and Medical Examination. If you receive a bill from the medical facility for the Forensic Examination, please contact us immediately
pinpoint: CVCP FAQ, Will you bill my insurance?
source_title: Idaho CVCP: Frequently Asked Questions

params: {"payer":"Industrial Commission; a provider it has paid may not collect more from the victim for the same services, except as subsection (3) allows"}
summary: A medical provider that the program has paid may not try to collect more from the victim for the same services, except when the program cannot pay the full allowable amount.
quote: Except as provided in subsection (3) herein, a medical provider who has received payment from the commission for medical services provided to a victim or claimant under this chapter may not attempt to collect any further payment from the victim or the claimant for those same services.
source_title: Idaho Code 72-1026 (Payments to medical providers)

params: {"payer":"Idaho Crime Victims Compensation Program, once it has the victim's signed application"}
summary: If the program gets a bill for your exam but no signed application from you, it holds the bill for 30 days and contacts you. If no signed application comes within 60 days, the bill is destroyed.
quote: If the Program received a medical bill for a sexual assault forensic and medical examination but does not receive a signed application from the victim, CVCP will hold the medical bill(s) for 30 days. The program will contact the victim to request completion of the application. The medical bills will be destroyed if no signed application is received within 60 days.
pinpoint: CVCP Sexual Assault Forensics Examinations page, Medical bills received by CVCP, but no application received
source_title: Idaho CVCP: Sexual Assault Forensics Examinations

summary: Compensation to a victim, and to the victim's dependents if the victim dies, for crimes by the same offender within a 6 month period may not exceed $25,000 in total. The statute's wording is built around death cases; the program applies $25,000 as its maximum for all claims.
quote: Compensation payable to a victim and all of the victim's dependents in cases of the victim's death, because of injuries suffered due to an act or acts of criminally injurious conduct involving the same offender and occurring within a six (6) month period, may not exceed twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000) in the aggregate.
source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

summary: The program pays treatment expenses after all other payment sources are used, up to a maximum of $25,000.
quote: The Idaho Crime Victims Compensation Program reimburses providers and victims for treatment expenses incurred on behalf of the victim after all other payment sources have been exhausted, up to a maximum of $25,000.
pinpoint: CVCP Benefits You May Be Eligible For page
source_title: Idaho CVCP: Benefits You May Be Eligible For

summary: Mental health treatment for the victim is capped at $2,500 unless the commission finds extenuating circumstances, in which case it can go up to the overall maximum.
quote: payments for mental health treatment received as a result of the victim's injury may not exceed two thousand five hundred dollars ($2,500) unless the industrial commission finds extenuating circumstances.
source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

params: {"expense":"counseling","amount_cents":50000,"per":"claim","applies_to":"family members of the victim (spouse, parent, grandparent, child, grandchild, sibling)"}
summary: Family members of a sexual assault victim can get mental health treatment reimbursed, up to $500 per person or $1,500 per family, if the victim was also awarded benefits.
quote: Total payments made under paragraph (a) of this subsection may not exceed five hundred dollars ($500) for each person or one thousand five hundred dollars ($1,500) for a family.
source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

summary: A victim with total wage loss gets 66 2/3 percent of their wages, up to $175 per week.
quote: The weekly benefit amount is sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66 2/3%) of the wages received at the time of the criminally injurious conduct, subject to a maximum of one hundred seventy-five dollars ($175).
source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

params: {"expense":"lost_wages","amount_cents":15000,"per":"week","applies_to":"victims who were employable but not employed"}
summary: A victim who was employable but not employed at the time of the injury may get up to $150 per week, at the commission's discretion.
quote: who was employable but was not employed at the time of such injury, may in the discretion of the commission be awarded weekly compensation benefits in an amount determined by the commission not to exceed one hundred fifty dollars ($150) per week.
source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

params: {"expense":"lost_wages","amount_cents":2000000,"per":"claim","applies_to":"victims who were employable but not employed"}
summary: Weekly benefits for a victim who was employable but not employed may not exceed $20,000 in total.
quote: Compensation payable to a victim or a victim's dependents under this subsection may not exceed twenty thousand dollars ($20,000), and the limitations of subsection (5) of this section apply to compensation under this subsection.
source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

summary: Reasonable funeral, burial or cremation costs, plus transporting the victim's body, are paid up to $5,000 after other collateral sources have paid.
quote: Reasonable funeral and burial or cremation expenses of the victim, together with actual expenses of transportation of the victim's body, shall be paid in an amount not exceeding five thousand dollars ($5,000) if all other collateral sources have properly paid such expenses but have not covered all such expenses.
source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

summary: The commission may pay reasonable doctor, hospital, and medicine costs for crime injuries.
quote: The commission may order payment of reasonable expenses actually incurred by the claimant for reasonable services by a physician or surgeon, reasonable hospital services and medicines, mental health counseling and care, and such other treatment as may be approved by the commission for the injuries suffered due to criminally injurious conduct.
source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

summary: Mental health counseling and care for crime injuries can be paid.
quote: The commission may order payment of reasonable expenses actually incurred by the claimant for reasonable services by a physician or surgeon, reasonable hospital services and medicines, mental health counseling and care, and such other treatment as may be approved by the commission for the injuries suffered due to criminally injurious conduct.
source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

params: {"expense":"transportation","scope":"necessary travel to get benefits the program covers"}
summary: The claimant or a close family member can be reimbursed for necessary travel to get covered benefits, under the commission's rules.
quote: A claimant or a spouse, parent, child or sibling of a claimant or victim may be reimbursed for his or her expenses for necessary travel incurred in connection with obtaining benefits covered pursuant to this chapter and in accordance with rules of the commission.
source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

summary: Covered exam costs include examiner, facility, and lab fees, STI antibiotics, HIV prophylaxis, and other medications; follow-up visits may also be covered.
quote: Sexual assault forensic and medical examination costs covered by the program include but are not limited to examiner fees, facility fees, laboratory fees, antibiotics for Sexually Transmitted Infections, HIV prophylaxis, medical prescriptions, and other medications. Follow up visits as prescribed by the treating physician due to an assault may also be covered.
pinpoint: CVCP FAQ, What benefits are offered by CVCP?
source_title: Idaho CVCP: Frequently Asked Questions

params: {"expense":"other","item":"medically necessary items such as eyeglasses, contacts, prostheses, medical devices"}
summary: The program does not pay for property damage, but it can pay for medically necessary items such as eyeglasses, contacts, prostheses, and other medical devices.
quote: CVCP cannot pay Property Damages. However, the Program can pay for certain medically necessary items, such as eyeglasses, contacts, medical and dental prostheses, and other medical devices or aids.
pinpoint: CVCP Sexual Assault Forensics Examinations page, Billing
source_title: Idaho CVCP: Sexual Assault Forensics Examinations

summary: Covered medical costs include dental, vision, hearing, prescriptions, ambulance, physical therapy, imaging, chiropractic care, and medical devices and prostheses.
quote: Examples include medical, surgical, dental, vision, hearing, medication/prescription, ambulance transport, physical therapy, diagnostic imaging, chiropractic care, medical devices, medical aids, medical and dental prostheses.
pinpoint: CVCP FAQ, What benefits are offered by CVCP? (Medical)
source_title: Idaho CVCP: Frequently Asked Questions

summary: Medications and prescriptions for crime injuries are covered medical costs.

pinpoint: CVCP FAQ, What benefits are offered by CVCP? (Medical)
source_title: Idaho CVCP: Frequently Asked Questions

summary: Property damage is not paid, so replacing personal property such as a phone is not covered. Pain and suffering is not paid either.
quote: Compensation benefits are not payable for pain and suffering or property damage.
source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

summary: Pain and suffering is not compensated.
quote: Compensation benefits are not payable for pain and suffering or property damage.
source_title: Idaho Code 72-1019 (Compensation benefits)

summary: The program will not pay counseling cancellation or missed-appointment fees, or sessions that included the offender.

source_title: Idaho CVCP: Frequently Asked Questions

params: {"expense":"transportation","item":"first 15 miles of any round trip, and round trips of 15 miles or less"}
summary: Mileage is not paid for the first 15 miles of a round trip, or for round trips of 15 miles or less; one round trip per day.
quote: Reimbursement is limited to one (1) round trip per day. The claimant shall not be reimbursed for the first fifteen (15) miles of any round trip, nor for traveling any round trip of fifteen (15) miles or less.
source_title: IDAPA 17.10.01, Administrative Rules Under the Crime Victims Compensation Act

summary: The program's FAQ lists crime-scene cleanup among costs it does not cover and points victims to court-ordered restitution from the offender instead. The same FAQ sentence also lists wage loss, which the statute does cover.
quote: A victim may request the criminal court to order the offender to pay restitution for expenses that are not covered by the program, such as property damage, wage loss, expenses to attend criminal court, or costs for crime-scene cleanup.
source_title: Idaho CVCP: Frequently Asked Questions

params: {"years":1,"from":"crime","extension":"or later if the commission extends it for good cause"}
summary: The claim must be filed within 1 year after the crime; the commission can extend this for good cause.
quote: Compensation may not be awarded unless the claim is filed with the commission within one (1) year after the day the criminally injurious conduct occurred causing the injury or death upon which the claim is based. The time for filing a claim may be extended by the commission for good cause shown.
source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

params: {"required":true,"within_hours":72,"alternatives":[],"good_cause_exception":true,"exception":"or later if the commission finds good cause for the delay"}
summary: The crime must be reported to law enforcement within 72 hours, unless the commission finds good cause for the delay.
quote: Compensation may not be awarded unless the criminally injurious conduct resulting in injury or death was reported to a law enforcement officer within seventy-two (72) hours after its occurrence or the commission finds there was good cause for the failure to report within that time.
source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

summary: An adult who does not want to report to police can use a separate application. It is meant for people who mainly want only the cost of the sexual assault forensic and medical exam paid. It is not for minors.
quote: This application should be used by victims who did not or do not wish to disclose to law enforcement at this time and are primarily seeking reimbursement for only the cost of sexual assault forensic and medical examination This form is not applicable for minor victims.
pinpoint: Adult Sexual Assault Forensic Examination Reimbursement Application, page 1
source_title: Idaho CVCP Adult Sexual Assault Forensic Examination Reimbursement Application (April 2026)

summary: To get benefits, the claimant must fully cooperate with all law enforcement agencies and prosecutors in catching and prosecuting the offender.
quote: In order to be entitled to benefits under this chapter, a claimant must fully cooperate with all law enforcement agencies and prosecuting attorneys in the apprehension and prosecution of the offender causing the criminally injurious conduct.
source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

summary: Except for the sexual assault exam rules in 72-1019(2), compensation is reduced or denied to the extent it can be recovered from insurance or other collateral sources.
quote: Subject to the limitations on payments for the costs of forensic and medical examinations of alleged victims of sexual assault described in section 72-1019 (2), Idaho Code, compensation otherwise payable to a claimant shall be reduced or denied to the extent the compensation benefits payable are or can be recouped from collateral sources.
source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

summary: An award may be reduced or denied in proportion to how much the commission finds the victim contributed to the injury.
quote: Compensation may be denied or reduced if the victim contributed to the infliction of death or injury with respect to which the claim is made.
source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

summary: Compensation is cut by 50 percent if the claimant was committing a felony or certain impaired-driving or boating violations when injured.
quote: Compensation otherwise payable to a claimant shall be reduced by fifty percent (50%) if at the time the injury was incurred the claimant was engaged in a felony or was in violation of section 18-8004 or 67-7034 , Idaho Code
source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

summary: The commission may deny or reduce an award if the claimant or victim did not fully cooperate with law enforcement or prosecutors.
quote: The commission, upon finding that the claimant or victim has not fully cooperated with appropriate law enforcement agencies or prosecuting attorneys, may deny or reconsider and reduce an award of compensation.
source_title: Idaho Code 72-1016 (Limitations on awards)

summary: If the claimant would face financial hardship and a final award looks likely, the commission may pay a tentative award, deducted from the final award later.
quote: If the commission determines that the claimant will suffer financial hardship unless a tentative award is made and it appears likely that a final award will be made, an amount may be paid to the claimant, to be deducted from the final award
source_title: Idaho Code 72-1017 (Tentative award of compensation)

summary: Covered injury includes physical harm and, for a victim, pregnancy, sexually transmitted disease, mental or nervous shock, or extreme mental distress.

source_title: Idaho Code 72-1003 (Definitions)

summary: Idaho's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Secretary of State, gives survivors of sexual assault and other listed crimes a substitute mailing address and mail forwarding so their new address stays confidential; state and local agencies must accept the substitute address.
quote: If you move to a new location to escape domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, malicious harassment or human trafficking, the Address Confidentiality Program (ACP) helps keep your new address confidential using a mail-forwarding service and substitute address.
pinpoint: Address Confidentiality Program page, introduction; Idaho Code 19-5701 and 19-5703
source_title: Idaho Secretary of State, Address Confidentiality Program page

summary: The information and records the Industrial Commission keeps for crime victim compensation claims are confidential and exempt from public disclosure, with limited exceptions (the claimant, a court in camera review, public officials doing their duties, and treating or advising health care providers).
quote: The information and records the commission maintains in its possession in the administration of this chapter shall be kept confidential and are exempt from public disclosure under chapter 1, title 74 , Idaho Code
source_title: Idaho Code 72-1007 (Public inspection and disclosure of commission records)

summary: A hospital or other provider giving a sexual assault survivor a medical forensic exam, medical care and treatment, transportation, follow-up care, or medication may not bill the survivor for any part of those costs, including insurance deductibles, co-pays, co-insurance, or denied claims.
quote: shall not: (1) charge or submit a bill for any portion of the costs of the services, transportation, or medications to the sexual assault survivor, including any insurance deductible, co-pay, co-insurance, denial of claim by an insurer, spenddown, or any other out-of-pocket expense
source_title: Sexual Assault Survivors Emergency Treatment Act, 410 ILCS 70 (full act, ILGA)

params: {"payer":"Survivor's health insurance or coverage program is billed first; leftover deductibles, co-pays, co-insurance, and denials go to the Illinois Sexual Assault Emergency Treatment Program (Department of Healthcare and Family Services)"}
summary: If the survivor has health insurance or a coverage program, the provider bills that insurer or program, and the survivor's out-of-pocket share goes to the state Sexual Assault Emergency Treatment Program instead of the survivor.
quote: the ambulance provider, hospital, approved pediatric health care facility, health care professional, laboratory, or pharmacy shall bill the insurance company or program. With respect to such insured patients, applicable deductible, co-pay, co-insurance, denial of claim, or any other out-of-pocket insurance-related expense may be submitted to the Illinois Sexual Assault Emergency Treatment Program of the Department of Healthcare and Family Services
source_title: Sexual Assault Survivors Emergency Treatment Act, 410 ILCS 70 (full act, ILGA)

params: {"payer":"Illinois Sexual Assault Emergency Treatment Program (Department of Healthcare and Family Services) for uninsured survivors and survivors who opt out of private insurance"}
summary: When the survivor has no Medicaid or insurance, or has opted out of billing private insurance, the provider sends the bill to the state Sexual Assault Emergency Treatment Program.
quote: the ambulance provider, hospital, approved pediatric health care facility, health care professional, laboratory, or pharmacy shall submit the request for reimbursement to the Illinois Sexual Assault Emergency Treatment Program under the Department of Healthcare and Family Services
source_title: Sexual Assault Survivors Emergency Treatment Act, 410 ILCS 70 (full act, ILGA)

params: {"payer":"Illinois Sexual Assault Emergency Treatment Program when a survivor who is not the policyholder opts out of private insurance"}
summary: A survivor who is not the subscriber or primary policyholder on the insurance (for example, someone on a parent's or partner's plan) may opt out of billing that private insurance; the exam bill then goes to the state program.
quote: a sexual assault survivor who is not the subscriber or primary policyholder of the sexual assault survivor's insurance policy may opt out of billing the sexual assault survivor's private insurance provider
source_title: Sexual Assault Survivors Emergency Treatment Act, 410 ILCS 70 (full act, ILGA)

params: {"payer":"Survivor or survivor's insurance may be billed for inpatient services"}
summary: The billing ban does not cover inpatient care: if the survivor is admitted to the hospital, the survivor or their insurance may be billed for inpatient services.
quote: Nothing in this Section precludes a hospital, health care provider, ambulance provider, laboratory, or pharmacy from billing the sexual assault survivor or any applicable health insurance or coverage for inpatient services.
source_title: Sexual Assault Survivors Emergency Treatment Act, 410 ILCS 70 (full act, ILGA)

params: {"payer":"Illinois Sexual Assault Emergency Treatment Program (Department of Healthcare and Family Services), billed with the sexual assault services voucher"}
summary: Follow-up care, lab work, and prescriptions after the exam are billed to the state Sexual Assault Emergency Treatment Program when the survivor presents the sexual assault services voucher the hospital issues.
quote: If a sexual assault survivor presents a sexual assault services voucher for follow-up healthcare, the healthcare professional, pediatric health care facility, or laboratory that provides follow-up healthcare or the pharmacy that dispenses prescribed medications to a sexual assault survivor shall submit the request for reimbursement for follow-up healthcare, pediatric health care facility, laboratory, or pharmacy services to the Illinois Sexual Assault Emergency Treatment Program under the Department of Healthcare and Family Services
source_title: Sexual Assault Survivors Emergency Treatment Act, 410 ILCS 70 (full act, ILGA)

params: {"payer":"Illinois Sexual Assault Emergency Treatment Program via the sexual assault services voucher, for follow-up healthcare"}
summary: Follow-up healthcare covered this way means care related to the assault, including lab and pharmacy services, given within 180 days of the first visit.
quote: "Follow-up healthcare" means healthcare services related to a sexual assault, including laboratory services and pharmacy services, rendered within 180 days of the initial visit as a result of the sexual assault.
pinpoint: 410 ILCS 70/1a (text in effect before P.A. 104-837, eff. 1-1-27; definition unchanged in the amended text)
source_title: Sexual Assault Survivors Emergency Treatment Act, 410 ILCS 70 (full act, ILGA)

summary: For a crime committed on or after August 7, 2022, the final award may not exceed $45,000 per victim.
quote: or $45,000 per victim for a crime committed on or after August 7, 2022

quote: $27,000 for a crime committed on or after August 7, 1998 and prior to August 7, 2022

summary: Lost earnings are figured from the victim's average net monthly earnings for the 6 months before the injury, or $2,400 per month, whichever is less.
quote: loss of earnings and loss of future earnings shall be determined on the basis of the victim's average net monthly earnings for the 6 months immediately preceding the date of the injury or on $2,400 per month, whichever is less
source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

summary: Legal fees for proceedings needed solely because of the crime, such as getting an order of protection or no contact order, can be paid up to $3,500.
quote: legal fees resulting from proceedings that became necessary solely because of the crime, including, but not limited to, establishing a legal guardian for the minor victim or the minor child of a victim, or obtaining a restraining order, no contact order, or order of protection, awarded up to a maximum of $3,500
source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

summary: Funeral, burial, headstone, cremation, and related travel costs can be paid up to $10,000 for each victim.
quote: in the case of death, expenses for reasonable funeral, burial, headstone, cremation, and travel and transport for survivors of homicide victims to secure bodies of deceased victims and to transport bodies for burial all of which may be awarded up to a maximum of $10,000 for each victim
source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

summary: Towing and storage of the victim's vehicle in connection with the crime can be paid up to $1,000.
quote: expenses incurred for the towing and storage of a victim's vehicle in connection with a crime of violence, to a maximum of $1,000
source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

summary: Medical and hospital expenses from the injury are covered, including medical examinations, rehabilitation, and needed nursing care.
quote: in the case of injury, appropriate medical expenses and hospital expenses including expenses of medical examinations, rehabilitation, medically required nursing care expenses
source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

summary: Counseling is covered when given by a psychiatrist or a licensed clinical psychologist, licensed clinical social worker, licensed professional counselor, or licensed clinical professional counselor. No dollar cap on counseling appears in the Act.
quote: appropriate psychiatric care or psychiatric counseling expenses, appropriate expenses for care or counseling by a licensed clinical psychologist, licensed clinical social worker, licensed professional counselor, or licensed clinical professional counselor
source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

params: {"expense":"transportation","scope":"trips to and from medical and counseling treatment"}
summary: Travel to and from medical and counseling appointments is covered.
quote: transportation expenses to and from medical and counseling treatment facilities
source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

summary: Temporary lodging or relocation needed because of the crime is covered, including the first 2 months' rent and the security deposit at the new home. The Act sets no dollar cap for it.
quote: costs associated with temporary lodging or relocation necessary as a result of the crime, including, but not limited to, the first 2 months' rent and security deposit of the dwelling that the claimant relocated to and other reasonable relocation expenses incurred as a result of the violent crime
source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

params: {"expense":"security","scope":"locks, doors, or windows needed or damaged because of the crime"}
summary: Locks, doors, or windows that are needed or were damaged because of the crime are covered.
quote: locks, doors, or windows necessary or damaged as a result of the crime
source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

params: {"expense":"clothing_bedding","scope":"replacing clothing and bedding used as evidence"}
summary: Replacing clothing and bedding kept as evidence is covered.
quote: replacement costs for clothing and bedding used as evidence
source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

summary: Crime scene clean-up is covered.
quote: the costs of appropriate crime scene clean-up
source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

params: {"expense":"tuition","scope":"lost tuition, if the crime leaves the victim unable to keep attending school"}
summary: Lost tuition is covered when the victim was enrolled in school or college and cannot keep attending because of the crime.
quote: loss of tuition paid to attend grammar school or high school when the victim had been enrolled as a student prior to the injury, or college or graduate school when the victim had been enrolled as a day or night student prior to the injury when the victim becomes unable to continue attendance at school as a result of the crime of violence
source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

summary: Prosthetic appliances, eyeglasses, and hearing aids that are needed or were damaged because of the crime are covered.
quote: prosthetic appliances, eyeglasses, and hearing aids necessary or damaged as a result of the crime
source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

summary: The program's sexual assault FAQ lists medical, hospital, and dental expenses as payable.
quote: Medical, hospital, and dental expenses.

source_title: Illinois Attorney General: Crime Victims Compensation FAQ by Sexual Assault Victims (Rev. 01/25)

quote: "Pecuniary loss" does not include pain and suffering or property loss or damage.
source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

summary: Apply within 5 years of the crime, or within one year after someone is criminally charged for it.
quote: Within 5 years of the occurrence of the crime, or within one year after a criminal charge of a person for an offense, upon which the claim is based, the applicant presents an application
source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

params: {"years":3,"from":"age_18","extension":"also runs from removal of a legal disability; legal disability includes a PTSD diagnosis"}
summary: A victim who was under 18, or under a legal disability, when it happened can apply within 3 years after turning 18 or after the disability is removed. The Act counts a diagnosis of posttraumatic stress disorder as a legal disability.
quote: he or she may present the application required by this subsection within 3 years after he or she attains the age of 18 years or the disability is removed, as the case may be. Legal disability includes a diagnosis of posttraumatic stress disorder.
source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

summary: The Attorney General may accept a late application if it finds you had good cause for the delay.
quote: The Attorney General and the Court of Claims may accept an application presented after the period provided in subsection (a) if the Attorney General determines that the applicant had good cause for a delay.
source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

summary: For sexual assault and sexual abuse offenses, law enforcement must be notified within 7 days, or later if the applicant shows the notice was timely under the circumstances.
quote: For victims of offenses defined in Sections 10-9, 11-1.20, 11-1.30, 11-1.40, 11-1.50, 11-1.60, 12-13, and 12-14 of the Criminal Code of 1961 or the Criminal Code of 2012, the appropriate law enforcement officials were notified within 7 days of the perpetration of the crime allegedly causing death or injury to the victim or, if the notification was made more than 7 days after the perpetration of the crime, the applicant establishes that the notice was timely under the circumstances.
pinpoint: 740 ILCS 45/6.1(b) (text in effect before P.A. 104-563, eff. 1-1-27)
source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

summary: Instead of a police report, going to a medical facility for care or sexual assault evidence collection, getting an order of protection or no contact order, or getting an independent medical evaluation from a mental health provider counts as notice.
quote: If, in lieu of a law enforcement report, the applicant or victim has obtained an order of protection, a civil no contact order, or a stalking no contact order, has presented to a medical facility for medical care or sexual assault evidence collection, has presented to a mental health provider for an independent medical evaluation, or is engaged in a legal proceeding involving a claim that the applicant or victim is a victim of human trafficking or law enforcement use of force, such action shall constitute appropriate notification under this Section.
pinpoint: 740 ILCS 45/6.1(b-1) (text in effect before P.A. 104-563, eff. 1-1-27)
source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

params: {"required":true,"scope":"what a survivor must tell the medical facility for the visit to count as notice"}
summary: A survivor who uses a medical facility visit as notice has to give the facility enough information to meet the Act's notice rules.
quote: For purposes of notification under this Act, a victim who presents to a medical facility shall provide information sufficient to fulfill the requirements of this Section
pinpoint: 740 ILCS 45/6.1(b-2) (text in effect before P.A. 104-563, eff. 1-1-27)
source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

summary: A survivor who uses a medical facility visit as notice does not have to name the offender to the medical provider.
quote: except that the victim shall not be required to identify the offender to the medical provider
pinpoint: 740 ILCS 45/6.1(b-2) (text in effect before P.A. 104-563, eff. 1-1-27)
source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

summary: The same steps also count as cooperating with law enforcement. One is getting an order of protection or a no contact order. Another is going to a medical facility for care or evidence collection. Another is getting an independent exam from a mental health provider.
quote: If the applicant or victim has obtained an order of protection, a civil no contact order, or a stalking no contact order, has presented to a medical facility for medical care or sexual assault evidence collection, obtained an independent medical examination from a mental health provider as described in subsection (b-4), has taken any of the actions described in subsection (b-3), or is engaged in a legal proceeding involving a claim that the applicant or victim is a victim of human trafficking, such action shall constitute cooperation under this subsection (c).
pinpoint: 740 ILCS 45/6.1(c) (text in effect before P.A. 104-563, eff. 1-1-27)
source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

summary: When the victim was under 18, cooperation is met if the applicant or victim files a police report, a mandated reporter reports the crime, or someone with firsthand knowledge reports it.
quote: If the victim is under 18 years of age at the time of the commission of the offense, the following shall constitute cooperation under this subsection (c): (1) the applicant or the victim files a police report with a law enforcement agency; (2) a mandated reporter reports the crime to law enforcement; or (3) a person with firsthand knowledge of the crime reports the crime to law enforcement.
pinpoint: 740 ILCS 45/6.1(c) (same text before and after P.A. 104-563, eff. 1-1-27)
source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

summary: The program pays only after other sources, such as health insurance, public aid, Medicare, or workers' compensation, have been used.
quote: Compensation under this Act is a secondary source of compensation and the applicant must show that he or she has exhausted the benefits reasonably available under the Criminal Victims' Escrow Account Act or any governmental or medical or health insurance programs
source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

summary: Money raised through crowdfunding does not count as another source of payment and does not reduce the award.
quote: Crowdfunding resources available to applicants are not considered collateral sources of payment, regardless of any statements made about what expenses the crowdfunding resources will be used to pay.
source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

summary: An award can be reduced or denied to the extent the victim's injury was caused by the victim's provocation or incitement or by the victim committing a criminal act.
quote: an award shall be reduced or denied according to the extent to which the victim's injury or death was caused by provocation or incitement by the victim or the victim assisting, attempting, or committing a criminal act.
source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

summary: A victim's criminal history or felony status does not prevent compensation.
quote: A victim's criminal history or felony status shall not prevent compensation to that victim or the victim's family.
source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

summary: No award is paid while the applicant is held in a correctional institution, though they can apply at any time.
quote: No compensation may be granted to an applicant under this Act while the applicant is held in a correctional institution. An applicant who is held in a correctional institution may apply for assistance under this Act at any time
source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

summary: Compensation cannot be denied just because the victim is related to the offender or lived with the offender.
quote: In no event shall an applicant be denied compensation solely because of the applicant's or the victim's familial relationship with the offender or because of the sharing of a dwelling by the victim or applicant and the offender.
source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

summary: If compensation is probable and waiting would cause undue hardship, an emergency award can be made before the final decision, but only for funeral and burial costs paid to a funeral home and for relocation expenses. It is deducted from the final award.
quote: the Attorney General may recommend and the Court may make an emergency award of compensation to the applicant, pending a final decision in the case. Emergency awards may be issued to the applicant for the purpose of paying funeral and burial expenses directly to a funeral home and for relocation expenses incurred by an applicant.
pinpoint: 740 ILCS 45/10.2(a) (text in effect before P.A. 104-563, eff. 1-1-27)
source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Act, 740 ILCS 45 (full act, ILGA)

summary: All records and information given to the Crime Victims Compensation Board and division to process a claim are confidential, and the records gathered to evaluate a claim cannot be obtained through discovery in a civil or criminal case except in situations the law lists.
quote: All records and information given to the board and the crime victims compensation division created by K.S.A. 75-773, and amendments thereto, to process a claim on behalf of a crime victim shall be confidential.
source_title: K.S.A. 74-7308 (confidentiality of records given to the Crime Victims Compensation Board)

summary: When a sexual assault exam is given, no hospital, exam facility, clinician, pharmacist, health department, the survivor's insurer, or the state may charge the survivor for the exam, even if the exam is not completed.
quote: When an examination of a victim of a sexual offense is provided in accordance with this section, no charge shall be made to the victim by the hospital, the sexual assault examination facility, the physician, the pharmacist, the health department, the sexual assault nurse examiner, other qualified medical professional, the victim's insurance carrier, or the Commonwealth for: (a) Sexual assault examinations, whether or not the exam is completed;
source_title: KRS 216B.400 (sexual offense examinations)

summary: The no-charge rule also covers preventive medication, strangulation assessments, and other tests or services tied to the assault or exam on the same date as the exam, including triage and ambulance costs.
quote: (b) Prophylactic medical treatment; (c) Strangulation assessments; or (d) Other medical tests or services, including triage and ambulance expenses, related to the incident, exam, or treatment which occur on the same date as the original exam.
source_title: KRS 216B.400 (sexual offense examinations)

summary: A survivor cannot be refused an exam or billed for it because they choose not to file a police report, cooperate with law enforcement, or take part in the criminal case.
quote: No victim shall be denied an examination, or billed in violation of subsection (10) of this section, because the victim chooses not to file a police report, cooperate with law enforcement, or otherwise participate in the criminal justice system.
source_title: KRS 216B.400 (sexual offense examinations)

summary: The exam program's FAQ says providers should bill the patient's Medicaid or private insurance first, but may not charge a co-pay or deductible.
quote: If a patient has insurance, whether Medicaid or Private insurance, that insurance should be billed first before billing the SAEP, but no co-pay or deductible may be charged as a condition for payment.
pinpoint: SAEP FAQ, "Can we bill the patient's Insurance?"
source_title: Sexual Assault Examination Program FAQ (revised 11/2023)

params: {"payer":"Crime Victims Compensation Board (Sexual Assault Examination Program), paid to the provider"}
summary: The Crime Victims Compensation Board pays for sexual assault exams and the related no-charge services, at rates set by its regulation.
quote: The examinations provided in accordance with this section and other services provided to a victim pursuant to subsection (10) of this section shall be paid for by the Crime Victims Compensation Board at a rate to be determined by the administrative regulation promulgated by the board
source_title: KRS 216B.400 (sexual offense examinations)

summary: The total award for a claimant cannot exceed $50,000.
quote: Any award made under KRS 49.270 to 49.490 shall not exceed fifty thousand dollars ($50,000) in total compensation to be received by or paid on behalf of a claimant from the fund.
source_title: KRS 49.370 (award requirements, expenses, amounts)

summary: Lost earnings or lost support are paid at net earnings, up to $500 for each week.
quote: the award shall be equal to net earnings at the time of the criminally injurious conduct; however, no award under this subsection shall exceed five hundred dollars ($500) for each week of lost earnings or financial support.
source_title: KRS 49.370 (award requirements, expenses, amounts)

summary: When the crime happened at the victim's home, moving to a new primary residence for safety within 6 months of the crime is covered up to $2,000. The board may allow relocation costs incurred after 6 months at its discretion.
quote: For the victim and for any child who is the victim's dependent, when the crime was committed at the primary residence of the victim: a. Relocation if the victim is moving from one (1) primary residence to another due to concern for the safety of themselves or other persons at the residence as a result of a crime within six (6) months of the crime, not to exceed two thousand dollars ($2,000). The board may, in its discretion, allow relocation expenses incurred after six (6) months
source_title: KRS 49.370 (award requirements, expenses, amounts)

summary: Temporary housing within 30 days of the crime, when the victim cannot stay at home because of the crime, is covered up to $2,000 (this applies when the crime happened at the victim's home).
quote: Temporary housing costs incurred within thirty (30) days of the crime, when the victim is unable to stay in the primary residence due to the crime, not to exceed two thousand dollars ($2,000);
source_title: KRS 49.370 (award requirements, expenses, amounts)

summary: Replacing or repairing windows and locks at the victim's home or business damaged in the crime is covered up to $1,500.
quote: Replacement or repair of windows and locks at the primary residence or business of the victim which were damaged by the commission of the crime, not to exceed one thousand five hundred dollars ($1,500);
source_title: KRS 49.370 (award requirements, expenses, amounts)

summary: Crime scene cleanup within 30 days at the victim's home or business is covered up to $2,000.
quote: Crime scene cleanup within thirty (30) days of the crime when the crime was committed at the primary residence or business of the victim, not to exceed two thousand dollars ($2,000);
source_title: KRS 49.370 (award requirements, expenses, amounts)

summary: Funeral and burial costs cannot exceed $10,000.
quote: In no event shall an award for funeral expenses exceed ten thousand dollars ($10,000).
source_title: KRS 49.370 (award requirements, expenses, amounts)

summary: Mental health counseling needed because of the crime is paid for up to 2 years. It is paid only after proper documentation is sent to the board.
quote: Mental health counseling, necessary as a result of the injury upon which the claim is based. Mental health counseling: a. Shall be paid for a maximum of two (2) years, but only after proper documentation is submitted to the board
source_title: KRS 49.370 (award requirements, expenses, amounts)

summary: Awards cover out-of-pocket expenses, including lost earnings or support and debts reasonably incurred for medical or other services.
quote: Any award made pursuant to KRS 49.270 to 49.490 shall be in an amount not exceeding out-of-pocket expenses, including loss of earnings or support resulting from the injury on which the claim is based and indebtedness reasonably incurred for medical or other services
source_title: KRS 49.370 (award requirements, expenses, amounts)

summary: The program lists medical and dental expenses as compensable.

quote: An award may be made for a claim filed more than ten (10) years after the criminally injurious conduct, due to a delay in the testing of or DNA profile matching from a sexual assault forensic examination kit or biological material collected as evidence related to a sexual offense, in which case the victim may collect a lump sum in the amount of five thousand dollars ($5,000)
source_title: KRS 49.370 (award requirements, expenses, amounts)

source_title: KRS 49.370 (award requirements, expenses, amounts)

source_title: Crime Victims Compensation Board FAQ (updated August 2024)

summary: Awards are reduced by money received or to be received from the offender, required insurance, public funds, the claimant's own insurance, an emergency award, or donations toward crime expenses.
quote: Any award made pursuant to KRS 49.270 to 49.490 shall be reduced by the amount of any payments received or to be received by the claimant as a result of the injury from the following sources: (a) From or on behalf of the person who committed the crime; (b) Under insurance programs mandated by law; (c) From public funds; (d) Under any contract of insurance wherein the claimant is the insured or beneficiary; (e) As an emergency award pursuant to KRS 49.360; and (f) From donations made on behalf of the victim or claimant toward expenses incurred as a result of the crime.
source_title: KRS 49.390 (reduction of award)

summary: The board may deny, reconsider, or reduce an award if the victim or claimant was charged with an offense, was offered immunity, knowingly took part in the conduct, or engaged in mutual aggression, in relation to the crime in the claim.
quote: The board may deny, reconsider, or reduce an award if the board finds that, in relation to the criminally injurious conduct alleged in the claim, the victim or claimant: (a) Has been charged with a criminal offense; (b) Has been offered immunity from prosecution in exchange for testimony; (c) Knowingly participated in the conduct; or (d) Engaged in conduct which may constitute mutual aggression with another person.
source_title: KRS 49.390 (reduction of award)

summary: An emergency award of up to $1,000 can be paid before the final decision, and it is deducted from the final award.
quote: The amount of an emergency award shall not exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000); (b) The amount of an emergency award shall be deducted from any final award made to the claimant;
source_title: KRS 49.360 (emergency award)
