summary: Costs that come more than one year after the crime are not paid. If the victim was 18 or younger when hurt, the limit is two years, but a minor's new medical or counseling costs from the crime can still be paid after that.
quote: The economic loss is incurred after one year from the date of the criminally injurious conduct that caused the injury or death for which the victim seeks the award, except in the case where the victim for whom compensation is sought was 18 years old or younger at the time the injury occurred. In that case an award of compensation will be denied if the economic loss is incurred after two years from the date of the criminally injurious conduct that caused the injury or death for which the victim seeks the award, unless the minor victim has new medical or counseling expenses directly attributable to the crime.
source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15B-11 (Grounds for denial of claim or reduction of award)

summary: Replacement services loss (paying someone for ordinary household services the injured person would have done) is limited to $200 per week for up to 26 weeks from the date of the injury.
quote: Replacement service loss will be limited to a 26-week period commencing from the date of the injury, and compensation may not exceed two hundred dollars ($200.00) per week.
source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15B-2 (Definitions)

summary: An application must be filed within two years after the date of the crime.
quote: The claimant fails to file an application for an award within two years after the date of the criminally injurious conduct that caused the injury or death for which the claimant seeks the award.
source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15B-11 (Grounds for denial of claim or reduction of award)

summary: The program's page says the two-year limit can be longer if the crime was an unreported sexual assault of a child.
quote: In most cases, you are eligible for compensation if you apply no more than two years after the day the crime occurred. There are two exceptions that would extend this time period: the unreported sexual assault of a minor child.
pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program FAQ, Am I eligible?
source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

summary: The crime must be reported to law enforcement within six months unless there was good cause for the delay.
quote: The criminally injurious conduct was not reported to a law enforcement officer or agency within six months of its occurrence, and there was no good cause for the delay.
source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15B-11 (Grounds for denial of claim or reduction of award)

summary: An award is reduced by anything insurance or another collateral source pays or will pay for the same loss.
quote: An award that has been approved shall nevertheless be denied or reduced to the extent that the economic loss upon which the claim is based is or will be recouped from a collateral source.
source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15B-11 (Grounds for denial of claim or reduction of award)

summary: The program pays last, after private or public insurance; deductibles and co-pays may be reimbursed.
quote: Like other compensation programs, North Carolina is a payer of last resort, meaning victims should first submit expenses to private or public insurance companies. Deductibles and co-pays may be reimbursed.
pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page, FAQ: Do I need to file a claim with my insurance?
source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

summary: A claim may be denied or reduced for the victim's contributory misconduct, with an exception for trafficking victims who were coerced or deceived.
quote: The claimant or a victim through whom the claimant claims engaged in contributory misconduct, unless the claimant or victim through whom the claimant claims is a victim as defined by G.S. 14-43.10(a) and was coerced or deceived into participating in the contributory misconduct as a direct result of the person's status as a victim.
source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15B-11 (Grounds for denial of claim or reduction of award)

summary: A claim can be denied or an award cut if the claimant or victim did not fully cooperate with police or the prosecution, unless there was good cause. A claim already decided can also be looked at again for this.
quote: A claim may be denied, an award of compensation may be reduced, and a claim that has already been decided may be reconsidered upon finding that the claimant or victim, without good cause, has not fully cooperated with appropriate law enforcement agencies or in the prosecution of criminal cases with regard to the criminally injurious conduct that is the basis for the award.
source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15B-11 (Grounds for denial of claim or reduction of award)

summary: Rape victims are eligible to apply.
quote: Victims of rape, assault, domestic violence, drunk driving and pedestrian hit and run, as well as the families of homicide victims, are eligible to apply for financial help.
pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page, FAQ: What financial support is available?
source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

params: {"rule":"Crimes in North Carolina; NC residents victimized in a state with no victim compensation program"}
summary: The crime must have happened in North Carolina, except that a North Carolina resident hurt in a state with no compensation program may qualify.
quote: Compensation shall only be awarded for criminally injurious conduct that occurs or is attempted in this State except that criminally injurious conduct that occurs or is attempted against a resident of this State while in another state which does not have a victims compensation program of any type may be a basis of compensation.
source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15B-4 (Award of compensation)

params: {"rule":"Non-residents eligible for crimes in North Carolina"}
summary: Survivors do not need to be North Carolina residents if the crime happened in North Carolina.
quote: Victims do not need to be residents of North Carolina.
pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page, FAQ: Am I eligible?
source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

params: {"method":"mail","target":"Office of Victim Compensation Services 4232 Mail Service Center Raleigh, NC 27699-4232"}
summary: A paper application can be mailed to the Office of Victim Compensation Services, 4232 Mail Service Center, Raleigh, NC 27699-4232.
quote: If you prefer to apply by mail, you may download and print a paper form . Mail your application to: Office of Victim Compensation Services 4232 Mail Service Center Raleigh, NC 27699-4232
pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page, How to Apply
source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

summary: Survivors can start an application online through ncdps.gov/4victims, which leads to the program's online portal.
quote: To learn more about the program and start an application, visit ncdps.gov/4victims.
pinpoint: NC DPS Rape Victim Assistance Program FAQ, 'Is financial help available for medical expenses beyond the cost of the forensic exam?'
source_title: NC DPS Rape Victim Assistance Program page and FAQ

summary: The application must be completed, signed, and dated.
quote: Complete, sign, and date the application.
pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program FAQ, 'How can applicants avoid delays?'
source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

params: {"document":"police_report","note":"law enforcement report or warrant that lists the victim's name"}
summary: Include a copy of the law enforcement report or warrant that names the victim.
quote: Include a copy of the law enforcement report or warrant that lists the victim’s name.
pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program FAQ, 'How can applicants avoid delays?'
source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

summary: Medical and counseling expenses need itemized bills from the providers.
quote: Submit itemized bills from certified providers of medical or counseling services.
pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program FAQ, 'What paperwork do I need to submit with my application?' (Medical and counseling services)
source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

params: {"document":"receipts","note":"proof of any payments by the victim, third parties, or insurance"}
summary: Include proof of any payments already made toward the itemized bills, by the victim, third parties, or insurance.
quote: Provide proof of payment made towards any of the itemized bills by the victim, third parties, or insurance companies.
pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program FAQ, 'How can applicants avoid delays?'
source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

params: {"document":"wage_verification","note":"employed: physician's letter with dates out of work, employer letter confirming the absence, last paystub before the crime"}
summary: For lost wages, an employed survivor sends a physician's letter on letterhead, an employer letter confirming the absence, and the last paystub before the crime.
quote: If you have an employer, you should submit a signed physician’s letter on the provider’s letterhead that details the dates and reasons you were advised to be out of work, an official employer letter on company letterhead that confirms your approved absence and your last paystub before the incident.
pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program FAQ, 'What paperwork do I need to submit with my application?' (Lost wages)
source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

params: {"document":"wage_verification","note":"self-employed or independent contractor: physician's letter plus signed federal tax return from the year before the crime"}
summary: For lost wages, a self-employed survivor sends a physician's letter on letterhead and a signed federal tax return from the year before the crime.
quote: If you are self-employed or are an independent contractor, you’ll need a signed physician’s letter on the provider’s letterhead and a copy of your signed federal tax return from the year before the crime.
pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program FAQ, 'What paperwork do I need to submit with my application?' (Lost wages)
source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

params: {"document":"other","note":"dental claims: proposed treatment plan on the dentist's letterhead (optional)"}
summary: For dental care, a survivor may send a proposed treatment plan on the dentist's letterhead.
quote: You may submit a proposed treatment plan on your dentist’s letterhead.
pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program FAQ, 'What paperwork do I need to submit with my application?' (Dental services)
source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

params: {"document":"other","note":"funeral claims: death certificate, itemized funeral bill, law enforcement report"}
summary: Funeral claims need a copy of the death certificate, the itemized funeral bill, and the law enforcement report.
quote: Submit a copy of the death certificate, itemized funeral bill and the law enforcement report.
pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program FAQ, 'What paperwork do I need to submit with my application?' (Funeral expenses)
source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

summary: The program says the average processing time is three to six months from when it receives the application.
quote: From the time an application is received, the average processing time is between three to six months.
pinpoint: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program FAQ, 'What happens after I submit my application?'
source_title: NC DPS Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ

params: {"program_name":"Address Confidentiality Program","agency":"North Carolina Office of the Attorney General","covers_sexual_assault":true,"enroll":"File an application with the Attorney General with the assistance of an application assistant."}
summary: North Carolina's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Attorney General, gives relocated victims of domestic violence, sexual offense, or stalking a substitute address so assailants cannot find them through public records.
quote: A program in the Office of the Attorney General to protect the confidentiality of the address of a relocated victim of domestic violence, sexual offense, or stalking to prevent the victim's assailants or potential assailants from finding the victim through public records.
source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15C-2 (Address Confidentiality Program definitions)

params: {"program_name":"Address Confidentiality Program","agency":"North Carolina Office of the Attorney General","covers_sexual_assault":true,"enroll":"An individual who wants to participate in the Address Confidentiality Program shall file an application with the Attorney General with the assistance of an application assistant."}
summary: To enroll, the survivor files an application with the Attorney General with help from a designated application assistant (an advocate at a victim services agency or nonprofit).
quote: An individual who wants to participate in the Address Confidentiality Program shall file an application with the Attorney General with the assistance of an application assistant.
source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15C-4 (Filing and certification of applications; authorization card)

summary: Victims' and claimants' personal information and all information about how claims were decided (except the total amount awarded) are held confidential by the Commission and Director; medical and law enforcement records are also confidential.
quote: All personal information, as that term is defined in 18 U.S.C. § 2725(3), of victims and claimants and all information concerning the disposition of claims for compensation, except for the total amount awarded a victim or claimant, shall be held confidential by the Commission and Director.
source_title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 15B-8.1 (Privilege and records of the Commission)

params: {"insurance_billing":"prohibited","condition":"if done within 120 hours of the assault"}
summary: When an acute forensic medical exam is done for alleged criminal sexual conduct or domestic violence (within 120 hours unless good cause is shown for the delay), neither the exam nor any preliminary medical screening may be charged to the survivor, directly or through insurance or another third-party payer.
quote: performed within one hundred twenty hours after the alleged crime unless good cause is shown for the delay in performing the examination. When an acute forensic medical examination is performed, the costs incurred by a health care facility or health care professional for performing the acute forensic medical examination or any preliminary medical screening examination may not be charged, either directly or through a third-party payer, to the alleged victim.
source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 12.1-34 (incl. 12.1-34-07, forensic medical examination costs)

summary: When a child's forensic exam is done, neither the exam nor any medical screening before it may be charged to the child or to a parent, guardian, or custodian. This includes billing through insurance or another third-party payer.
quote: When a child forensic medical examination is performed, the costs incurred by a health care facility or health care professional for performing the child forensic medical examination or any preliminary medical screening examination may not be charged, either directly or through a third-party payer, to the alleged child victim or the child's parent, guardian, or custodian.
source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 12.1-34 (incl. 12.1-34-07, forensic medical examination costs)

params: {"payer":"North Dakota Attorney General, from the state general fund, reimburses the health care facility or professional"}
summary: The Attorney General reimburses the hospital or provider for the reasonable cost of the medical screening and acute forensic exam, within the limits of legislative appropriations.
quote: Upon submission of appropriate documentation, the attorney general, within the limits of legislative appropriations, shall reimburse from the general fund the health care facility or a health care professional for the reasonable costs incurred in performing the medical screening and acute forensic medical examination.
source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 12.1-34 (incl. 12.1-34-07, forensic medical examination costs)

summary: The total award for one victim and all claimants together may not exceed $25,000.
quote: Compensation payable to a victim and to all other claimants sustaining economic loss because of injury to or death of that victim may not exceed twenty-five thousand dollars in the aggregate.
source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

summary: For adult victims, mental health counseling is limited to 30 sessions and $3,600 total.
quote: For adult victims, no more than thirty sessions, and total compensation may not exceed three thousand six hundred dollars.
source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

summary: For minor victims, mental health counseling is limited to 40 sessions and $4,800 total.
quote: For minor victims, no more than forty sessions, and total compensation may not exceed four thousand eight hundred dollars.
source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

summary: If the provider shows a need, up to 10 more counseling sessions and up to $1,200 more may be allowed.
quote: If a provider substantiates the need for additional sessions, the division may allow up to ten additional sessions and up to one thousand two hundred dollars total compensation for the additional sessions.
source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

summary: Counseling is paid for no longer than 2 years from the first session.
quote: No longer than a two-year period beginning on the date of the first session
source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

summary: Work loss (and replacement services and dependent's losses) is paid at no more than $300 per week.
quote: Compensation for work loss, replacement services loss, dependent's economic loss, and dependent's replacement services loss may not exceed three hundred dollars per week.
source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

summary: Work loss is capped at $300 per week and $4,800 in total.
quote: Payment for work loss may not exceed more than three hundred dollars per week up to a maximum of four thousand eight hundred dollars.
source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

summary: Reimbursement for crime-related lodging, meals, and mileage is capped at $1,000.
quote: The maximum reimbursement for lodging, meals, and mileage is one thousand dollars.
source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

summary: Travel is paid only when the trip is at least 150 miles round trip from home.
quote: Travel distance must be at least one hundred fifty miles round trip from the claimant's residence in order for the claimant to be eligible for reimbursement of travel expenses.
source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

summary: New prescription medications are covered up to $1,000.
quote: The division may not pay more than one thousand dollars for new prescription medications.
source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

summary: Dental services are covered up to $5,000.
quote: The division may not pay more than five thousand dollars for dental services.
source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

summary: Funeral, cremation, and burial expenses are covered up to $5,000.
quote: The term includes a total charge not in excess of five thousand dollars for expenses in any way related to funeral, cremation, and burial.
source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

summary: Replacement services loss (paying someone for household services the victim can no longer do) is capped at $1,000.
quote: The division may not pay more than one thousand dollars for replacement services loss.
source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

summary: Reasonable charges for needed medical care, rehabilitation, and other remedial treatment caused by the injury are allowable expenses.
quote: "Allowable expense" means reasonable charges incurred for reasonably needed products, services, and accommodations required due to the injury, including those for medical care, rehabilitation, rehabilitative occupational training, and other remedial treatment and care.
source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

summary: Mental health assessment, diagnosis, and treatment, including individual or group counseling, is covered.
quote: Assessment, diagnosis, and treatment, including individual or group counseling sessions.
source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

summary: Work loss (income the victim would have earned if not injured) is a compensable economic loss.
quote: "Work loss" means loss of income from work the victim would have performed if the victim had not been injured
source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

summary: The program may reimburse meals, lodging, and travel directly related to the crime.
quote: The division may reimburse a claimant for meals, lodging, and travel expenses for travel directly related to the criminally injurious conduct.
source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

summary: Medical and dental expenses from the incident may be covered.
quote: Medical/Dental benefits for the Victim – If the victim has medical or dental expenses from the incident, they may be eligible for medical/dental benefits.
source_title: ND DOCR CVC Application Tips (PDF)

summary: The program's application guide lists dependent care benefits when the victim was the primary caregiver.
quote: Dependent Care – If the victim was the primary caregiver, the family may be eligible for dependent care benefits.
source_title: ND DOCR CVC Application Tips (PDF)

summary: Claims for property loss or damage are not covered.
quote: Claims for property loss or damage.
source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

summary: Noneconomic harm such as pain, suffering, and inconvenience is not a compensable loss by itself.
quote: Noneconomic detriment is not loss.
source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

summary: The program does not pay interest, finance charges, or collection fees on bills.
quote: The division may not pay compensation for interest, finance, or collection fees.
source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

summary: Attorney's fees for help filing a claim are not paid.
quote: Attorney's fees are not allowable for assisting a claimant in filing a claim.
source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

params: {"item":"travel for the victim to meet with law enforcement or to go to court"}
summary: The program does not pay travel costs for the victim to meet with law enforcement, or for the victim or a homicide victim's immediate family to go to court.
quote: The division may not pay reimbursement for travel expenses for the victim or immediate family of a homicide victim to attend court proceedings or for the victim to meet with law enforcement.
source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

params: {"years":1,"from":"report","extension":"or later if the division finds the interests of justice require it"}
summary: File within one year from the date the crime was reported to law enforcement; the program may extend this when the interests of justice require.
quote: A claim for compensation must be filed within one year from the date the criminally injurious conduct was reported to a law enforcement officer. The division may extend the time for filing if it determines that the interests of justice so require.
source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

params: {"required":true,"within_hours":96,"exception":"or later if the program finds good cause for the delay"}
summary: The crime must be reported to law enforcement within 96 hours, unless the program finds good cause for the delay.
quote: Compensation may not be awarded unless the criminally injurious conduct resulting in injury or death was reported to a law enforcement officer within ninety-six hours after its occurrence or the division finds there was good cause for the failure to report within that time.
source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

params: {"required":true,"scope":"what counts as good cause for a late report"}
summary: Good cause for a late report includes evidence, such as medical records or verifiable third-party reports, that reporting on time would have put the applicant's health or safety at risk.
quote: Evidence, including medical records or verifiable reports from third parties, which substantiate the applicant's health or safety would have been jeopardized if the criminally injurious conduct had been reported in a timely manner.
source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

params: {"required":true,"scope":"what counts as good cause for a late report"}
summary: Good cause for a late report also includes law enforcement confirming that the victim feared retaliation.
quote: Law enforcement substantiates there was a fear of retaliation.
source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

params: {"required":true,"exception":"or, for abuse of a child, within 3 years after the child becomes an adult"}
summary: For child abuse or sexual molestation of a child, the report to law enforcement must be made within three years after the child reaches the age of majority.
quote: In the case of child abuse or sexual molestation of a child, the criminally injurious conduct must be reported to a law enforcement officer within three years after the child reaches the age of majority.
source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

summary: Awards are reduced or denied to the extent the loss is recouped from other sources, including insurance and other collateral sources.
quote: To the extent the economic loss upon which the claim is based is recouped from other persons, including collateral sources;
source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

summary: The fund pays only for losses not paid by other sources such as health insurance, Medicaid, employer-paid leave, and online fundraising.
quote: The crime victims compensation fund is a secondary source for payment for economic losses not paid by other collateral sources, including disability benefits; employer-paid leave, including sick leave or annual leave; health insurance, including medical, vision, and dental benefits; life insurance; Medicare; medical assistance or Medicaid; motor vehicle insurance; personal and charity fundraising, including online fundraising;
source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

summary: An award may be reduced or denied to the extent the program deems reasonable because of the victim's contributory misconduct.
quote: To the extent the division deems reasonable because of the contributory misconduct of the claimant or of a victim on whose behalf compensation is claimed;
source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

summary: An award may be reduced or denied if the program finds the victim's intoxication was a factor causing the crime.
quote: To the extent the division deems reasonable when it is determined that a victim was under the influence of an alcoholic beverage or a controlled substance at the time the criminally injurious conduct occurred and the victim's intoxication was a factor causing the criminally injurious conduct.
source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

summary: The program may deny, reconsider, or reduce an award if the claimant has not fully cooperated with law enforcement.
quote: The division, upon finding that the claimant has not fully cooperated with appropriate law enforcement agencies, may deny, reconsider, or reduce an award of compensation.
source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

summary: The admin rule requires denial when the claimant's conduct contributed substantially to the incident; the listed conduct includes intoxication that was a factor in the crime. Human trafficking victims are excluded from this rule.
quote: The division shall deny compensation if the claimant's conduct contributed substantially to the incident.
source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

summary: A tentative award may be paid if the claimant would otherwise suffer financial hardship and a final award appears likely; it is deducted from the final award.
quote: If the division determines that the claimant will suffer financial hardship unless a tentative award is made, and it appears likely that a final award will be made, an amount may be paid to the claimant which must be deducted from the final award
source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

summary: Victims who suffered physical or emotional injuries from a violent crime can qualify. The sources do not list crimes by name; bodily injury is defined to include pregnancy and nervous shock.
quote: The victim suffered physical or emotional injuries as a result of a violent crime, drunk driving, or hit and run.
pinpoint: DOCR CVC page, What is Eligibility Criteria?
source_title: ND DOCR Crime Victims Compensation program page

summary: Bodily injury means harm that requires medical treatment and results in economic loss; it includes pregnancy and nervous shock.
quote: "Bodily injury" means any harm that requires medical treatment and results in economic loss and includes pregnancy and nervous shock.
source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

params: {"rule":"Covers crimes in North Dakota. A North Dakota resident hurt outside the state has the same rights if the place where the crime happened has no compensation law covering the injury."}
summary: Crimes in North Dakota are covered. A North Dakota resident hurt by a crime somewhere else has the same rights as for a North Dakota crime if they show that place has no crime victims compensation law covering the injury.
quote: If a resident of this state is a victim of criminally injurious conduct, but the criminally injurious conduct occurred outside the geographical boundaries of this state, the resident has the same rights under this chapter as if the criminally injurious conduct occurred within this state upon a showing that the state, territory, country, or political subdivision of the country in which the criminally injurious conduct occurred does not have a crime victims compensation law which covers the bodily injury or death of the victim.
source_title: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-23.4 (Crime Victims Compensation)

params: {"method":"online","target":"https://portalapps.nd.gov/docr/cvc-application/","note":"The program page links to the online application; the portal itself could not be saved as a snapshot. No official source states a mail, email, or fax filing method for the application."}
summary: Apply online through the ND DOCR Crime Victim's Compensation Application portal linked from the program page.
quote: Clicking the link below will take you to the online application for Crime Victim
pinpoint: Program page, Crime Victims Compensation Application and Forms
source_title: ND DOCR Crime Victims Compensation program page

params: {"weeks":4,"note":"The program page says to allow 2 to 4 weeks for an application or a reimbursement request."}
summary: Allow 2 to 4 weeks for the program to process an application or a reimbursement request.
quote: Please allow 2-4 weeks for processing CVC application or claim reimbursement requests.
source_title: ND DOCR Crime Victims Compensation program page

params: {"document":"other","note":"Completed application signed by the claimant or the claimant's parent, guardian, or legal representative, on the division's form."}
summary: Submit a completed application on the program's form, signed by the claimant or a parent, guardian, or legal representative; an employer, provider, or insurer cannot apply for you.
quote: A claimant for benefits shall submit a completed application for compensation signed by the claimant or the claimant's parent, guardian, or legal representative on an application form prescribed by the division.
source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

params: {"document":"other","note":"Written explanation of the late report, only if the crime was not reported to law enforcement within the reporting window."}
summary: If the crime was not reported to law enforcement in time, explain the reason for the late report in the application.
quote: There may be a justifiable reason for the late report. Please explain.
pinpoint: CVC Application Tips, Section 3 (Incident Information, continued)
source_title: ND DOCR CVC Application Tips (PDF)

params: {"document":"itemized_bill","note":"Billing statement with the medical provider's name, business address, telephone number, and treatment plan."}
summary: For medical costs, include a billing statement showing the provider's name, business address, phone number, and treatment plan.
quote: A request for compensation for medical services must include a billing statement containing the medical provider's name, business address, telephone number, treatment plan, and other information necessary for the division to determine the claim is for services directly related to the criminally injurious conduct.
source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

params: {"document":"itemized_bill","note":"Billing statement with the dental provider's name, business address, telephone number, and treatment plan."}
summary: For dental costs, include a billing statement showing the dentist's name, business address, phone number, and treatment plan.
quote: A request for compensation for dental services must include a billing statement containing the dental provider's name, business address, telephone number, treatment plan, and other information necessary for the division to determine the claim is for services directly related to the criminally injurious conduct.
source_title: N.D. Admin. Code ch. 94-03-03 (application for compensation)

params: {"document":"itemized_bill","note":"Billing statement of itemized transactions from the mental health provider."}
summary: For counseling, the provider's billing statement must list itemized transactions with the provider's name, business address, and phone number.

summary: Nebraska's Address Confidentiality Program is for victims of abuse, sexual assault or stalking who fear for their safety, among other conditions.

source_title: Nebraska Secretary of State: Address Confidentiality Program page

source_title: Neb. Rev. Stat. 81-1842 (sexual assault victim; records; confidential)

summary: A physician or hospital that examines a survivor of an alleged sexual offense to gather evidence must provide the exam without charge to the survivor.
quote: If a physician or a hospital provides any physical examination of a victim of an alleged sexual offense to gather information and evidence of the alleged crime, these services shall be provided without charge to the individual.
source_title: RSA 21-M:8-c, Victim of Alleged Sexual Offense

summary: The bill for a sexual assault medical exam may not be sent or given to the survivor or the survivor's family.
quote: The bill for the medical examination of a sexual assault victim shall not be sent or given to the victim or the family of the victim.
source_title: RSA 21-M:8-c, Victim of Alleged Sexual Offense

summary: If a survivor with insurance chooses to bill it, the provider bills the insurer, and neither the survivor nor the department may be billed for anything above the coverage limit. A separate rule says that for survivors on Medicaid or Medicare whose kit is not anonymous, the provider bills Medicaid or Medicare.
quote: If the victim of a felonious sexual assault has insurance, and chooses to bill their healthcare insurance, the health provider shall seek payment from the patient's healthcare insurer. Neither the patient nor the department shall be billed for anything above the coverage limit
source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

summary: If a survivor chooses to remain anonymous, the provider bills the Department of Justice or writes off the charges, even when the survivor has insurance.
quote: If the victim of a felonious sexual assault chooses to remain anonymous, even if they have healthcare insurance, the health provider shall seek payment directly from the department or shall write off such charges
source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

summary: The Department of Justice reimburses the physician or hospital for the exam to the extent the cost is not covered by health insurance or a similar third party.
quote: Upon submission of appropriate documentation, the physician or hospital shall be reimbursed for the cost of such examination by the department of justice to the extent such costs are not the responsibility of a third party under a health insurance policy or similar third party obligation.
source_title: RSA 21-M:8-c, Victim of Alleged Sexual Offense

summary: If a survivor uses insurance for the exam, the Department of Justice pays or reimburses any deductible or co-payment.

source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

summary: A person examined by a physician or hospital after a felonious sexual assault, for treatment or to gather evidence, may not be charged for services related to the assault or other crime-related injuries. Payments are at the fee for service Medicaid rate.
quote: a person who claims to be a victim of a felonious sexual assault who is examined by a physician or hospital for the purpose of treatment, gathering information or evidence shall not be charged for such services or examination that relate to the sexual assault and any other crime-related injuries
source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

params: {"payer":"Medicaid or Medicare (survivor enrolled and kit not anonymous)"}
summary: If the survivor is covered by Medicaid or Medicare and the kit is not anonymous, the provider bills Medicaid or Medicare directly. This is an exception to billing insurance only by choice.

source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

summary: The Department of Justice also pays for follow-up services and exams related to the sexual assault, but not for other crime-related injuries under this rule.

source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

summary: The statute caps recovery at $50,000 per claimant per incident. The program web page states a lower figure; the statute controls.
quote: There shall be a $50,000 maximum recovery per claimant per incident.
source_title: RSA 21-M:8-h, Claimant Eligibility; Compensation

summary: Counseling is covered up to $4,000 or 40 visits, whichever comes first.
quote: The commission shall award compensation up to $4,000 in total expenses, or 40 visits, whichever comes first
source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

summary: Therapists who sign the program's treatment plan form agree to accept $75 per individual session and $35 per group session as payment in full.
quote: I will accept the NH Victims' Compensation Program's reimbursement of $75 for an individual, crime-related, therapy session and $35 for a group, crime-related, therapy session as payment in full
source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

summary: Relocation expenses are capped at $5,000, as a one-time benefit per claim.
quote: Relocation expenses shall be capped at $5,000
source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

summary: Safety and security expenses are capped at $3,000.
quote: Safety and security expenses shall be capped at $3,000.
source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

summary: Mileage for crime-related interviews, court proceedings, protective order hearings and parole is capped at $500.
quote: A $500 cap for mileage reimbursement for travel to crime-related interviews, pre-trial, trial, sentencing, hearings for securing protective orders and parole.
source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

summary: Reasonable and necessary medical treatment by licensed providers is covered after insurance and other sources are applied.
quote: The actual cost of reasonable and necessary medical treatment provided by licensed health-care personnel, after first applying any available insurance or other available collateral financial source
source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

summary: The program lists medical and dental care among the costs it can pay.
quote: Medical and dental care;
pinpoint: NH DOJ Victims' Compensation Program page, What Costs May Be Paid?
source_title: New Hampshire DOJ, Victims' Compensation Program page and FAQ

summary: Prescription medications for the survivor's physical and mental health injuries are covered.
quote: The portion of the cost of all prescription medications prescribed to treat the victim's physical and mental health injuries
source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

summary: Individual or group therapy by licensed mental health providers is covered for issues directly caused by the crime, after insurance.
quote: The actual cost of treatment, whether individual, group, or both, provided by licensed mental health personnel, after first applying any available insurance or other available collateral financial source, for mental health issues that were directly caused by the crime
source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

summary: Lost wages are covered at up to 75% of pre-crime wages for up to 3 months, counting any workers' compensation or disability benefits.
quote: The total compensation paid for lost wages shall not exceed 75% of the claimant's pre-crime wages, not to exceed 3 months, including any workers' compensation or disability benefits received.
source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

summary: Lost wages can be paid even if the survivor used paid leave to cover the time off, including time for medical, counseling, police and court appointments.
quote: Wages lost for any of the reasons listed under (c) above shall be compensable even if the claimant had leave time available from his or her employer and was paid by using such leave time.
source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

summary: Relocation is paid only if the offender is a continuing, credible threat to your safety. You also need a police report and a temporary restraining order or other court order. A final restraining order also counts. If you have no restraining order, a letter from a victim's advocate explaining why can count instead.
quote: The offender poses a continuing credible threat to the safety of the claimant; (2) There is either: a. A police report and a temporary restraining order or other court order have been issued against the claimant’s abuser or potential abuser or a final restraining order has been issued against the claimant’s abuser or potential abuser; or b. If the claimant does not have a restraining order against the abuser, the claimant shall present a letter from a victim’s advocate setting forth the basis for not obtaining a protective order, which may include, among other reasons, safety concerns for the claimant
source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

summary: Security costs are covered, including installing a home monitoring system, up to one year of monitoring, and locks for windows and doors.
quote: Installation costs of a residential monitoring system; (2) Up to one year of residential monitoring; (3) Installation of locks and other devices to secure windows and doors in the residence
source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

summary: Mileage to medical appointments is paid at the Medicaid rate for trips over 10 miles round trip, capped at 100 miles round trip.
quote: Mileage to and from appointments with licensed health care providers, at the rate used by Medicaid to compensate mileage. Mileage shall be paid for trips over 10 miles round trip and is capped at 100 miles round trip
source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

summary: Shelter for the survivor and family is one of the goods a crisis center can pay for from emergency funds, which the commission then reimburses to the crisis center.
quote: The cost of shelter for the victim and the victim's family
source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

summary: As part of a relocation award, the cost of changing a cell phone number is covered.
quote: The cost, as billed by the cellular provider, for changing a cell phone number.
source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

summary: If the examining provider finds the survivor may have been exposed to HIV, the survivor is given a voucher for preventive medication.
quote: If it is determined by the examining health care provider that the victim may have been exposed to HIV/AIDS as a result of the assault, a voucher for prophylactic medication(s) shall be given to the victim.
source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

summary: Under medical expenses, the program can replace lost or badly damaged assistive devices the survivor already had, such as hearing aids, dentures, wheelchairs, and prescription glasses or contact lenses.
quote: Replacement of lost or badly damaged existing physically assistive devices such as: a. Hearing aids; b. Dentures; c. Prosthetic and other devices; d. Wheelchairs; e. Prescription eyeglasses and other corrective lenses, including contact lenses
source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

summary: The program cannot pay for property loss or for pain and suffering.
quote: The program does not have authority to award money for property loss or pain and suffering.
pinpoint: NH DOJ Victims' Compensation Program page, What Costs May Be Paid?
source_title: New Hampshire DOJ, Victims' Compensation Program page and FAQ

params: {"item":"cable television, long-distance telephone and internet service after relocation"}
summary: Relocation awards do not pay for cable television, long-distance phone service or internet service.
quote: No compensation shall be awarded for cable television, long-distance telephone, internet service
source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

params: {"item":"hospital care for an insured victim unless the hospital denied free or reduced-fee care"}
summary: Hospital care is not paid if the victim had health insurance and the hospital has not denied free or reduced-fee care.
quote: The commission shall not award compensation for hospital care if: a. The victim had health insurance at the time of treatment for injuries sustained as a direct result of the crime; and b. Free or reduced fee care has not been denied by the hospital
source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

params: {"years":2,"from":"crime","extension":"You can apply later with good cause, and some sexual abuse survivors have no deadline."}
summary: A claim must be filed within 2 years of the crime unless good cause is shown. A survivor of sexual abuse that happened when they were a minor may file at any time.
quote: The claimant, guardian ad litem or child advocate, or parent may file a claim for compensation within 2 years of the crime, unless good cause is shown. A claimant who was the victim of sexual abuse or human trafficking under subparagraph I(a)(3), or a guardian ad litem, child advocate, or parent on behalf of such claimant, may file a claim at any time.
source_title: RSA 21-M:8-h, Claimant Eligibility; Compensation

summary: A claim is denied if the crime was not reported within 5 days, unless good cause is shown, such as a medical condition, fear for safety, fear of retribution, or the survivor's emotional state or mental health.
quote: The crime was not reported within 5 days of the crime unless good cause, which shall include but not be limited to the following, is shown
source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

summary: A sexual assault survivor who sought a medical exam or treatment is treated as having reported to law enforcement and as having shown credible evidence of the crime.
quote: A victim who has sought medical treatment pursuant to (a) and (d) above shall be deemed to: (1) Have made a report to law enforcement in compliance with Jus 605.02(c); and (2) Have presented credible evidence that an eligible crime has occurred
source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

summary: A claim is denied if the victim did not cooperate in a meaningful way with law enforcement, unless there was good cause, such as fear of retaliation.
quote: The primary victim failed to cooperate materially with law enforcement agencies without good cause such as fear of retaliation by or on behalf of the offender
source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

summary: No reimbursement is paid unless the claimant has at least $100 in reimbursable expenses.
quote: No reimbursement shall be paid unless the claimant has incurred reimbursable expenses of at least $100.
source_title: RSA 21-M:8-h, Claimant Eligibility; Compensation

summary: The program is a payer of last resort: insurance and other sources are applied first.
quote: help eligible victims of eligible crimes with the expenses that have been incurred as a direct result of the crime by acting as a payer of last resort
source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

summary: If expenses the fund paid are later covered by insurance, a civil settlement, restitution or another source, the claimant must pay the fund back for the amount recovered.
quote: If expenses paid through the victims' assistance program fund are later covered by insurance settlements, civil suit settlements, or restitution, or through any other source, the claimant shall reimburse the fund for the amount of expenses recovered.
source_title: RSA 21-M:8-h, Claimant Eligibility; Compensation

summary: The commission considers the victim's contributory fault when deciding eligibility and the award amount.
quote: In determining eligibility and the amount of compensation to be awarded, the commission shall consider the contributory fault of the victim in causing his injury.
source_title: RSA 21-M:8-h, Claimant Eligibility; Compensation

summary: Contributory fault is not considered in setting the award for a survivor of sexual abuse or human trafficking that happened when they were a minor.
quote: The commission shall not consider contributory fault in determining the amount of compensation to be awarded if the claimant was a victim of sexual abuse or human trafficking under subparagraph I(a)(3).
source_title: RSA 21-M:8-h, Claimant Eligibility; Compensation

summary: A crisis center can give a domestic violence or sexual assault victim 10-day emergency funds (food, clothing, shelter, transportation, locks, medications), and the commission reimburses the crisis center, not the victim. The crisis center must send a police report or a restraining order with its request.
quote: the commission shall award compensation to a crisis center for payment of 10-day emergency funds by the crisis center to a victim of domestic violence or sexual assault
source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

summary: Emergency funds through a crisis center are limited to $1,000 per adult, not counting clothing.
quote: The per-adult limit for the provision of all goods and services, except the purchase of clothing pursuant to (d)(2) and (e)(1) above, shall be $1,000
source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

summary: Anyone who suffers personal injury from a felony or misdemeanor, including sexual assault, is an eligible victim.
quote: Any person who sustains personal injury as a result of a felony or misdemeanor
source_title: RSA 21-M:8-h, Claimant Eligibility; Compensation

summary: Personal injury includes mental health harm, not only physical injury.
quote: means death or corporeal or mental health damage suffered as a result of an eligible crime
source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

summary: A person who was a victim of sexual abuse while under 18 is an eligible victim.
quote: Any person who is a victim of sexual abuse or human trafficking and is under the age of 18 at the time of the offense
source_title: RSA 21-M:8-h, Claimant Eligibility; Compensation

params: {"rule":"Crime in New Hampshire (any victim), or crime elsewhere with no qualifying compensation program if the victim lived in New Hampshire"}
summary: Victims of crimes in New Hampshire are eligible regardless of where they live. New Hampshire residents hurt in a place without a qualifying compensation program are also covered.
quote: Any person who suffered personal injury or death as a direct result of an eligible crime occurring in either: (1) New Hampshire; or (2) Any other state or jurisdiction that does not have a crime compensation program meeting the requirements of 34 U.S.C. 20102(b), and such person was domiciled in New Hampshire at the time of the crime
source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

params: {"rule":"Citizenship and immigration status are not required"}
summary: Immigration status does not bar eligibility: non-citizens, with or without legal status, are eligible.
quote: an individual who is not a citizen of the United States or who is not a legal alien shall be considered victims eligible for compensation under this section.
source_title: RSA 21-M:8-h, Claimant Eligibility; Compensation

params: {"method":"mail","target":"New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Department of Justice 33 Capitol Street Concord, N.H. 03301-6397"}
summary: Mail the completed paper application to the Victims' Compensation Program at the Department of Justice in Concord. This is the return address printed on the application form.
quote: Please return completed application to: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Department of Justice 33 Capitol Street Concord, N.H. 03301-6397
source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

params: {"method":"mail","target":"New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Department of Justice 1 Granite Place South Concord, NH 03301"}
summary: The program page lists a newer office address in Concord (Granite Place South). The form still prints the Capitol Street address, so a survivor may want to call the program to confirm which address to use.
quote: How To Contact Our Office New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Department of Justice 1 Granite Place South Concord, NH 03301
pinpoint: Program page, How To Contact Our Office
source_title: New Hampshire DOJ, Victims' Compensation Program page and FAQ

params: {"document":"itemized_bill","note":"Copies of bills from every provider listed (hospital, doctors, dentists, counselors, ambulance, radiology, prescriptions), if available."}
summary: For medical, dental, or counseling costs, list every provider and enclose copies of their bills if you have them.
quote: If applicable, list all providers that provided treatment, including hospital, doctors, dentists, mental health counselors, ambulance, radiology and prescriptions (drugs and eyeglasses). Attach additional sheets if necessary. If available, please enclose copies of bills.
source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

params: {"document":"itemized_bill","note":"Photocopies of all crime-related mental health counseling bills."}
summary: After the application arrives, the program may ask for photocopies of all crime-related counseling bills.
quote: Photocopies of all crime-related mental health counseling bills
source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

params: {"document":"other","note":"A signed HIPAA-compliant hospital and/or medical release so the program can request records and itemized statements from providers."}
summary: To claim medical or hospital costs, sign a HIPAA-compliant medical release so the program can get itemized statements and records from your providers.
quote: If a claimant seeks compensation for medical expenses, the victim or victim's parent or guardian shall complete and submit a HIPAA- compliant hospital and/or medical release.
source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

params: {"document":"wage_verification","note":"Copies of pay stubs if employed when the crime happened."}
summary: To claim lost wages, fill in the employment section and send copies of your pay stubs.
quote: If yes, complete the following section, and submit copies of your pay stubs.
source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

params: {"document":"wage_verification","note":"If self-employed, a copy of the tax return for the year before the crime."}
summary: If you were self-employed, send a copy of your tax return for the year before the crime instead of pay stubs.
quote: If you were self-employed at the time of the crime, please submit a copy of your tax return documentation for the year before the crime.
source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

params: {"document":"other","note":"A doctor's statement verifying how long you could not work, if you missed more than two weeks."}
summary: If you missed more than two weeks of work, include a doctor's statement saying how long you were unable to work.
quote: If you have missed more than two weeks of work, please provide a doctor's statement verifying length of time you were unable to work.
source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

params: {"document":"other","note":"Copies of written appointment confirmations (medical, mental health, police, and other crime-related appointments)."}
summary: For lost wages, keep and send copies of written confirmations of crime-related appointments such as medical, counseling, and police meetings.
quote: Copies of all written confirmations of appointments with medical providers, mental health providers, police and other law-enforcement officials, and any other appointments necessitated as a direct result of the crime.
source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

params: {"document":"insurance_statement","note":"Automobile insurance policy declarations page, only if the crime involved a motor vehicle."}
summary: If the crime involved a motor vehicle, include your auto insurance policy declarations page.
quote: Did the crime involve motor vehicles? (If yes, please provide your automobile insurance policy declarations page.)
source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

params: {"document":"other","note":"A separate sheet explaining any insurance, benefits, or other resources that may cover the expenses, with names, addresses, and phone numbers."}
summary: If insurance, leave, benefits, restitution, or any other resource might cover part of the costs, explain it on a separate sheet and attach it.
quote: please explain in full on a separate piece of paper and attach it to this application.
pinpoint: Application, Section 12 (Statement of Facts and Authorization)
source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

params: {"document":"other","note":"Copies of documents showing you were found ineligible for Medicaid, Medicare, hospital free care, or other public assistance, if you applied."}
summary: If you applied for Medicaid, Medicare, hospital free care, or public assistance and were turned down, attach copies of the denial documents.
quote: attach copies of the documents that show your ineligibility for public assistance.
pinpoint: Application, Section 12 (Statement of Facts and Authorization)
source_title: New Hampshire Victims' Compensation Program Application Form (rev. 02/11/2021)

summary: After the program receives the application, staff will contact the applicant by mail or email within 2 weeks. This is first contact, not a decision.
quote: Once the program receives your application, you will be contacted by mail or email within 2 weeks.
pinpoint: Program page FAQ, How Long Will It Take?
source_title: New Hampshire DOJ, Victims' Compensation Program page and FAQ

summary: Once an application is complete, the rules say no more than 60 days should pass before the commission can decide. The program page warns the whole process may take several months or longer while police reports are gathered.
quote: In no case shall placement on the agenda result in the passage of more than 60 days after the claimant submitted a completed application before a decision can be made by the commission.
source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

params: {"program_name":"Address Confidentiality Program (ACP)","agency":"New Hampshire Department of Justice, Office of the Attorney General","covers_sexual_assault":true,"enroll":"Contact a New Hampshire crisis center first for consultation and assistance, which the law requires; the application is then filed with the attorney general on the form the attorney general prescribes, with a sworn statement that the applicant is a victim of domestic violence, stalking, or sexual assault and fears for their safety. A restraining order, pending charges, or a police report are not required."}
summary: Survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, or stalking can apply to New Hampshire's Address Confidentiality Program if they meet its eligibility guidelines.
quote: Any adult person, a parent or guardian acting on behalf of a minor or guardian acting on behalf of an incapacitated person, may apply to the program if they are a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault or stalking and meet the eligibility guidelines.
pinpoint: DOJ ACP page, FAQ: What are the eligibility guidelines?
source_title: New Hampshire DOJ, Address Confidentiality Program page and FAQ

params: {"program_name":"Address Confidentiality Program (ACP)","agency":"New Hampshire Department of Justice, Office of the Attorney General","covers_sexual_assault":true}
summary: You do not need a restraining order, pending criminal charges, or a police report to take part in the program.
quote: Having a restraining order, criminal charges pending or even reporting the abuse to law enforcement are not required in order to participate in the ACP.
pinpoint: DOJ ACP page, FAQ: What are the eligibility guidelines?
source_title: New Hampshire DOJ, Address Confidentiality Program page and FAQ

summary: Everything the compensation program receives or keeps about a claim is confidential and may not be released to anyone unless the claimant authorizes it or another law allows it.
quote: All information received, obtained, or maintained by the program in connection with any claim for victims' compensation shall be maintained as confidential material, and shall not be released or disclosed to any person or entity whatsoever, except as authorized by the claimant or as otherwise provided by law.
source_title: N.H. Admin. Rules, Chapter Jus 600, Victims' Compensation

summary: Each county Sexual Assault Nurse Examiner program must make sure survivors are not charged any fee for services directly tied to the forensic exam, including screening, STI prophylaxis, pregnancy tests and emergency contraception.
quote: Develop and implement procedures to ensure that victims of sexual assault are not charged any fee for services that are directly associated with forensic sexual assault examinations, including routine medical screening, medications for prophylaxis of sexually transmitted infections, pregnancy tests, emergency contraception, supplies, equipment and use of space.

summary: The Attorney General's office says the medical-forensic exam is free, and a survivor does not have to report to police to get one.
quote: The medical-forensic exam is free and a victim of sexual assault does not need to report the assault to the police to have an exam.
pinpoint: NJ OAG, Sexual Assault Victims page (Forensic Nurse Examiner section)
source_title: NJ OAG Sexual Assault Victims page

summary: Under the Attorney General's SART standards, survivors are not charged for the forensic exam, preventive medication or the evidence kits, but emergency care beyond the exam itself can be billed under hospital policy.
quote: Victims shall not be charged for the medical forensic exam, prophylactic medication, or the SAFE Kit and/or DFSA/Tox Kit. (N.J.S.A 52:4B-52(k)). However, the victim shall be charged pursuant to hospital policy for any services provided beyond this scope.
pinpoint: AG Standards for Providing Services to Victims of Sexual Assault (2018), Standard on the medical forensic exam, Non-Participating Examination Facilities
source_title: Attorney General Standards for Providing Services to Victims of Sexual Assault (2018)

summary: Except as the statute otherwise provides, the most the program can award is $25,000.
quote: compensation shall not be awarded under P.L.1971, c.317 (C.52:4B-1 et seq.) in an amount in excess of $25,000

params: {"amount_cents":2500000,"exception":"or more in cases the program finds catastrophic"}
summary: Except in cases the program finds catastrophic, no award can be more than $25,000.
quote: Except for cases determined to be catastrophic in nature, no compensation shall be awarded in an amount in excess of $ 25,000.
source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

summary: Counseling is capped at $20,000 per claim, no matter how many sessions, except in catastrophic cases.
quote: (b) Except for cases determined to be catastrophic in nature, the maximum award for unreimbursed and unreimbursable counseling expenses shall be $ 20,000, notwithstanding the number of counseling sessions attended.
source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

summary: Lost earnings are paid at no more than $600 a week.
quote: (h) The weekly maximum reimbursement for loss of earnings or support shall not exceed $ 600.00.
source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

summary: Lost earnings are limited to 104 weeks, or 260 weeks (five years) for a victim who is permanently disabled.
quote: (e) The maximum reimbursement for loss of earnings shall not exceed a total of 104 weeks, unless a victim has been rendered permanently disabled as defined by 42 U.S.C. §§ 1381. et seq., in which case loss of earnings may be awarded for a total period of 260 weeks (five years).
source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

summary: Moving expenses are capped at $3,000, when the Office finds relocation is needed for the victim's health and safety.
quote: (d) Maximum reimbursement for moving expenses shall be $ 3,000.
source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

summary: If the victim cannot move, the same $3,000 relocation allotment can go toward an alarm system, new locks, or other home security devices. It is not an extra $3,000 on top of relocation.
quote: In the event a victim is unable to relocate due to home ownership or other personal circumstances, the Office may apply the $ 3,000 allotted for moving expenses towards the victim's purchase of a security alarm system, new door locks, or any other reasonable home security device(s), needed for the purpose of protecting the health and safety of the victim and the victim's family.
source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

summary: Crime-related transportation is reimbursed at up to $10 a day, figured at 31 cents per mile.
quote: (a) Maximum reimbursement for transportation expenses incurred as a direct result of the incident giving rise to the claim shall not exceed $ 10.00 a day, calculated at the rate of.31 cents per mile up to the daily maximum allowance.
source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

summary: Transportation that is not medical is not covered, except travel to court proceedings related to the crime.
quote: All non-medically related transportation costs are excluded other than attendance at any court proceeding related to the crime.
source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

summary: Child care or day care is capped at $6,500 in total, except in catastrophic cases.
quote: 2. Except for cases determined to be catastrophic in nature, reimbursement for child care and/or day care services shall not exceed $ 6,500 in the aggregate.
source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

summary: Crime scene clean-up is capped at $4,000 in total.
quote: (f) An award of compensation for crime scene clean-up shall not exceed $ 4,000 in the aggregate.
source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

summary: The Office can pay up to $10,000 to a lawyer who helps the victim with a legal matter arising from the crime (other than the compensation claim itself).
quote: (b) The Office may allow payment of an attorney fee, including costs, up to a maximum of $ 10,000, to an attorney who provides legal assistance to a victim in any legal matter, other than a decision of the Office, arising from, or related to, having been the victim of the offense that forms the basis of the victim's or claimant's application for compensation.
source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

summary: When the victim dies, funeral costs are capped at $7,500.
quote: In claims involving the death of a victim, the maximum reimbursement for funeral expenses shall be $ 7,500.
source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

summary: Domestic help needed because of the crime (housecleaning, laundry, cooking and similar day-to-day support) is capped at $6,500 in total, except in catastrophic cases.
quote: Except for cases determined to be catastrophic in nature, the total amount of reimbursement for domestic help shall not exceed $ 6,500 in the aggregate.
source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

summary: Unreimbursed out-of-pocket medical care and other necessary services caused by the crime are reimbursable.
quote: Reimbursable expenses include those unreimbursed and unreimbursable out-of-pocket expenses or indebtedness for medical care or other necessary services, loss of earnings, loss of support, pecuniary loss to the dependents of deceased victims, and other reasonable pecuniary loss resulting from the personal injury or death of the victim.
source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

summary: Lost earnings caused by the crime are reimbursable.
quote: Reimbursable expenses include those unreimbursed and unreimbursable out-of-pocket expenses or indebtedness for medical care or other necessary services, loss of earnings, loss of support, pecuniary loss to the dependents of deceased victims, and other reasonable pecuniary loss resulting from the personal injury or death of the victim.
source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

summary: Mental health counseling related to the crime and not covered by insurance can be paid.
quote: Counseling: Mental health counseling expenses related to the incident and not covered by insurance.
source_title: NJ VCCO Application and Instructions (rev. 8/25/20)

summary: Dental costs from a crime-related injury that insurance does not fully cover can be paid.
quote: Dental: Dental expenses directly related to a crime related injury and not totally covered by insurance.
source_title: NJ VCCO Application and Instructions (rev. 8/25/20)

summary: Prescription costs from a crime-related injury that insurance does not fully cover can be paid.
quote: Prescription: Prescription expenses directly related to a crime related injury and not totally covered by insurance.
source_title: NJ VCCO Application and Instructions (rev. 8/25/20)

summary: As part of crime scene clean-up, the Office may pay the reasonable replacement value of bedding and clothing.
quote: The Office may award compensation for the reasonable replacement value of bedding and clothing;
source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

params: {"item":"personal property loss or damage (for example, a phone)"}
summary: Lost or damaged personal property, such as a phone, is not reimbursed unless the rules specifically allow it (for example, some crime scene items).
quote: (f) Except as otherwise permitted by this chapter, no compensation shall be awarded for loss of personal property or property damage.
source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

summary: The program does not pay for pain and suffering.
quote: (e) In making its award, the Office shall make no allowance for pain and suffering.
source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

params: {"years":5,"from":"crime","extension":"or later if the program finds good cause for the delay"}
summary: Apply within 5 years of the injury, or later if the Office finds good cause for the delay.
quote: unless the application has been made within five years after the date of the personal injury or death or after that date upon determination by the office that good cause exists for the delayed filing

summary: If the victim was under 18, the 5-year clock starts on their 18th birthday.
quote: If the victim is under 18 years of age, the five-year limit on filing shall commence on the day the victim turns 18 years old.

summary: For child sexual abuse, the application is due within 5 years after reasonable discovery of the injury and its link to the abuse, unless good cause is shown.
quote: In the case of child sexual abuse, defined as an act of sexual contact or sexual penetration between a child under the age of 18 and an adult, an application for compensation shall be filed within five years after reasonable discovery of the injury and its causal relationship to an act of child sexual abuse, unless good cause is shown, in accordance with N.J.S.A. 2A:61B-1.
source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

params: {"required":true,"alternatives":[],"within_months":9,"exception":"counted from the crime or from when it was reasonably discovered"}
summary: The crime must have been reported to police or another law enforcement agency within 9 months of when it happened or was reasonably discovered.
quote: which had been reported to the police or other appropriate law enforcement agency within nine months after its occurrence or reasonable discovery

summary: The Office can excuse a late police report for good cause.
quote: The Office reserves the right to, upon determination that good cause exists for the delayed filing, make an exception to the requirement that the incident be reported to the police within the stated time period.
source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

summary: The Attorney General's SART standards tell hospitals to inform survivors that compensation is only available to those who report the crime to law enforcement, even though the exam itself does not require a report.
quote: Victims shall be informed that VCCO benefits are only eligible to those victims who report the crime to law enforcement.
pinpoint: AG Standards for Providing Services to Victims of Sexual Assault (2018), Standard on the medical forensic exam
source_title: Attorney General Standards for Providing Services to Victims of Sexual Assault (2018)

summary: The program will not pay if the victim did not cooperate with reasonable requests from law enforcement. A compelling health or safety reason for not cooperating is the exception.
quote: No compensation shall be awarded if: a. Compensation to the victim proves to be substantial unjust enrichment to the offender or if the victim did not cooperate with the reasonable requests of law enforcement authorities unless the victim demonstrates a compelling health or safety reason for not cooperating

summary: There is no minimum loss requirement for crimes on or after June 26, 1995.
quote: There are no minimum loss requirements for incidents occurring on or after June 26, 1995.
pinpoint: NJ VCCO Eligibility page, Preconditions for Eligibility
source_title: NJ VCCO Eligibility page

summary: The program pays last, after insurance and other sources.
quote: The Victims of Crime Compensation Office (VCCO) is the payer of last resort.
pinpoint: NJ VCCO Eligibility page, Moneys from other Sources
source_title: NJ VCCO Eligibility page

summary: Money received or receivable from other sources because of the crime is taken into account when setting the award.
quote: (a) In determining the amount of compensation to be awarded, the Office shall take into consideration amounts received or receivable from other sources by the victim, claimant, and/or his or her dependents as a result of the offense or occurrence giving rise to the application.
source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

summary: The Office must consider whether the victim's conduct contributed to the injury and may reduce or deny the award on that basis.
quote: In determining the amount of an award, the office shall determine whether, because of the victim's conduct, the victim of such crime contributed to the infliction of the victim's injury, and the office shall reduce the amount of the award or reject the application altogether, in accordance with the determination

summary: When an award is reduced for the victim's conduct, it cannot exceed $12,500 in total.
quote: Where an award is to be limited or reduced due to contribution or other circumstances relating to the victim's behavior or action, said award shall not exceed $ 12,500 in the aggregate.
source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)
