summary: New Jersey's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Division on Women in the Department of Children and Families, is meant to keep the addresses of victims of domestic violence, stalking and sexual assault confidential. The law lets public agencies accept a program participant's substitute mailing address.
quote: to enable interagency cooperation with the Director of the Division on Women in the Department of Children and Families in providing address confidentiality for victims of domestic violence, stalking, and sexual assault, and reproductive health service patients and providers, and to enable public agencies to accept a program participant's use of an address designated by the director as a substitute mailing address.
source_title: N.J.S.A. 47:4-2 Address confidentiality for certain individuals (Justia 2025)

summary: VCCO claim files are confidential and are not government records open under the Open Public Records Act; nobody may inspect a victim's or claimant's file unless the law or a court order allows it.
quote: The files maintained by the Office that relate directly to the handling of any claim for compensation filed by a victim or claimant are not government records subject to disclosure under the Open Public Records Act and shall be considered confidential.
source_title: N.J.A.C. 13:75 (VCCO administrative code, OAG copy)

summary: A health care provider may not charge the survivor, directly or indirectly, for the costs of collecting a sexual assault examination kit. The statute does not say whether the survivor's insurance may be billed.
quote: No costs incurred by a health care provider for the collection of a sexual assault examination kit shall be charged directly or indirectly to the survivor of the sexual assault.
source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 30-9-21 (Sexual assault survivor's bill of rights)

params: {"payer":"The administrator under the Sexual Crimes Prosecution and Treatment Act (NMSA 29-11-3 defines this as the director of the mental health division of the Department of Health, or a designee)"}
summary: Under the Sexual Crimes Prosecution and Treatment Act, the state administrator must provide free forensic medical exams to victims of sexual crimes, arrange free exams, or reimburse victims for the exam cost.
quote: The administrator shall: A. provide free forensic medical exams to victims of sexual crimes; B. arrange for victims of sexual crimes to obtain free forensic medical exams; or C. reimburse victims of sexual crimes for the cost of forensic medical exams
source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 29-11-7 (Free forensic medical exams for victims of sexual crimes)

params: {"payer":"The administrator under the Sexual Crimes Prosecution and Treatment Act, by reimbursement"}
summary: If the victim is reimbursed for the exam instead of getting it free, reimbursement covers the full cost with no deductible or limit, and the victim can apply for reimbursement for one year from the exam date.
quote: the reimbursement covers the full cost of the forensic medical exam, without any deductible requirement or limit on the amount of the reimbursement; (2) the victim of a sexual crime is entitled to apply for reimbursement for a period of one year from the date of the forensic medical exam
source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 29-11-7 (Free forensic medical exams for victims of sexual crimes)

params: {"amount_cents":2000000,"exception":"or up to $30,000 more if an injury leaves you fully disabled for life"}
summary: The maximum award is $20,000 per victim. The commission may add up to $30,000 more for extraordinary losses when the injury is catastrophic and causes permanent total disability.
quote: No award of reparation shall be in excess of twenty thousand dollars ($20,000) per victim, except that the commission may award up to an additional thirty thousand dollars ($30,000) for extraordinary pecuniary losses, if the personal injury to a victim is catastrophic and results in a permanent total disability.
source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 31-22-14 (Limitations on award; collateral recovery; preliminary award)

summary: Mental health counseling is approved for up to 30 sessions per eligible person unless the commission approves more therapy.
quote: The commission shall approve up to thirty sessions per person deemed eligible under the application submitted unless approval for additional therapy has been granted by the commission.
source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

summary: Funeral expenses are capped at $6,000.
quote: Awards for funeral expenses shall not exceed six thousand dollars ($6,000.00).
source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

summary: Replacement of eyeglasses or contact lenses damaged in the crime is capped at $350.
quote: Awards for eyeglasses or contact lenses shall not exceed three hundred fifty dollars ($350.00).
source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

summary: Native American medicine man treatment fees can be considered, up to $3,000 per application unless the board approves more in advance.
quote: In all cases of medicine man care, the commission board shall only approve up to $3,000.00 per application unless prior approval has been granted by the commission board for additional treatment.
source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

summary: The commission may pay expenses actually and reasonably incurred because of the victim's injury.
quote: The commission may order payment of reparation for: A. expenses actually and reasonably incurred as a result of the victim's injury or death;
source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 31-22-9 (Award of reparation)

summary: The program lists medical and dental care and mental health counseling (30 session maximum) as types of reparation.
quote: Medical and dental care; Mental health counseling; (30 session maximum)
pinpoint: CVRC Compensation FAQ, What are the types of reparation?
source_title: CVRC Compensation Application and FAQ page

summary: The commission may pay for the victim's lost earning power from total or partial incapacity.

source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 31-22-9 (Award of reparation)

summary: Lost wages can be paid for a recovery period of up to 14 calendar days after the crime without a physician's certification. The person must have been employed at the time of the incident.
quote: Loss of wages may be paid to the victim, claimant, and/or, in the case of a minor victim, guardian, for up to fourteen calendar days after the crime for a recovery period.
source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

This travel shall be verified by the health provider's billing and reports for the travel requested. The gas will be reimbursed at the rate of twenty cents per mile.
source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

summary: Attorney fees are not paid as part of or on top of a reparation award.
quote: None of the appropriation in this act [31-22-1 to 31-22-21 NMSA 1978] shall be used to pay attorney fees either as part of or in addition to awards of reparation.
source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 31-22-6 (Medical examination; attorneys' fees; penalty)

summary: Apply within two years after the injury. The statute makes an exception for minors who were victims of child abuse or abandonment, criminal sexual penetration, or criminal sexual contact of a minor. It does not say what deadline applies to them instead.
quote: An application for reparation shall be made within two years after the injury or death, except for minors who are victims of criminal activity under the provisions of Section 30-6-1 NMSA 1978, regarding abandonment or abuse of a child, Section 30-9-11 NMSA 1978, regarding criminal sexual penetration, or Section 30-9-13 NMSA 1978, regarding criminal sexual contact of a minor.
source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 31-22-14 (Limitations on award; collateral recovery; preliminary award)

summary: A police report is not the only option. The crime must have led to an arrest, been reported to police in a reasonable time, or been reported to a licensed medical, mental health or counseling provider, or a tribal health provider.
quote: provided an arrest has been made or the act or omission constituting a crime has been reported to the police in a reasonable time or the act or omission constituting a crime has been reported to a licensed medical, mental health or counseling provider, or tribal health provider.
source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 31-22-7 (Eligibility for reparation)

summary: The victim or claimant must have fully cooperated with law enforcement, unless the commission finds they acted reasonably under the circumstances.
quote: the claimant or victim fully cooperated with the appropriate law enforcement agencies or the commission finds that the claimant or victim acted reasonably under the circumstances.
source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 31-22-7 (Eligibility for reparation)

summary: Payments from collateral sources such as insurance, Medicaid, Medicare, or government benefits are deducted from the award.
quote: the commission shall deduct from any reparation awarded any payments received from a collateral source or from the United States or the state or any of its political subdivisions for injury or death subject to reparation under the Crime Victims Reparation Act.
source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 31-22-14 (Limitations on award; collateral recovery; preliminary award)

summary: Expenses covered by insurance or another collateral source must be submitted there first. Only what those sources do not cover is considered.
quote: shall submit covered expenses to the source(s) for payment. Only those expenses not covered by the collateral source(s) will be considered for reparation.
source_title: 10.40.2 NMAC (Crime Victims Reparation Commission, Compensation)

summary: The commission considers the victim's behavior and reduces the award by the degree of responsibility it attributes to the victim. Shown for information only.
quote: The commission shall consider the behavior of the victim and whether, because of provocation or otherwise, the victim bears responsibility for the act or omission constituting a crime that caused the victim's injury or death and shall reduce the amount of reparation in accordance with its assessment of the degree of responsibility attributable to the victim.
source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 31-22-7 (Eligibility for reparation)

summary: If a final award looks likely, the director can authorize a preliminary award with the commission chair's agreement. It is deducted from the final award.
quote: If it appears that a final award of reparation will be made by the commission, a preliminary award may be authorized by the director of the commission or the commission's designee when the commission chair concurs.
source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 31-22-14 (Limitations on award; collateral recovery; preliminary award)

summary: Criminal sexual penetration and criminal sexual contact of a minor are covered crimes.
quote: (9) criminal sexual penetration; (10) criminal sexual contact of a minor;
source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 31-22-8 (Crimes enumerated)

summary: Injury includes bodily harm, pregnancy, and extreme mental distress, so a victim does not need a physical injury to qualify.

source_title: NMSA 1978, Section 31-22-3 (Definitions)

summary: New Mexico's Safe at Home program, run by the Secretary of State, lets survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, attempted sexual assault or stalking use the Secretary of State's address as a substitute address with state and local agencies, with mail forwarded to their real address. Applicants fill out the application packet with an application assistant from a domestic violence or sexual assault program, and the forms are notarized.

summary: The costs of a sexual assault forensic medical exam must not be charged directly to the survivor. The statute does not say whether the survivor's insurance may be billed.

params: {"payer":"State Fund for the Compensation of Victims of Crime; the county where the offense happened pays any remainder if the Fund is short"}
summary: A medical provider's costs for the forensic exam are paid from the state Fund for the Compensation of Victims of Crime. If the Fund does not have enough money, the county where the assault happened pays the rest.
quote: any costs incurred by a medical provider for the forensic medical examination of the victim must be paid out of the Fund for the Compensation of Victims of Crime, unless there is not sufficient money in the Fund to pay such costs. If there is not sufficient money in the Fund to pay such costs, the county in whose jurisdiction the offense was committed shall pay any remaining costs.
source_title: NRS Chapter 217 (Aid to Certain Victims of Crime), Rev. 4/15/2026

source_title: NRS Chapter 217 (Aid to Certain Victims of Crime), Rev. 4/15/2026

summary: The costs of the county-paid medical care for physical injuries from the assault must not be charged directly to the survivor.

quote: no such award shall exceed six hundred dollars for each week of lost earnings or support.
source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

summary: Relocation expenses are capped at $2,500.
quote: reasonable relocation expenses not exceeding twenty-five hundred dollars
source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

summary: Employment-related transportation (extra cost of getting to work because of crime injuries) is capped at $2,500. Medical and court travel are not under this cap.
quote: reasonable employment-related transportation expenses, not exceeding twenty-five hundred dollars
source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

summary: Crime scene cleanup and securing a crime scene (for example repairing doors, windows, and locks) are capped at $2,500.
quote: the costs of crime scene cleanup and securing of a crime scene not exceeding twenty-five hundred dollars
source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

summary: Repair or replacement of essential personal property is capped at $2,500, with cash losses limited to $100.
quote: Any award made for the cost of repair or replacement of essential personal property, including cash losses of essential personal property, shall be limited to an amount of twenty-five hundred dollars, except that all cash losses of essential personal property shall be limited to the amount of one hundred dollars.
source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

params: {"expense":"property_replacement","amount_cents":150000,"per":"item","item":"items related to the victim's ability to communicate"}
summary: Essential property related to the victim's ability to communicate is paid at the receipted amount, up to $1,500 per item.
quote: All awards made pursuant to Executive Law article 22 and this Part related to a victim's ability to communicate shall be limited to the receipted amount, in an amount not exceeding one-thousand five-hundred dollars per item.
source_title: 9 NYCRR 525.12 (Manner of payment; awards), via Cornell LII

params: {"expense":"property_replacement","amount_cents":250000,"per":"item","item":"items for the safe operation of the victim's personal means of transportation"}
summary: Essential property related to safely operating the victim's own means of transportation is paid at the receipted amount, up to $2,500 per item.
quote: All awards made pursuant to Executive Law article 22 and this Part related to a victim's safe operation of their personal means of transportation shall be limited to the receipted amount, in an amount not exceeding two-thousand five-hundred dollars per item.
source_title: 9 NYCRR 525.12 (Manner of payment; awards), via Cornell LII

summary: Medically necessary life-sustaining equipment lost or damaged in the crime has its own cap of $10,000 instead of the general essential property cap.
quote: In the case of medically necessary life-sustaining equipment which was lost or damaged as the direct result of a crime, the award shall be limited to the amount of ten thousand dollars.
source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

summary: Outerwear, suits, and footwear are paid at the receipted amount, up to $500 per item.
quote: Items of outerwear, suits and footwear shall be the receipted amount, in an amount not exceeding five-hundred dollars per item.
source_title: 9 NYCRR 525.12 (Manner of payment; awards), via Cornell LII

params: {"expense":"property_replacement","amount_cents":10000,"per":"item","item":"clothing other than outerwear, suits and footwear"}
summary: Other clothing is paid at the receipted amount, up to $100 per item.
quote: All other items of clothing shall be the receipted amount, in an amount not exceeding one-hundred dollars per item.
source_title: 9 NYCRR 525.12 (Manner of payment; awards), via Cornell LII

summary: A mattress and platform or box spring are paid at the receipted amount, up to $2,000.
quote: Mattress and platform or box spring shall be the receipted amount, in an amount not exceeding two-thousand dollars.
source_title: 9 NYCRR 525.12 (Manner of payment; awards), via Cornell LII

params: {"expense":"property_replacement","amount_cents":50000,"per":"claim","item":"bedding other than mattress and box spring"}
summary: Other bedding is paid at the receipted amount, up to $500 in total.
quote: All other items of bedding shall be the receipted amount, in a cumulative amount not exceeding five-hundred dollars.
source_title: 9 NYCRR 525.12 (Manner of payment; awards), via Cornell LII

summary: Attorney fees for representation before OVS or on judicial review are capped at $1,000.
quote: the cost of reasonable attorneys' fees for representation before the office and/or before the appellate division upon judicial review not to exceed one thousand dollars.
source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 626 (Out-of-pocket loss; definition)

params: {"item":"periodic monitoring or maintenance charges for security devices"}
summary: For security devices, only the device and installation are covered; monitoring and maintenance fees are not.
quote: Compensable costs shall be limited to the devices themselves and their installation, and shall not include the periodic service charges for monitoring or maintaining any such devices.
source_title: 9 NYCRR 525.12 (Manner of payment; awards), via Cornell LII

summary: Meals during travel for medical care are not reimbursed as transportation.
quote: Meals shall not be considered a related transportation expense.
source_title: 9 NYCRR 525.3 (Definitions), via Cornell LII

params: {"item":"purchase, lease or rental of a vehicle"}
summary: Employment-related transportation does not cover buying, leasing, or renting a vehicle.
quote: Such costs shall not include the purchase, lease or rental of a vehicle.
source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 621 (Definitions)

params: {"years":3,"from":"crime","extension":"or of when the crime was discovered, or later if OVS finds good cause"}
summary: File within 3 years of the crime or its discovery; OVS may extend this for good cause.
quote: A claim must be filed by the claimant not later than three years after the occurrence or discovery of the crime upon which such claim is based, three years after a court finds a lawsuit to be frivolous, or not later than three years after the death of the victim, provided, however, that upon good cause shown, the office may extend the time for filing.
source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 625 (Filing of claims)

params: {"years":3,"from":"crime","extension":"good reasons, including not knowing compensation existed or not knowing you may be eligible"}
summary: Even after 3 years, OVS can waive the deadline for good reasons, such as not knowing the program existed or not knowing you were eligible.
quote: Please keep in mind that even if it has been more than three years, OVS has the ability to waive this requirement if the claimant or victim/survivor can show they had good reasons for not filing a claim within that timeframe. Good reasons can include, but are not limited to not knowing that victim compensation existed, or not knowing that they may be eligible for compensation.
pinpoint: OVS Compensation Program Updates for Victims and Survivors, Timely Filing
source_title: OVS Compensation Program Updates for Victims and Survivors

summary: A police report is not required. The crime must have been reported, but records of a support agency for survivors of crime can show this instead of police records.
quote: the records of a support agency for survivors of crime or the records of a criminal justice agency show that such crime was reported.
source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

summary: A medical facility that provides forensic exams for rape and sexual assault counts as a support agency, so its records can stand in for a police report.
quote: any medical facility established under the laws of the state that provides a forensic physical examination for victims of rape and sexual assault
source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

summary: For sex offenses, a family court also counts as a support agency.
quote: in cases involving any sex offense or family offense a support agency for survivors of crime shall also include a family court
source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

summary: Since December 31, 2025, a victim service provider or a medical or mental health professional can fill out a Crime Verification Form instead of a police report.
quote: Starting December 31, 2025, instead of filing a report with law enforcement, you can go to a local victim service provider , or a medical or mental health professional, and tell them that you or a loved one experienced a crime. The provider can fill out a short form to tell OVS about the crime.
pinpoint: OVS Compensation Program Updates for Victims and Survivors, Reporting a Crime
source_title: OVS Compensation Program Updates for Victims and Survivors

summary: Under the statute, when the victim cannot report to or cooperate with police because of age, physical or psychological state, cultural or language barriers, or another health or safety concern, a court that issued a restraining or protective order, a contracted victim services provider, or a licensed medical or mental health provider also counts as a support agency.
quote: in cases where a physically injured claimant and/or victim is unable to report to or otherwise cooperate with a criminal justice agency because of the victim's age, physical condition, psychological state, cultural or linguistic barriers, or any other health or safety concern that jeopardizes the victim's wellbeing, a support agency for survivors of crime shall also include: (A) a court which issued a temporary or permanent restraining order or protective order against the party or parties alleged to have committed the crime against the victim, or (B) a "victim services provider"
source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

summary: Awards are reduced by payments from the offender, mandated insurance, public funds, the claimant's own insurance, and any emergency award.
quote: Any award made pursuant to this article shall be reduced by the amount of any payments received or to be received by the claimant as a result of the injury (a) from or on behalf of the person who committed the crime, (b) under insurance programs mandated by law, (c) from public funds, (d) under any contract of insurance wherein the claimant is the insured or beneficiary, (e) as an emergency award pursuant to section six hundred thirty of this article.
source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

summary: OVS pays last: insurance or benefit plans must be billed first. The forensic exam has its own billing rules, shown in the exam section.
quote: OVS is the payer of last resort and can only consider your out-of-pocket loss. OVS can only process payments for crime-related expenses. You must bill your insurance company or benefits plan before OVS can pay.
source_title: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (English, fillable PDF)

summary: OVS considers whether the victim's own conduct contributed to the injury and can reduce or deny the award on that basis.
quote: the office shall determine whether, because of such victim's conduct, the victim of such crime contributed to the infliction of such victim's injury, and the office shall reduce the amount of the award or reject the claim altogether, in accordance with such determination.
source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 631 (Awards)

summary: Being a victim of sexual assault is a mitigating factor, and OVS may then make the award with no conduct reduction.
quote: However, when considering conduct contributing the office shall examine the following mitigating factors: the victim was a minor, a victim of human trafficking, a sex worker, or a victim of sexual assault. If any such mitigating factors are found in the investigation of the claim pursuant to subdivision (b) of section 525.5 of this part, the office may make an award without reduction for conduct contributing.
source_title: 9 NYCRR 525.12 (Manner of payment; awards), via Cornell LII

summary: When an award is likely and waiting would cause undue hardship, OVS can make emergency awards totaling up to $2,500, which are later deducted from the final award.
quote: the office may make one or more emergency awards to the claimant pending a final decision of the office or payment of an award in the case, provided, however, that the total amount of such emergency awards shall not exceed twenty-five hundred dollars.
source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 630 (Emergency awards)

summary: Victims of sex offenses under Penal Law article 130 are presumed to have suffered physical injury, which is the usual gateway to compensation.
quote: For the purposes of this subdivision, the victim of a sex offense as defined in article one hundred thirty of the penal law is presumed to have suffered physical injury.
source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 626 (Out-of-pocket loss; definition)

summary: Acts committed in New York count as crimes for compensation whether or not anyone was arrested, charged, or prosecuted, and whether or not the claimant dealt with police.
quote: an act committed in New York state which would, if committed by a mentally competent criminally responsible adult, who has no legal exemption or defense, constitute a crime as defined in and proscribed by law, regardless of whether any suspect was arrested, charged, apprehended or prosecuted for the commission of the act or whether the claimant has interacted with a criminal justice agency investigating such act
source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 621 (Definitions)

params: {"rule":"New York residents victimized in a state without an eligible compensation program"}
summary: A New York resident hurt by a crime in another state can apply only if that state has no eligible compensation program.
quote: an act committed outside the state of New York against a resident of the state of New York which would be compensable had it occurred within the state of New York and which occurred in a state which does not have an eligible crime victim compensation program
source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 621 (Definitions)

quote: Mailing Address: NYS Office of Victim Services AE Smith Building 80 S. Swan Street Albany, NY 12210-8002

quote: Email applications and documents to: OVSIntake@ovs.ny.gov
pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 2, OVS Contact Information
source_title: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (English, fillable PDF)

summary: A claim can be filed online through the OVS Compass Applicant Portal, as a guest or with a NY.gov account.
quote: Yes, you can visit https://ovs.ny.gov/ to access the secure OVS Compass Applicant Portal, or Victim Advocate Portal, and file an application online.

source_title: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (English, fillable PDF)

summary: Include one completed HIPAA authorization for each medical and mental health provider seen for crime-related care.
quote: One completed HIPAA form for each medical and mental health provider you saw for services related to this crime.
pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 2, Processing Your Claim
source_title: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (English, fillable PDF)

params: {"document":"insurance_statement","note":"letters from insurers or government agencies denying or approving payment"}
summary: Include any letters from insurance companies or government agencies that denied or authorized payment for the claimed expenses.
quote: Letters from any insurance or government agencies denying or authorizing payments related to goods and services you described in this application.
pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 2, Processing Your Claim
source_title: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (English, fillable PDF)

params: {"document":"other","note":"crime verification: one third-party document, such as a Crime Verification Form from a victim service provider or a medical or mental health professional"}
summary: Only one third-party document confirming the crime is needed, and a Crime Verification Form from a victim service provider or medical or mental health professional works.
quote: You only need to submit one document showing OVS that a third-party has confirmed that you or the victim/survivor experienced a crime. You can speak to a victim service provider or medical or mental health professional, and they can fill out a Crime Verification Form.
pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 9, Supporting Documentation for Crime Verification
source_title: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (English, fillable PDF)

params: {"document":"police_report","note":"optional; a police or other criminal justice agency report is one way to verify the crime, not the only way"}
summary: A police or other criminal justice agency report can be submitted as the crime verification document, but it is a choice.
quote: You may also choose to report the crime to law enforcement and submit a criminal justice agency report, like a police report, as part of this application.
pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 9, Supporting Documentation for Crime Verification
source_title: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (English, fillable PDF)

params: {"document":"exam_record","note":"optional; the applicant can choose to use the forensic rape exam report as part of the application"}
summary: If a forensic rape exam was done, the survivor can choose to use the exam report in the application.
quote: If an FRE was performed, do you want to use the report as part of your application?
pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 10, Medical Care
source_title: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (English, fillable PDF)

params: {"document":"other","note":"Workers' Compensation or disability insurance decision letter, only if the victim has that coverage"}
summary: If the victim has Workers' Compensation or disability insurance coverage, OVS needs that provider's decision letter.
quote: If the victim has coverage through either Worker's Compensation or a Disability Insurance provider, OVS will need the decision letter from either Worker's Compensation or the Disability Insurance provider to help determine eligibility for compensation.
pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 16, Workers Compensation/Disability
source_title: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (English, fillable PDF)

Completed applications may either be mailed or faxed. Filing instructions are on the form. (DOS ACP: (518) 474-7306, toll-free (855) 350-4595, Address Confidentiality Program, P.O. Box 1110, Albany, NY 12201-1110, fax (518) 474-0709.)"}
summary: The Department of State runs an Address Confidentiality Program that gives eligible victims, including victims of a sexual offense, a designated substitute address to use instead of their real address, with free mail forwarding.
quote: There is created in the office of the secretary of state a program to be known as the "address confidentiality program" to protect victims of domestic violence, victims of human trafficking, victims of kidnapping, victims of a sexual offense, victims of stalking, and reproductive health care services providers, employees, volunteers, patients, or immediate family members of reproductive health care services providers by authorizing the use of designated addresses for such victims and their minor children.
source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 108 (Address confidentiality program)

summary: OVS records and proceedings on a victim's or claimant's compensation claim are confidential and are not shared with government or private entities, except for listed purposes such as criminal justice requests, judicial subpoenas, the claimant's own requests, and program administration.
quote: Records maintained by the office and proceedings by the office based thereon regarding a claim submitted by a victim or a claimant shall be deemed confidential and shall not be shared with any government or private entity, with the following exceptions:
source_title: N.Y. Executive Law 633 (Confidentiality of records)

params: {"insurance_billing":"prohibited","scope":"the exam and tests done to gather evidence","condition":"if the crime was in Ohio"}
summary: Hospitals may not bill a survivor of a sex crime under Ohio law, or the survivor's insurance, for the medical exam and tests done to gather evidence. The rule covers only that evidence exam, not other care at the same visit.
quote: No costs incurred by a hospital or emergency facility in conducting a medical examination and test of any victim of an offense under any provision of sections 2907.02 to 2907.06 of the Revised Code for the purpose of gathering physical evidence for a possible prosecution of a person shall be billed or charged directly or indirectly to the victim or the victim's insurer.
source_title: ORC 2907.28 (payment for sexual assault medical examination)

params: {"payer":"Ohio reparations fund, paid by the Attorney General (SAFE Program) directly to the hospital or facility"}
summary: The state reparations fund pays the hospital for the forensic exam, including antibiotics and HIV post-exposure prophylaxis given as part of the exam.
quote: Any cost incurred by a hospital or emergency medical facility in conducting a medical examination of a victim of an offense under any provision of sections 2907.02 to 2907.06 of the Revised Code for the purpose of gathering physical evidence for a possible prosecution, including the cost of any antibiotics administered as part of the examination and the cost of HIV post-exposure prophylaxis provided as part of the examination, shall be paid out of the reparations fund established pursuant to section 2743.191 of the Revised Code
source_title: ORC 2907.28 (payment for sexual assault medical examination)

params: {"payer":"Ohio Attorney General SAFE Program (flat fee to the facility)"}
summary: The hospital must accept a flat fee of $632 from the state as payment in full for the forensic exam, including antibiotics given during it.
quote: A hospital, children's advocacy center, or other emergency medical facility shall accept a flat fee payment of: (A) Six hundred thirty-two dollars as payment in full for any cost incurred in conducting a medical examination and test of a victim of an offense under any provision of sections 2907.02 to 2907.06 of the Revised Code for the purpose of gathering physical evidence for a possible prosecution of a person, including the cost of any antibiotics administered as part of the examination.
source_title: OAC 109:7-1-02 (sexual assault examination payment amount)

summary: Payment for the forensic exam does not depend on the survivor cooperating with police.
quote: The sexual assault forensic exam and reimbursement is not dependent on the patient cooperating with law enforcement.
pinpoint: SAFE Reimbursement Instructions, item 12 (Law enforcement reporting)
source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Instructions for SAFE and HIV Prophylaxis Reimbursement Form

summary: If an adult patient does not report to police and asks to stay fully anonymous, the provider can send the exam's payment form as Jane or John Doe.
quote: If the adult patient chooses not to report to law enforcement and asks that their identity be kept completely confidential, a reimbursement form submitted on behalf of “Jane/John Doe” is an acceptable submission.
source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Instructions for SAFE and HIV Prophylaxis Reimbursement Form

params: {"payer":"Patient, when an adult's last incident was more than 96 hours before the exam"}
summary: For an adult, the Attorney General's billing instructions list the exam procedures as billable to the patient when the last incident was more than 96 hours before the exam.
quote: Last incident(s) greater than 96 hours**** - procedures billable to patient
pinpoint: SAFE Reimbursement Instructions, mandated examination components table (18 and over); see item 9
source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Instructions for SAFE and HIV Prophylaxis Reimbursement Form

params: {"payer":"Ohio Attorney General SAFE Program, for evidence collected after 96 hours when justified; payment not guaranteed"}
summary: The instructions say evidence should sometimes be collected more than 96 hours after the assault, for example when the patient was unconscious. The provider must explain why, and that does not guarantee the SAFE Program will pay.
quote: There are cases in which evidence should be collected beyond 96 hours. Examples include where the patient was unconscious or sedentary or where an exam may corroborate chronic injury or excessive force related to the sexual assault. Documentation must clearly justify the reasoning for the forensic collection as it relates to the sexual assault. Documentation does not guarantee payment by the SAFE Program.
pinpoint: SAFE Reimbursement Instructions, item 9 (Date/Time of Abuse/Assault)
source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Instructions for SAFE and HIV Prophylaxis Reimbursement Form

params: {"payer":"Patient or insurer (emergency contraception given at the exam)"}
summary: Emergency contraception given to an adult or adolescent at the sexual assault exam is not part of the state-paid exam and can be billed to the patient or the patient's insurer.
quote: If an adult/adolescent patient presenting in the emergency department as a victim of sexual assault is provided emergency contraception those costs are billable to the patient/insurer
source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Instructions for SAFE and HIV Prophylaxis Reimbursement Form

params: {"payer":"Ohio Attorney General SAFE Program (HIV post-exposure prophylaxis, actual amount billed up to the cap)"}
summary: The facility is paid the actual amount billed for HIV post-exposure prophylaxis, up to $2,500, as payment in full.
quote: (B) A hospital, children's advocacy center, or other emergency medical facility shall accept payment of the actual amount billed; not to exceed twenty-five hundred dollars, as payment in full for any cost incurred in administration of HIV post-exposure prophylaxis protocol in rule 109:7-1-01 of the Administrative Code.
source_title: OAC 109:7-1-02 (sexual assault examination payment amount)

summary: Total compensation for an injured victim, together with everyone else claiming for that victim's injury, is capped at $50,000.
quote: Reparations payable to a victim described in division (L)(1) of section 2743.51 of the Revised Code and to all other claimants sustaining economic loss because of injury to or the death of that victim shall not exceed fifty thousand dollars in the aggregate.
source_title: ORC 2743.60 (denial or reduction of award)

params: {"expense":"counseling","amount_cents":500000,"per":"claim","applies_to":"an immediate family member who lived with a sexual assault victim and needs counseling, not the victim"}
summary: An immediate family member living with a sexual assault victim can claim counseling on their own, capped at $5,000; for this kind of claimant counseling is the only payable expense.
quote: Reparations payable to a victim described in division (L)(2) of section 2743.51 of the Revised Code shall not exceed five thousand dollars.
source_title: ORC 2743.60 (denial or reduction of award)
set_aside_reason: applies_to "an immediate family member who lived with a sexual assault victim and needs counseling, not the victim"

summary: Cleanup of the crime scene and repairs to damaged property for personal security (for example doors and windows) are capped at $750 per claim.
quote: (2) Reasonable and necessary costs of cleaning the scene and repairing, for the purpose of personal security, property damaged at the scene where the criminally injurious conduct occurred, not to exceed seven hundred fifty dollars in the aggregate per claim.
source_title: ORC 2743.51 (definitions)

summary: Replacing property that police took as evidence (such as a phone or clothing) is capped at $750 per claim.
quote: (U) "Cost of evidence replacement" means costs for replacement of property confiscated for evidentiary purposes related to the criminally injurious conduct, not to exceed seven hundred fifty dollars in the aggregate per claim.
source_title: ORC 2743.51 (definitions)

params: {"expense":"legal","amount_cents":100000,"per":"claim","item":"lawyer's fees for an order that separates you from the offender"}
summary: Attorney's fees for successfully getting a restraining order, custody order, or other order that physically separates the victim from the offender are covered up to $1,000, at no more than $100 an hour.
quote: (b) Attorney's fees not exceeding one thousand dollars, at a rate not exceeding one hundred dollars per hour, incurred to successfully obtain a restraining order, custody order, or other order to physically separate a victim from an offender.
source_title: ORC 2743.51 (definitions)

params: {"expense":"other","amount_cents":1500000,"per":"claim","applies_to":"a family member with trauma so severe it keeps them from normal daily activities, such as an immediate family member who cares for a dependent sexual assault victim, not the victim"}
summary: A family member with trauma so severe it keeps them from normal daily activities, including an immediate family member who is the caretaker of a dependent sexual assault victim, can claim only work loss and counseling, capped at $15,000.
quote: Reparations payable to a victim described in division (L)(3) of section 2743.51 of the Revised Code shall not exceed fifteen thousand dollars.
source_title: ORC 2743.60 (denial or reduction of award)
set_aside_reason: applies_to "a family member with trauma so severe it keeps them from normal daily activities, such as an immediate family member who cares for a dependent sexual assault victim, not the victim"

summary: Medical care, rehabilitation, and other remedial treatment are allowable expenses for an injured victim.
quote: "allowable expense" means reasonable charges incurred for reasonably needed products, services, and accommodations, including those for medical care, rehabilitation, rehabilitative occupational training, and other remedial treatment and care
source_title: ORC 2743.51 (definitions)

params: {"expense":"dental","scope":"replacing dentures, hearing aids, eyeglasses, and mobility aids"}
summary: Replacement of dentures, retainers, and other dental appliances is an allowable expense, along with hearing aids, mobility aids, and eyeglasses.
quote: including replacement costs for hearing aids; dentures, retainers, and other dental appliances; canes, walkers, and other mobility tools; and eyeglasses and other corrective lenses
source_title: ORC 2743.51 (definitions)

summary: The application lets the victim request counseling expenses for themselves.
quote: Counseling expenses for victim
pinpoint: Application for Crime Victim Compensation, Section 4
source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (with program overview)

summary: Lost income from work the victim could not do because of the injury is covered as work loss.
quote: (G) "Work loss" means loss of income from work that the injured person would have performed if the person had not been injured
source_title: ORC 2743.51 (definitions)

params: {"expense":"clothing_bedding","scope":"replacing clothing removed to check for or treat injuries"}
summary: Clothing removed from the victim so injuries could be assessed or treated can be replaced.
quote: (1) The replacement cost for items of clothing removed from a victim in order to make an assessment of possible physical harm or to treat physical harm;
source_title: ORC 2743.51 (definitions)

params: {"expense":"childcare","scope":"paying someone for child care, housecleaning, or errands the victim would normally do"}
summary: Replacement services, meaning paying someone to do what the victim would normally do such as child care, housecleaning, or errands, can be claimed.
quote: Replacement services (paying someone to do what the victim would normally do such as housecleaning, child care, errands, etc.)
pinpoint: Application for Crime Victim Compensation, Section 4; see ORC 2743.51(H)
source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (with program overview)

params: {"item":"stolen, damaged, or lost property; pain and suffering"}
summary: The program does not pay for stolen, damaged, or lost property (for example a broken or stolen phone), or for pain and suffering. Property police kept as evidence is handled separately as evidence replacement.
quote: Yes. Compensation cannot be paid for pain and suffering, stolen, damaged, or lost property.
pinpoint: Application for Crime Victim Compensation, program overview (Are there limits on compensation?)
source_title: Ohio Attorney General, Application for Crime Victim Compensation (with program overview)

summary: Pain, suffering, and other noneconomic harm are not compensable economic loss.
quote: Noneconomic detriment is not economic loss
source_title: ORC 2743.51 (definitions)

summary: Apply within three years of the crime. Other parts of the law allow more time in some cases.
quote: All applications for an award of reparations may be filed at any time within three years after the occurrence of the criminally injurious conduct, except as provided in divisions (A)(2)(b) to (d) of section 2743.60 of the Revised Code.
source_title: ORC 2743.56 (application for award)

summary: If the claimant was under twenty-one when the crime happened, the claim is not time-barred until after the claimant's twenty-fourth birthday.

summary: The crime must have been reported to a law enforcement officer or agency at some point. Without a report, no award can be made.

summary: The award is reduced by anything recovered from other sources, such as insurance, so the program pays after those sources.

summary: If a claimant unreasonably fails to file a timely claim with insurance or another source that would have paid, the award can be reduced or denied to that extent.
quote: If a claimant unreasonably fails to present a claim timely to a source of benefits or advantages that would have been a collateral source and that would have reimbursed the claimant for all or a portion of a particular expense, the attorney general or the court of claims may reduce an award of reparations or deny a claim for an award of reparations to the extent that it is reasonable to do so.
source_title: ORC 2743.60 (denial or reduction of award)

summary: An award can be reduced or denied for contributory misconduct, which the statute defines narrowly as unlawful or intentionally tortious conduct at the time of the crime that caused or threatened serious harm and provoked the crime.
quote: The attorney general or the court of claims shall reduce an award of reparations or deny a claim for an award of reparations to the extent it is determined to be reasonable because of the contributory misconduct of the claimant or the victim.
source_title: ORC 2743.60 (denial or reduction of award)

summary: An award can be denied or reduced if the victim or claimant did not fully cooperate with law enforcement.
quote: The attorney general or the court of claims, upon a finding that the claimant or victim has not fully cooperated with appropriate law enforcement agencies, may deny a claim or reconsider and reduce an award of reparations.
source_title: ORC 2743.60 (denial or reduction of award)

summary: If a final award looks likely and waiting would cause undue hardship, the Attorney General can make an emergency award of up to $2,000, which is taken out of the final award.

The Board may, after approval of an initial award of Twenty-five Thousand Dollars ($25,000.00), grant an additional sum not to exceed Twenty-five Thousand Dollars ($25,000.00), specifically for loss of wages for the victim or loss of support for dependents of a deceased victim, provided there is verifiable economic loss after deducting payments from other sources.

source_title: 21 O.S. 142.13 Payment of award and limits

summary: Inpatient mental health treatment is reviewed case by case and may be paid up to $20,000.

source_title: 21 O.S. 142.13 Payment of award and limits

source_title: 21 O.S. 142.13 Payment of award and limits

summary: All records and information given to the Crime Victims Compensation Board to process a claim are confidential and generally cannot be obtained through discovery in a civil or criminal case, with narrow exceptions for an appeal of a Board decision or a strict showing to a court.

summary: A provider that bills the SAVE Fund for a sexual assault medical assessment may not bill the survivor for it, unless the Fund lacks money or declines to pay. The statute does not address billing the survivor's insurance; the SAVE Fund rule does, and it bars billing insurance too.
quote: A provider who submits a bill under this subsection may not bill the victim for the medical assessment except to the extent that the department is unable to pay the bill due to lack of funds or declines to pay the bill.
source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

params: {"insurance_billing":"prohibited","condition":"if Oregon's SAVE Fund pays for it"}
summary: A provider that bills the SAVE Fund may not bill the survivor or the survivor's insurance for the exam, evidence collection, or other services given with the exam (exceptions: the Fund lacks money or declines to pay for reasons other than a late or incomplete bill).
quote: An eligible medical services provider (including subcontractor or other designee) who submits a bill to the Fund under these rules may not bill the victim or the victim's insurance carrier for a medical examination, collection of forensic evidence using the Oregon State Police SAFE Kit, or other services provided in conjunction with the sexual assault exam
source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 84 (SAVE Fund)

params: {"payer":"Oregon Department of Justice, Sexual Assault Victims' Emergency Medical Response (SAVE) Fund"}
summary: The Oregon Department of Justice pays for a sexual assault medical assessment through the SAVE Fund, subject to available funds and the time frame set by rule.
quote: Subject to the availability of funds from gifts, grants and donations in the Sexual Assault Victims' Emergency Medical Response Fund, the Department of Justice shall pay the costs of a medical assessment obtained by a victim if the victim obtains the medical assessment within the time frame established in rules adopted by the department.
source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

summary: The SAVE Fund law counts you as a victim only if the sexual assault happened in Oregon.
quote: “Victim” means a person who has experienced an incident of sexual assault as defined in ORS 181A.323 that occurred in this state.
source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

summary: You can get the exam and fill out the SAVE Fund form whether or not you report the assault to police.
quote: A victim may obtain a medical assessment and complete and submit a form under this section regardless of whether the victim reports the sexual assault to a law enforcement agency.
source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

summary: The SAVE Fund also covers 5 counseling sessions, which must be used within 18 months of the exam.
quote: Five (5) counseling sessions; counseling sessions expire 18 months from the date of the sexual assault exam.
source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 84 (SAVE Fund)

summary: The most compensation that can be awarded in total is $47,000.
quote: The maximum amount of compensation that may be awarded, in aggregate, to the victim and the survivors and dependents of a deceased victim is $47,000.
source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

summary: Medical and hospital expenses, including counseling and medications, are covered up to $20,000 combined.
quote: The victim's reasonable medical and hospital expenses, including counseling expenses and the cost of any medications, up to a maximum amount of $20,000
source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

summary: The victim's counseling counts toward the same $20,000 limit as medical and hospital expenses.
quote: The victim's reasonable medical and hospital expenses, including counseling expenses and the cost of any medications, up to a maximum amount of $20,000
source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

summary: An applicant who does not meet the eligibility requirements (for example, the reporting requirement) may still get a limited counseling award of up to $5,000.
quote: If the applicant files an application for a compensable crime and does not meet the eligibility requirements set forth in ORS 147.015, the Department may grant a limited counseling award of up to $5,000.00.
source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 76 (Crime Victims' Compensation)

summary: On an approved claim, CVC pays for 30 counseling sessions and needs a treatment plan from the provider for more.
quote: If CVC approves the claim, we can pay for 30 counseling sessions. We require a treatment plan from the provider for any further sessions.
pinpoint: CVC FAQ, How much do compensation benefits cover?
source_title: Oregon DOJ: Crime Victims' Compensation FAQ

summary: Lost earnings are paid at up to $600 per week.
quote: Loss of the victim's earnings, at a maximum rate of $600 per week, up to a maximum amount of $20,000
source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

summary: Lost earnings are capped at $20,000 in total.
quote: Loss of the victim's earnings, at a maximum rate of $600 per week, up to a maximum amount of $20,000
source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

summary: Lost earnings are figured at 75% of the victim's documented gross earnings on the date of the crime.
quote: Compensation for lost earnings under ORS 147.035(2)(b) shall be computed on the basis of 75% of the victim's documented gross earnings on the date of the compensable crime.
source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 76 (Crime Victims' Compensation)

summary: Missing more than 10 working days requires confirmation from a health provider, or a licensed therapist for an emotional injury.
quote: Lost earnings compensation for periods of disability in excess of 10 working days may be paid only if the period of disability is confirmed by a health provider , or a licensed therapist when the victim has missed work due to an emotional injury.
source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 76 (Crime Victims' Compensation)

summary: A parent or guardian who misses work to care for a minor victim can get up to $5,000 in lost earnings.
quote: Loss of earnings for the parent or guardian are compensable up to a maximum of $5,000.00 under the child victim's claim under ORS 147.035 (2)(f).
source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 76 (Crime Victims' Compensation)

summary: Travel for the victim's covered medical care or counseling is paid up to $3,000, only when the care is more than 30 miles from home and adequate care is not available closer.
quote: Expenses related to transportation for the victim's medical care or counseling, at a rate determined by the Department of Justice, up to a maximum amount of $3,000, when: (A) The medical care or counseling is compensable under this section; (B) The medical care or counseling is provided more than 30 miles away from the victim's residence; and (C) Adequate medical care or counseling is not available in closer proximity to the victim's residence.
source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

params: {"scope":"mileage to medical and mental health treatment"}
summary: Mileage to medical and mental health treatment is reimbursed at 50 cents per mile, up to $3,000.
quote: Reimbursement of mileage (50¢ per mile) for travel to medical and mental health treatment, up to $3,000.
pinpoint: CVC brochure (2024), What Does CVC Pay For?
source_title: Oregon DOJ: Crime Victims' Compensation brochure (2024)

summary: Rehabilitation expenses, such as physical therapy, are covered up to $4,000.
quote: The victim's rehabilitation expenses, up to a maximum amount of $4,000
source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

summary: Crime scene cleaning is covered up to $2,500.
quote: Reasonable cleaning expenses, up to a maximum of $2,500
source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

summary: Damaged eyeglasses, hearing aids, dentures and other medically necessary devices can be replaced if mentioned in the police report or medical chart notes.
quote: Replacement of damaged eyeglasses, hearing aids, dentures and other medically necessary devices and expenses (must be mentioned in the police report or medical chart notes)
pinpoint: Compensation for Victims of Crime page, benefits list
source_title: Oregon DOJ: Compensation for Victims of Crime

summary: Crime-related dental work is covered; without insurance, CVC must first approve a treatment plan from a licensed dental provider.
quote: If you do not have insurance, CVC must review and approve a treatment plan provided by a licensed dental provider. All treatment needs to be directly related to the crime.
source_title: Oregon DOJ: Crime Victims' Compensation FAQ

summary: Compensation is not paid for property damage or for noneconomic damages.
quote: Compensation may not be awarded under ORS 147.005 to 147.367 for property damage or noneconomic damages as defined in ORS 31.705.
source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

summary: CVC cannot pay for lost items or property damage.
quote: The CVC Program cannot pay for lost items or property damage.
source_title: Oregon DOJ: Crime Victims' Compensation brochure (2024)

summary: CVC does not pay relocation costs.
quote: CVC can not reimburse damages for property crimes, or pay for relocation costs.
pinpoint: Compensation for Victims of Crime page
source_title: Oregon DOJ: Compensation for Victims of Crime

summary: The SAVE Fund does not pay for DNA testing, prescriptions filled off-site, follow-up services, anesthesia, or transportation; the provider may bill these to the survivor or insurance, and CVC may cover them on an accepted claim.
quote: Examples of services not covered by the Fund include, but are not limited to: DNA testing; prescriptions filled off-site of the location of a medical examination; follow-up services; anesthesia services; and transportation.
source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 84 (SAVE Fund)

params: {"years":1,"from":"crime","extension":"or later if the department gives you more time for good cause"}
summary: The application must be filed within one year of the injury, or later if the department allows an extension for good cause.
quote: Within one year of the date of the injury to the victim; or (B) Within such further extension of time as the department, for good cause shown, allows.
source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

params: {"years":1,"from":"crime","extension":"good cause includes lack of knowledge of the program, police failure to inform, or emotional or physical trauma"}
summary: Good cause for filing after one year includes not knowing about the program, police not giving the required information, or trauma that got in the way of filing on time.
quote: "Good cause" for failure to file an application for compensation within one year of the date of the crime as required by ORS 147.015(1)(e) includes but is not limited to the victim's lack of knowledge of the Crime Victims' Compensation Program, failure of a law enforcement official to provide information to the victim as required by ORS 147.365(1), or emotional or physical trauma sustained by the victim that was a barrier to timely filing the application for compensation.
source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 76 (Crime Victims' Compensation)

summary: The crime must be reported to law enforcement, unless the department finds the applicant acted reasonably in not reporting. No fixed number of days is set.
quote: The appropriate law enforcement officials were notified of the perpetration of the crime allegedly causing the death or injury to the victim, unless the Department of Justice finds that, notwithstanding the failure of notification, the applicant acted reasonably under the circumstances
source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

summary: The report rule can also be met in other ways. A sexual assault medical assessment or any other forensic exam counts. So does a health, tribal health, student health, or community mental health provider certifying that the victim reported the crime to them. So does other documentation that counts as notice under the department's rules.
quote: (E) A medical assessment, as defined in ORS 147.395, for sexual assault, or any other forensic exam or medical assessment; (b) A health provider, tribal health provider, student health provider or community mental health provider certifies that the victim reported the crime to the provider; or (c) The victim provides to the department documentation that qualifies as law enforcement notification under the rules of the department.
source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

summary: Getting a sexual abuse restraining order (or a stalking, abuse prevention or no contact order) because of the crime also meets the reporting requirement.
quote: A sexual abuse restraining order under ORS 163.760 to 163.777
source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

summary: Survivors can meet the reporting requirement by reporting to police, telling a medical or mental health provider, getting a protective order, or getting a forensic exam.
quote: You may report your crime in one of the following ways: • Report to law enforcement • Report to a medical or mental health provider • Obtain a protective order • Obtain a forensic medical exam due to sexual assault or strangulation
source_title: Oregon DOJ: Crime Victims' Compensation brochure (2024)

summary: The report (or alternative) must happen before the department receives the application.
quote: Notification of the perpetration of the crime as required by ORS 147.015 must have been done prior to the application being received by the Department in order for a person to be eligible for an award of compensation.
source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 76 (Crime Victims' Compensation)

summary: The award is reduced by benefits from workers' compensation, government funds, or any other source that the victim received or is entitled to because of the injury.
quote: shall deduct the amount of benefits, payments or awards that are payable under the Workers' Compensation Law, from local governmental, state or federal funds or from any source, and that the victim or survivors or dependents of the victim have received or to which the victim or survivors or dependents of the victim are entitled as a result of the death or injury of the victim
source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

summary: Health insurance (including OHP), auto, workers' comp, disability, homeowner's, Paid Leave Oregon, unemployment, restitution and settlements must be used first; Indian Health Services is not a prior resource.
quote: A prior resource may include but is not limited to: private or public health insurance, automobile insurance, workers' compensation, disability insurance, homeowner's insurance, Paid Leave Oregon or equivalent plan, unemployment benefits, restitution, civil settlements, and tribal per capita payments. Indian Health Services insurance is not considered a prior resource.
source_title: OAR Chapter 137 Division 76 (Crime Victims' Compensation)

summary: After insurance pays, CVC can cover copays, deductibles, and crime-related treatment insurance does not cover.
quote: CVC will pay for copays, deductibles, and crime-related treatment that insurance does not cover within the scope of this program.
source_title: Oregon DOJ: Crime Victims' Compensation brochure (2024)

summary: Eligibility depends on the department finding the victim acted reasonably given the victim's specific situation. Shown for information only.
quote: The department determines that the victim acted reasonably with respect to the incident causing the death or injury to the victim, taking into account the specific situation of the victim and what a reasonable action would be for a person in the victim's circumstances
source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

summary: The department may make an emergency award of up to $1,000 before a final decision when an award is likely and waiting would cause undue hardship.
quote: The amount of such emergency award shall not exceed $1,000.
source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

summary: Sexual assault is an eligible crime.
quote: Eligible crimes include domestic violence, sexual assault, child abuse, assault, homicide, hate/bias crimes, and other crimes resulting in physical or psychological injury.
source_title: Oregon DOJ: Crime Victims' Compensation brochure (2024)

summary: Injury includes mental or emotional harm and pregnancy, not only physical harm.
quote: "Injury" means abuse of a corpse, actual bodily harm, mental or emotional harm and, with respect to a victim, includes pregnancy and mental or nervous shock.
source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

summary: Oregon DOJ's Address Confidentiality Program is a free mail forwarding service that gives survivors of sexual assault, domestic violence, stalking, human trafficking, and bias crimes a substitute address to use instead of their real one.

summary: Information an applicant gives the DOJ is open to the public by default, but the department may keep it confidential when the crime is rape, sodomy, sexual abuse, trafficking, or domestic violence and the victim's interests require it. The statute does not make the whole claim file confidential.

All information submitted to the Department of Justice by an applicant and
all hearings of the Workers’ Compensation Board under ORS 147.005 to 147.367
shall be open to the public unless the department or board determines that the
information shall be kept confidential or that a closed hearing shall be held
because: (a) The alleged
assailant has not been brought to trial and disclosure of the information or a
public hearing would adversely affect either the apprehension or the trial of
the alleged assailant; (b) The offense
allegedly perpetrated against the victim is rape, sodomy, sexual abuse,
trafficking in persons or a crime involving domestic violence as defined in ORS
135.230, and the interests of the victim or of the victim’s dependents require
that the information be kept confidential or that the public be excluded from
the hearing;
source_title: ORS Chapter 147 (Crime Victims; compensation and SAVE Fund)

summary: The cost of a forensic rape exam and the medications prescribed to the survivor may not be charged to the survivor.

summary: The hospital or provider bills the state compensation program (Office of Victims' Services) for the exam when insurance does not cover it, or when the survivor asks that their insurance not be billed.
quote: A hospital or other licensed health care provider may submit a claim for reimbursement for the cost of a forensic rape examination if the cost is not covered by insurance or if the victim requests that the insurance carrier not be billed.
source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

summary: The survivor does not have to report to police or talk to law enforcement for the program to pay for the exam.

summary: For the program to pay for the exam, the hospital must notify the local police where the assault happened within 12 hours of collecting the evidence.
quote: In order for payments to be considered, hospitals or licensed health care providers requesting reimbursement of costs associated with a forensic rape examination are required to notify the local law enforcement agency where the reported sexual assault occurred within 12 hours of collection of the sexual assault evidence as per the Sexual Assault Testing and Evidence Collection Act (Act 165 of 2006).
pinpoint: VCAP Protocol and Billing Procedures for FREs, introduction
source_title: VCAP Protocol and Billing Procedures for Forensic Rape Examinations (2024)

summary: Adults 18 or older can choose an anonymous report when evidence is collected, if they are worried about the kit going to police. A minor's exam cannot be done anonymously.
quote: Adult victims (age 18 or older) have the option of anonymous reporting and gathering of evidence and may consider this option if they have concerns about the kit being provided to police. An exam cannot be completed anonymously for a minor.
source_title: VCAP Forensic Rape Examination Frequently Asked Questions (September 2024)

summary: If the program pays the maximum and a balance remains, the provider still may not bill the survivor; the program payment is payment in full.

summary: The provider must file the exam claim within one year of the crime or its discovery; if the provider misses that deadline, the survivor still cannot be billed.
quote: The claim must be filed by a hospital or other licensed health care provider, within one year of the date of the crime or discovery of the crime. Failure to file within the prescribed time frame will result in non-payment of the claim and the victim cannot be billed for those costs.
pinpoint: VCAP Protocol and Billing Procedures for FREs, A.4
source_title: VCAP Protocol and Billing Procedures for Forensic Rape Examinations (2024)

summary: A survivor who was billed by mistake and paid for the forensic rape exam or related medications can be reimbursed, up to $1,000.
quote: OVS will reimburse a direct victim who is erroneously billed and subsequently pays the cost of the forensic rape examination or medications directly related to the sexual offense. The reimbursement will be subject to the $1,000 monetary limitation.
