summary: Payment for a forensic rape exam and related medications is capped at $1,000, and this sits outside the $35,000 total award cap.
quote: In no case shall the total amount of an award exceed $35,000 except for payment of the following: (i) counseling, the maximum amount of which shall be in accordance with paragraph (4.1); (ii) forensic rape examination and medications directly related to the sexual assault or rape, the amount of which shall not exceed $1,000
source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

params: {"payer":"Survivor or insurance for care beyond the forensic rape exam (for example x-rays or other treatment); a standard VCAP claim can be filed for it"}
summary: The no-bill rule covers only the forensic rape exam costs and related medications. Providers must tell the survivor they may be billed for other care, such as x-rays or other medical treatment, which can be submitted on a standard VCAP claim.
quote: They must inform the victim that they may be billed for services in instances where they have additional expenses beyond the forensic rape examination costs, such as x-rays or other medical treatment not associated with a forensic rape examination.
pinpoint: VCAP Protocol and Billing Procedures for FREs, introduction
source_title: VCAP Protocol and Billing Procedures for Forensic Rape Examinations (2024)

params: {"amount_cents":3500000,"exception":"not counting some costs that are paid on top"}
summary: The total award is capped at $35,000, except that counseling, forensic rape exam costs, and crime scene cleanup are paid on top of that cap.
quote: In no case shall the total amount of an award exceed $35,000 except for payment of the following
source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

summary: Counseling for an adult direct victim is capped at $5,000, and a minor direct victim at $10,000; counseling is paid on top of the total award cap.
quote: The amount of an award under paragraph (4)(i) shall not exceed $5,000 where the direct victim is an adult and shall not exceed $10,000 where the direct victim is a minor.
source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

summary: Counseling for a direct victim who was a minor is capped at $10,000.
quote: The amount of an award under paragraph (4)(i) shall not exceed $5,000 where the direct victim is an adult and shall not exceed $10,000 where the direct victim is a minor.
source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

summary: The program pays for counseling, and for the transportation to get to counseling, when done by or under a psychiatrist, psychologist, licensed professional counselor, or licensed social worker.
quote: An award for counseling performed by or under the supervision of a psychiatrist, psychologist, licensed professional counselor or licensed social worker and reimbursement of associated transportation costs
source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

summary: A direct victim of sexual abuse in Pennsylvania can get counseling paid through a separate sexual assault counseling claim, paid directly to the provider.
quote: The Office of Victims' Services shall provide funding for counseling services related to sexual abuse for an individual who is a direct victim of sexual abuse. Payment shall be made directly to the health care provider that provides the services from funding provided for the implementation of this section.
source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

summary: Sexual assault counseling claims are capped at $5,000 if the survivor was 18 or older at the time of the abuse, and $10,000 if under 18.
quote: (1) Five thousand dollars if the individual was, at the time of the abuse, 18 years of age or older. (2) Ten thousand dollars if the individual was, at the time of the abuse, under 18 years of age.
source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

summary: Lost earnings are capped at $15,000 in total, and this counts toward the overall award cap.
quote: Except as set forth in subparagraph (iii), the aggregate award for the loss shall not exceed $15,000.
source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

summary: Lost earnings caused by the injury are covered, up to the state average weekly wage for each week, if not otherwise reimbursed.
quote: OVS may make an award within the monetary limitations of the act to compensate a direct victim, intervenor or claimant for loss of earnings attributable to the injury not to exceed the average weekly wage if the claimant was not otherwise reimbursed for the loss.
source_title: 37 Pa. Code Chapter 411: Crime Victims Compensation

summary: Relocation for safety is capped at $1,000 per household for each direct victim.
quote: This reimbursement will not exceed $1,000 per household for each direct victim for the following:
source_title: 37 Pa. Code Chapter 411: Crime Victims Compensation

summary: Temporary or permanent relocation is covered when there is an immediate need to protect the safety and health of the victim and household, verified by a medical provider, human services provider, or law enforcement.
quote: expenses resulting from the temporary or permanent relocation of a direct victim and individuals residing in the household of the direct victim due to the incident forming the basis of the victim's claim when there is an immediate need to protect the safety and health of the victim and individuals residing in the household, as verified by a medical provider, human services provider or law enforcement
source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 1: Definitions (18 P.S. 11.103)

summary: The move must happen within 120 days of the crime, or within 120 days of a new threat or sign of danger.
quote: Relocation must occur within 120 days from the date of crime, or 120 days from the date the victim is threatened by any change of circumstance or indicator of danger.
source_title: VCAP flyer: Relocation Expenses (11/2023)

summary: Lodging while relocating for safety is reimbursed up to $75 per day, inside the $1,000 relocation limit.
quote: This reimbursement will not exceed $1,000 per household for each direct victim for the following: (1)  Relocation expenses to be reimbursed are as follows: (i)   Lodging to a daily maximum of $75.
source_title: 37 Pa. Code Chapter 411: Crime Victims Compensation

summary: Travel to medical care or counseling, and to criminal justice or protection from abuse proceedings, is reimbursed.
quote: OVS will reimburse expenses associated with travel necessary and reasonable as determined by OVS to obtain medical care or counseling, attend or participate in criminal justice or protection from abuse proceedings, and other circumstances when good cause is shown by the claimant.
source_title: 37 Pa. Code Chapter 411: Crime Victims Compensation

summary: Car rental for crime-related travel (medical care, counseling, court) is reimbursed up to $30 per day.
quote: Car rental, up to $30 a day.
source_title: PCCD Manual for Compensation Assistance (VCAP Manual 2025)

summary: Meals are reimbursed up to $28 per day ($6 breakfast, $6 lunch, $16 dinner), but only when travel to a provider is 50 miles or more one way.
quote:
Additionally, if travel to a provider is 50 miles or more (one way) from the eligible person’s
home, the following is eligible for reimbursement:
• Meals. Up to $28 a day, with no more than $6 for breakfast, $6 for lunch and $16 for
dinner.
source_title: PCCD Manual for Compensation Assistance (VCAP Manual 2025)

summary: Unreimbursed medical care and treatment caused by the crime are covered.
quote: expenses for unreimbursed and unreimbursable expenses or indebtedness incurred for medical care, nonmedical remedial care and treatment as approved by the Office of Victims' Services or other services
source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 1: Definitions (18 P.S. 11.103)

summary: Once the program accepts a claim, the hospital or provider must take the program's payment as payment in full and may not collect more from the survivor.
quote: If the Office of Victims' Services accepts a claim, the hospital or other licensed health care provider shall accept such payment as payment in full and may not attempt to collect from the victim any amount exceeding the amount of reimbursement made by the Office of Victims' Services.
source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

params: {"expense":"property_replacement","amount_cents":100000,"per":"claim","item":"replacing medical devices, eyeglasses, and prescription medicine"}
summary: Replacing eyeglasses, hearing aids, dental devices, prescription medications and similar health items stolen or damaged in the crime is capped at $1,000, with eyeglass frames limited to $200. This is not a cap on ordinary medical bills.
quote: OVS will reimburse a claimant for costs for the replacement of each prosthetic device, wheelchair, cane, walker, hearing aid, eyeglasses or other corrective lenses, dental device or prescription medications. Reimbursement will not exceed $1,000 and will be subject to the following limitations: (1)  Two hundred dollars for eyeglass frames.
source_title: 37 Pa. Code Chapter 411: Crime Victims Compensation

params: {"expense":"childcare","scope":"services needed because of the crime, such as child care, cleaning, or laundry"}
summary: Services needed because of the crime, such as child care, cleaning, laundry, and meal preparation, can be reimbursed.
quote: The cost of obtaining services needed as a result of the crime such as laundering, cleaning, child care, administration of medication, food shopping and meal preparation.
source_title: 37 Pa. Code Chapter 411: Crime Victims Compensation

summary: A helper who is not a family member is paid at most $8 an hour. A family member who does the work is paid their own lost earnings, up to the average weekly wage.
quote: The cost of obtaining services needed as a result of the crime such as laundering, cleaning, child care, administration of medication, food shopping and meal preparation. (i) Members of the family of the direct victim or intervenor engaged to perform the services will be paid their net loss of earnings not to exceed the average weekly wage and if not otherwise reimbursed for the loss of earnings. (ii) Individuals engaged to perform services who are not family members will be paid a maximum hourly rate of $8.
source_title: 37 Pa. Code Chapter 411: Crime Victims Compensation

summary: Cleaning a crime scene at a private residence or privately owned vehicle is capped at $500, paid on top of the total award cap.
quote: reasonable and necessary costs of cleaning the crime scene of a private residence or privately owned motor vehicle, the amount of which shall not exceed $500.
source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

summary: Property damage and pain and suffering are not covered.
quote: Except as otherwise provided, the term does not include property damage or pain and suffering.
source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 1: Definitions (18 P.S. 11.103)

params: {"item":"property loss or damage (only certain medical equipment and supplies and, case by case, official documents are excepted; phones are not named)"}
summary: Lost or damaged property is not paid, except certain medical equipment and supplies and, case by case, certain official documents such as a driver's license or passport.
quote: Property - A claim cannot be paid for property loss or damage (except certain medical equipment and supplies; or certain official documents, i.e., driver's license, passport, etc. on case by case basis).
pinpoint: VCAP Manual 2025, Miscellaneous Eligibility Information (p. 10 to 11)
source_title: PCCD Manual for Compensation Assistance (VCAP Manual 2025)

params: {"years":5,"from":"discovery","extension":"or later in some cases, such as sexual abuse counseling claims, some survivors who were children, or when the program finds good cause"}
summary: Under the current law, a claim must be filed within five years after the crime is discovered.
quote: a claim must be filed not later than five years after the discovery of the occurrence of the crime upon which the claim is based
source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

summary: The program's page says the 5-year limit is for crimes on or after 9/8/2022. For an older crime, it asks you to contact the program to find out the filing rules.
quote: For crimes occurring on or after 9/8/2022, the claim must be filed within 5 years of the crime. For crimes occurring prior to 9/8/2022, please contact the Program to determine filing requirements.
pinpoint: PA.gov Apply for Victims' Compensation page, Who is eligible?
source_title: PA.gov: Apply for Victims' Compensation (VCAP)

summary: Claims for counseling related to sexual abuse are an exception to the filing deadline.
quote: (2) Exceptions shall be as follows: (i) ((i) deleted by amendment). (i.1) Claims for counseling services related to sexual abuse under section 701.1.
source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

summary: If the survivor was under 18 and the abuser was a parent, a caretaker, someone living in the same home, or a parent's partner, the deadline does not start until the survivor turns 21. It then runs until the later of the criminal time limit for the crime or the usual deadline.
quote: If a direct victim is under 18 years of age at the time of the occurrence of the crime and the alleged offender is the direct victim's parent or a person responsible for the direct victim's welfare, an individual residing in the same home as the direct victim or a paramour of the direct victim's parent, all of the following shall apply: (A) The limitation period under this subsection is tolled until the direct victim reaches 21 years of age. (B) The limitation period shall run until the later of: (I) the end of the limitation period for the offense as set forth in 42 Pa.C.S. Ch. 55 Subch. C (relating to criminal proceedings); or (II) the end of the limitation period under paragraph (1).
source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

summary: If the survivor was under 18 and the claim is only for counseling, the deadline does not start until the survivor turns 21.
quote: (ii.1) If a direct victim is under 18 years of age at the time of the occurrence of the crime and the direct victim is seeking reimbursement for counseling services only, all of the following shall apply: (A) The limitation period under this subsection is tolled until the direct victim reaches 21 years of age.
source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

summary: The Office of Victims' Services may accept a late claim for good cause, such as when the victim was incapacitated or a minor, feared retaliation, or the crime was not readily apparent.
quote: (iii.1) The Office of Victims' Services may find good cause to accept a claim beyond the limitation period under paragraph (1) if one of the following circumstances existed at the time of the occurrence of the crime or the discovery of the occurrence of the crime: (A) The direct victim, intervenor or claimant was mentally or physically incapacitated. (B) The victim was a minor. (C) There was a fear of retaliation. (D) The occurrence of the crime was not readily apparent. (E) Other circumstances when good cause is shown by the claimant.
source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

summary: Under the current law, the crime must have been promptly reported to the proper authorities. The law sets no fixed number of hours.
quote: The crime was promptly reported to the proper authorities.
source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

summary: The program's manual says the filing, reporting, and minimum loss rules are different for a crime before 9/8/2022, and asks you to contact the program about them.
quote: For eligibility requirements for crime occurring prior to 9/8/2022, please contact the program as there are different filing requirement, reporting requirement, and minimum loss requirements.
pinpoint: VCAP Manual for Compensation Assistance, Eligibility
source_title: PCCD Manual for Compensation Assistance (VCAP Manual 2025)

summary: Starting a court case for a sexual violence or intimidation protection order can meet the reporting requirement without a police report.
quote: may satisfy the eligibility requirement under subsection (a)(3) for reporting a crime to the proper authorities by commencing an action brought in accordance with 42 Pa.C.S. Ch. 62A (relating to protection of victims of sexual violence or intimidation)
source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

params: {"required":false,"scope":"a protection order case that is later withdrawn"}
summary: If you start a protection order case to meet the report rule and then drop it, you cannot get an award unless the program finds you had good reason to drop it.
quote: An award may not be made if the record shows that the petition was withdrawn, except if the Office of Victims' Services finds the withdrawal to have been justified, consistent with regulations of the Office of Victims' Services.
source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

params: {"required":true,"alternatives":["forensic_exam"],"exam_condition":"for a crime on or after September 8, 2022"}
summary: For crimes on or after 9/8/2022, having a forensic rape exam counts as reporting to the proper authorities, so a survivor who had the exam can file a standard claim without reporting the crime to police.
quote: Effective for crimes occurring on or after 9/8/2022, a forensic rape exam is considered acceptable for reporting to proper authorities. This change allows victims who have the FRE completed to be eligible for a standard claim without having to report the crime to law enforcement.
pinpoint: VCAP Protocol and Billing Procedures for FREs, introduction
source_title: VCAP Protocol and Billing Procedures for Forensic Rape Examinations (2024)

summary: A survivor of sexual abuse in Pennsylvania who did not or does not want to report can still file a counseling-only claim.
quote: A direct victim of sexual abuse which occurred in Pennsylvania, who did not report or does not want to report the crime to authorities, is eligible to submit a claim for counseling services related to their abuse.
pinpoint: PA.gov VCAP page, Sexual Assault Counseling Claims
source_title: PA.gov: Apply for Victims' Compensation (VCAP)

summary: For a standard claim, the survivor must also have fully cooperated with law enforcement and the program, unless the program finds there was a good reason not to.
quote: The direct victim, intervenor or claimant has fully cooperated with all law enforcement agencies and the Office of Victims' Services, unless the Office of Victims' Services finds the noncompliance to have been justified consistent with the Office of Victims' Services regulations.
source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

summary: The program may excuse not cooperating if the survivor was incapacitated, feared retaliation, was a minor, or shows other good cause.
quote: OVS may consider a failure to cooperate with law enforcement and OVS to be justified when one of the following circumstances exist: (1) The direct victim, intervenor or the claimant is mentally or physically incapacitated. (2) There is a fear of retaliation. (3) The victim is a minor. (4) Other circumstances when good cause is shown by the claimant.
source_title: 37 Pa. Code Chapter 411: Crime Victims Compensation

summary: The claimant must have at least $50 in out-of-pocket loss or lost earnings, unless the victim or claimant was 60 or older.
quote: no award shall be made on a claim unless the claimant has incurred an aggregate minimum out-of-pocket loss, loss of earnings or loss of support of $50. (b) Exception.--Subsection (a) shall not apply if the direct victim or claimant was 60 years of age or older at the time the crime occurred.
source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

summary: The award is reduced by insurance, public funds, offender payments, settlements and similar payments; the program pays last.
quote: an award made under this chapter shall be reduced by the amount of any payments received or to be received by the claimant as a result of the injury
source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

summary: In general, the program may reduce or deny an award if the victim's conduct contributed to the injury.
quote: The Office of Victims' Services may reduce the amount or deny the claim altogether in accordance with the determination.
source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

summary: If the crime is rape or sexual assault, the victim's conduct may not be considered at all.
quote: If the crime involved is rape or sexual assault, the conduct of the direct victim shall not be considered.
source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

summary: An emergency award can be no more than $5,000 per claim.
quote: The total amount of an emergency award will not exceed $5,000 per claim.
source_title: 37 Pa. Code Chapter 411: Crime Victims Compensation

summary: Sexual offenses under Chapter 31 of the Pennsylvania Crimes Code (including rape and sexual assault) are personal injury crimes covered by the program.
quote: 18 Pa.C.S. Ch. 31 (relating to sexual offenses).
source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 1: Definitions (18 P.S. 11.103)

params: {"rule":"Crime in Pennsylvania, regardless of the victim's residence; or a Pennsylvania resident injured or killed in a foreign country that has no compensation program; or an act of international terrorism. Exam claims have a wider rule (PA-RES-2)."}
summary: The crime must have occurred in Pennsylvania, or be against a Pennsylvania resident in a foreign country with no compensation program, or be international terrorism.
quote: The crime occurred in Pennsylvania, or to a Pennsylvania resident who is injured or killed in a foreign country that does not have a compensation program, or by an act of international terrorism.
pinpoint: VCAP Manual 2025, Requirements for receiving compensation, 1
source_title: PCCD Manual for Compensation Assistance (VCAP Manual 2025)

params: {"rule":"Exam claims: crime in Pennsylvania, or a Pennsylvania resident assaulted in another state who returns to Pennsylvania for the exam."}
summary: A Pennsylvania resident sexually assaulted in another state who comes back to Pennsylvania for the exam can have the exam paid by the Pennsylvania program.
quote: Any provider performing a forensic rape examination on a sexual assault victim may file a claim with VCAP if the crime occurred in Pennsylvania, OR if a Pennsylvania resident that is sexually assaulted in another state returns to Pennsylvania to have the exam done by a hospital or licensed health care provider as defined by the Crime Victims Act.
pinpoint: VCAP Protocol and Billing Procedures for FREs, A.5
source_title: VCAP Protocol and Billing Procedures for Forensic Rape Examinations (2024)

source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

summary: Include itemized counseling bills related to the crime.
quote: Provide all itemized counseling bills related to the crime.
source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

pinpoint: Claim form (July 2024), Section 7: Loss of Earnings
source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

quote: The Acknowledgement and Reimbursement Agreement and Authorization to Obtain Information must be signed before a claim can be verified and processed for payment.
pinpoint: Claim form (July 2024), Acknowledgement & Reimbursement Agreements section
source_title: VCAP Claim Form (long form, July 2024)

summary: The program says most claims are processed in 12 weeks or less, though each claim differs.
quote: Most organizations process claims in 12 weeks or less.
pinpoint: PA.gov apply page, FAQ: How long does it take the Program to make a decision?
source_title: PA.gov: Apply for Victims' Compensation (VCAP)

source_title: VCAP flyer: Claim Process (11/2023)

quote:
All reports, records or other information
obtained or produced by the Office of Victims' Services during
the processing or investigation of a claim shall be confidential
and privileged, shall not be subject to subpoena or discovery,
shall be used for no purpose other than the processing of a
claim
source_title: Crime Victims Act (1998 Act 111), Chapter 7: Compensation (18 P.S. 11.701 to 11.710)

source_title: Sexual Assault Victims Bill of Rights, Rhode Island Attorney General

pinpoint: Attorney General's Sexual Assault Victims Bill of Rights page, Your right to choose whether to report
source_title: Sexual Assault Victims Bill of Rights, Rhode Island Attorney General

summary: First or second degree sexual assault is one of the offenses the program covers.
quote: First or second degree sexual assault;
source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-25-20 (Offenses to which chapter applies)

summary: A covered injury includes physical harm, mental or nervous shock, and a pregnancy resulting from a sexual attack.
quote: “Personal injury” means actual bodily harm, mental or nervous shock, and a pregnancy resulting from sexual attack.
source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-25-17 (Definitions)

summary: The total award to a victim cannot exceed $25,000 (plus any attorney fees awarded on appeal).
quote: No compensation shall be awarded under this chapter to the victim, or in the case of death to dependent relatives or to the legal representative, in a total amount in excess of twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000)
source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-25-22 (Limitations upon awarding compensation)

summary: A claim must be filed within 3 years of the injury.
quote: Actions for compensation under this chapter shall be commenced within three (3) years after the date of the injury or death
source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-25-22 (Limitations upon awarding compensation)

summary: For a victim who was a minor, the application is due within three years after turning eighteen.
quote: If the personal injury to the minor victim or secondary victim occurred on or after September 1, 1999, then the application must be filed within three years after the date on which the minor victim or secondary victim reaches the age of eighteen.
source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

summary: If you found out about the crime more than 1 year after it happened, the time to apply starts when you found out, or should have. This applies only if the crime led to a criminal complaint, an indictment or criminal information, or another court finding of probable cause.
quote: If the Applicant did not discover the act which constitutes a crime until more than one year after the crime was committed, the filing period shall not commence until the Applicant discovered or, in exercise of reasonable diligence, should have discovered, the act which constitutes a crime, provided, however, that in such cases, the crime for which the Applicant seeks compensation must have resulted in the issuance of a criminal complaint, indictment or criminal information, or other judicial determination of probable cause that an act constituting a crime occurred
source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

summary: The office may accept a late application if the victim was of unsound mind or shows good cause.
quote: office may allow an application for compensation to be filed with the office after the expiration of the statute of limitations if the victim or secondary victim was of unsound mind or for good cause shown.
source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

summary: Not knowing the filing rules does not count as good cause for a late application.
quote: Delay resulting from the lack of knowledge of the filing requirements of R.I. Gen. Laws §§ 12-25-1, et seq. shall not constitute good cause.
source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

summary: The crime must be reported to police within 15 days, but the office may allow a claim without a police report when a sexual assault survivor had a medical forensic exam within 15 days of the crime.
quote: no compensation shall be awarded for an injury or death resulting from a crime that was not reported to the appropriate law enforcement authority within fifteen (15) days of its occurrence; provided, that the office shall have the authority to allow a claim that was not reported pursuant to this section when a victim of a sexual assault receives a medical forensic examination within fifteen (15) days of the crime
source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-25-22 (Limitations upon awarding compensation)

summary: Applying to a court for a restraining order under R.I. Gen. Laws 15-15-3 with a supporting affidavit, or applying for a criminal complaint, counts as a report to law enforcement.
quote: The reporting of a crime to a court through a citizen application for a restraining order under R.I. Gen. Laws § 15-15-3 accompanied by an affidavit in support of the application for protection, or through a citizen application for a criminal complaint, shall constitute a report to law enforcement authorities.
source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

summary: Telling a rape crisis center, private security, rescue personnel, or the compensation program does not count as a police report.
quote: Reports to private security personnel, rape crisis centers, rescue personnel, or the Crime Victim Compensation Program do not constitute reports to law enforcement authorities.
source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

summary: A late police report can be excused for good cause, such as being physically or psychologically unable to make a report, or a reasonable fear of retaliation by the offender or others.
quote: Good cause for delay shall include, but not be limited to, delay caused by physical or psychological incapacity which prevented the making of a report; or by reasonable fear of retaliation by the offender or others.
source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

params: {"required":true,"alternatives":[],"scope":"what counts as good cause for a late report"}
summary: Believing police will not investigate, or not knowing that an award depends on reporting the crime, is not good cause for a late report. The program's rule also says good cause excuses only the delay, not the reporting requirement itself.
quote: Delay resulting from a belief that law enforcement authorities will not investigate the crime, or delay resulting from lack of knowledge that an award under R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-25-1 et. seq. is contingent upon reporting the crime to law enforcement authorities, does not constitute good cause for delay. d. A finding of good cause for delay does not excuse the reporting requirement which must be satisfied as a condition of receiving compensation.
source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

summary: A crime against a minor can be reported to the Department of Children, Youth and Families instead of the police.
quote: Crimes involving minor victims may be reported to the Department of Children, Youth and Families pursuant to the reporting requirements of R.I. Gen. Laws §§ 40-11-3 and 40-11-3.1.
source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

summary: The program's rule says a victim must cooperate with reasonable requests from law enforcement in the investigation and prosecution of the crime. It says this includes reporting the crime, helping identify the suspect, and following reasonable requests for information and help.
quote: A victim must cooperate with the reasonable requests of law enforcement agencies and personnel in the investigation and prosecution of the crime. a. Victim’s obligations: Cooperation with law enforcement agencies and personnel includes reporting the crime to law enforcement authorities; assisting in identifying the suspect; and complying with all reasonable requests of law enforcement agencies and personnel for information and assistance.
source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

summary: The program pays only after insurance, government benefits, and payments from the offender.
quote: The Criminal Injuries Compensation Act shall be regarded as a fund of last resort.
source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-25-23 (Terms of the award)

summary: The office may reduce or deny an award if the victim's own behavior, including past behavior, directly or indirectly contributed to the injury, unless the victim was lawfully trying to stop a crime or catch an offender.
quote: The behavior of the victim, including past behavior, that directly or indirectly contributed to his or her injury or death, unless the injury or death resulted from the victim’s lawful attempt to prevent the commission of a crime or to apprehend an offender. The office may reduce or deny an award based on these circumstances.
source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-25-19 (Awarding compensation)

summary: Emergency awards can cover relocation, safety modifications to the home, crime scene cleanup, and burial; they are at the administrator's discretion and are deducted from the final award.
quote: The office may award emergency compensation under this chapter for the: (1) Burial expenses of a victim who dies as a direct result of a violent crime as defined in this chapter; (2) Cost of the crime scene clean up; (3) Relocation expenses; and (4) Compensation for modifications to a victim’s residence necessary to ensure safety.
source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-25-21.1 (Emergency fund for victims)

summary: Medical expenses, including psychiatric care, that no other source pays are covered.
quote: Medical expenses (including psychiatric care) for which the victim is not compensated by any other source;
source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-25-17 (Definitions)

summary: When the program pays a medical provider, the provider must accept that as full payment and cannot charge the victim more.
quote: Medical service providers shall be required to accept these awards as full payment for services rendered and shall be prohibited from assessing any additional charges against the victim or secondary victim.
source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-25-19 (Awarding compensation)

summary: Dental expenses are among the covered expense types.
quote: Medical, dental and counseling expenses
pinpoint: CVCP FAQ, "What expenses are eligible for reimbursement?"
source_title: Crime Victim Compensation Program page and FAQ, Office of the General Treasurer

summary: Mental health counseling and psychiatric care caused by the crime are covered.
quote: A victim shall be eligible for compensation for reasonable and necessary mental health counseling and psychiatric care expenses that have been actually and reasonably incurred as a direct result of the crime.
source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

summary: Individual sessions with a licensed psychiatrist are paid at up to $130 per hour.
quote: $130 per hour is reimbursed for individual services provided by a licensed psychiatrist;
source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

summary: Individual sessions with a licensed clinical psychologist are paid at up to $110 per hour.
quote: $110 per hour is reimbursed for individual services provided by a licensed clinical psychologist;
source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

summary: Individual sessions with a licensed clinical social worker, mental health nurse, marriage and family therapist, or psychiatric clinical nurse specialist are paid at up to $90 per hour.
quote: $90 per hour is reimbursed for individual services provided by a licensed clinical social worker, mental health nurse, marriage and family therapist (MFT), or clinical nurse specialist with a specialty in psychiatric mental health nursing;
source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

summary: Lost earnings that no other source replaces are covered.
quote: Loss of past earnings for which the victim is not compensated by any other source;
source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-25-17 (Definitions)

summary: Lost earnings for injuries on or after January 1, 2022 are figured at 62% of gross earnings.
quote: All net earnings for injuries occurring on or after January 1, 2022 are calculated based on 62% of the victim’s gross earnings.
source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

summary: Travel and overnight stays to get medical care or counseling or to attend court are capped at $1,000 per claim (the administrator may waive the cap for good cause).
quote: An award for reasonable and necessary travel expenses and overnight accommodation shall not exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000) per claim.
source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

summary: Temporary or permanent relocation costs of a victim can be covered.
quote: The Administrator may issue an award for expenses resulting from the temporary or permanent relocation of a victim
source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

summary: Emergency relocation is capped at $5,000. Any relocation award is deducted from the final award.
quote: Compensation awarded for emergency relocation expenses shall not exceed the sum of five thousand dollars ($5,000.00). Any award for emergency relocation expenses shall be deducted from the final award.
source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

summary: To be paid for a move, the crime must have happened in your home. If it did not, you must show the crime makes you reasonably afraid to stay there. You must also need to move right away, reasonably fear living as you did before the crime, or be unable to afford your documented housing costs right after the crime.
quote: The crime must have occurred in the victim’s primary place of residence or the Applicant must demonstrate that, as a result of the crime, he or she reasonably fears for his or her continued safety in his or her primary place of residence. (2) An Applicant must have an immediate need to relocate, a reasonable fear to continue to live within the arrangements as established prior to the crime, or, alternatively, immediately following the crime, the Applicant must be unable to afford the documented housing costs.
source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

summary: Safety modifications to the home are capped at $1,000 and cannot be paid on top of an emergency relocation award.
quote: An award for expenses associated with reasonable modifications to the victim’s residence necessary to ensure victim safety shall not exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000) and shall not be awarded in addition to an award for emergency compensation for relocation costs.
source_title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 12-25-21.1 (Emergency fund for victims)

summary: Property losses are not covered.
quote: Property losses are not compensable expenses.
source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

summary: Pain and suffering is not paid for crimes on or after September 1, 1999.
quote: any claims involving crimes resulting in personal injury or death which occurred on or after September 1, 1999 would not be eligible for an award for pain and suffering.
source_title: 120-RICR-00-00-2, Rules and Regulations Pertaining to the Crime Victim Compensation Program (version posted by Treasury; active rule effective 11/27/2024)

summary: Rhode Island's Address Confidentiality Program, run by the Department of State, helps victims of domestic violence, stalking, sexual assault, trafficking, or abuse who have moved or are about to move. To qualify, you must live in Rhode Island, fear for your own or your children's safety, live or plan to live at an address the person who harmed you does not know, and agree not to give that person the address. You apply by mailing a sworn application to the Department, which can help you fill it out.
quote: The goal of the Address Confidentiality Program (ACP/Program) is to help victims of domestic violence, stalking, sexual assault, and trafficking and/or abuse as defined by RI Gen. Laws §42-164-2 who have relocated or are about to relocate

summary: Medical, counseling, psychiatric, employment, financial, and investigative records the compensation office gets with a claim are confidential and cannot be released without the applicant's permission unless law allows it. params: {"days":180,"from":"crime","extension":"or of a later date in some cases, such as when police learned it was a crime. With good cause, the program can allow up to 4 years after the crime"}
summary: A claim must be filed within 180 days. The days count from the latest of these: the crime, the victim's death, the day police learned it was a crime, or, for a crime against a minor, the day a resulting injury was diagnosed. With good cause, the time can be extended, but not past 4 years after the crime, the diagnosis, or the death.
quote: A claim must be filed by the claimant not later than one hundred eighty days after the latest of the following events: (1) the occurrence of the crime upon which the claim is based; (2) the death of the victim; (3) the discovery by the law enforcement agency that the occurrence was the result of crime; or (4) the manifestation of a mental or physical injury is diagnosed as a result of a crime committed against a minor. (C) Upon good cause shown, the time for filing may be extended for a period not to exceed four years after the occurrence, diagnosed manifestation, or death.
source_title: S.C. Code Title 16, Chapter 3 (Articles 13, Victim Compensation, incl. 16-3-1110 to 16-3-1360)

summary: The crime must be reported to the proper authority promptly; a report more than 48 hours after the crime is not prompt unless special circumstances justify the delay.
quote: For the purposes of subsection (A)(3), a crime reported more than forty-eight hours after its occurrence is not "promptly reported", absent a showing of special circumstances or causes which justify the delay.
source_title: S.C. Code Title 16, Chapter 3 (Articles 13, Victim Compensation, incl. 16-3-1110 to 16-3-1360)

summary: No award can be made unless the crime was promptly reported and recorded in police records. The crime must have directly caused the victim physical or mental harm. The claimant must also have fully cooperated with all law enforcement agencies and with the program.
quote: No award may be made unless: (1) a crime was committed; (2) the crime directly resulted in physical or psychic trauma to the victim; (3) the crime was promptly reported to the proper authority and recorded in police records; and (4) the claimant or other award recipient has fully cooperated with all law enforcement agencies and with the Office of the Attorney General, South Carolina Crime Victim Services Division, Department of Crime Victim Compensation.
source_title: S.C. Code Title 16, Chapter 3 (Articles 13, Victim Compensation, incl. 16-3-1110 to 16-3-1360)

source_title: SDCL 22-22-26, Forensic medical examination, costs to county

params: {"payer":"the county where the alleged rape or sexual offense occurred"}
summary: The exam cost the county pays includes the provider and facility services for the exam, forensic supplies, scope procedures, lab tests such as STI, HIV, and pregnancy screening, any medication given during the exam, and radiology tied to the exam.
quote: The cost of a forensic medical examination includes: (1) Provider, hospital, or clinic services directly related to the examination; (2) Necessary forensic supplies; (3) Scope procedures directly related to the examination, including anoscopy and colposcopy; (4) Laboratory testing directly related to the examination, including drug screening, urinalysis, pregnancy screening, syphilis screening, chlamydia culture, gonorrhea coverage culture, HIV screening, hepatitis B and C screening, herpes culture, and any other sexually transmitted disease testing directly related to the examination; (5) Any medication provided during the examination; and (6) Any radiology service directly related to the examination.
source_title: SDCL 22-22-26, Forensic medical examination, costs to county

summary: For an exam under section 22-22-26, which has the county where the assault happened pay, hospitals and clinics must tell survivors the exam is available at no cost to them. A survivor does not have to take part in the criminal case or cooperate with police to get the exam. The statute does not say whether the survivor's insurance may be billed.
quote: Each hospital and clinic that provides a forensic medical examination under § 22-22-26 shall coordinate with the county to establish a payment process by which the county shall pay for the cost of the examination, and to notify any victim of rape or sexual offense of the availability of an examination at no cost to the victim. A victim of rape or sexual offense is not required to participate in the criminal justice system or to cooperate with law enforcement to be provided with a forensic medical examination.
source_title: SDCL 22-22-26.2, Forensic medical examinations, payment, notice to victim

summary: The compensation program does not reimburse rape or sexual offense exams that are provided under the county-pay exam statute.

summary: Total compensation for one victim's injury or death may not exceed $15,000.
quote: Compensation granted to any claimant suffering economic loss as the result of injury to or death of any one victim may not exceed fifteen thousand dollars.
source_title: SDCL chapter 23A-28B, Crime Victims' Compensation Program

summary: Except for an emergency award, the commission may go above the limits on single costs when the claimant shows evidence of need. In no case can payments go above the program's overall limit.
quote: With the exception of an emergency award, the commission may deviate from the limits established in this chapter. The claimant must submit evidence to the commission that substantiates the need for the deviation. Based on the evidence submitted, the commission shall determine whether the deviation is warranted. Within 15 days of the commission's decision, the department shall notify the individual in writing. Under no circumstances may payments exceed the program limits established in SDCL 23A-28B-21.
source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

summary: Security devices are covered up to $500, including materials and labor.
quote: Payment for security devices may not exceed $500, including materials and labor.
source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

summary: Basic funeral and burial expenses are capped at $8,000.
quote: Payment for basic funeral and burial expenses may not exceed $8,000.
source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

summary: Homicide scene cleanup is capped at $1,500.
quote: Payment for homicide scene cleanup may not exceed one thousand five hundred dollars.
source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

summary: Lost earnings are paid based on the victim's average monthly earnings for the 6 months before the injury or the monthly minimum wage, whichever is less. The monthly minimum wage is the federal hourly minimum wage times 173.2 hours.
quote: Loss of earnings, loss of future earnings, and loss of support shall be determined on the basis of the victim's average monthly earnings for the six months immediately preceding the date of injury, or the monthly minimum wage as of the date of the crime underlying the claim, whichever is less. The monthly minimum wage shall be based upon the federal hourly minimum wage in effect as of the date of the crime multiplied by 173.2 hours per month.
source_title: SDCL chapter 23A-28B, Crime Victims' Compensation Program

summary: When the victim is the claimant, lost earnings are paid only for the 12 months right after the crime.
quote: Payment for lost earnings or loss of future earnings is limited to the following: (1) If the claimant is the victim, the 12-month period immediately following the date of the crime;
source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

summary: Mental health services are covered, including individual or group counseling by a qualified mental health professional, for a limited number of months after the crime.
quote: Payment for mental health services is limited to assessment, diagnosis, and treatment, including individual or group counseling sessions provided by a mental health professional
source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

summary: If the victim was a juvenile at the time of the crime and the late-filing deadline is waived for good cause, mental health services can be paid for up to 24 months from the date of the application.
quote: If the victim is a juvenile, or was a juvenile at the time of victimization, and there is good cause to waive the one-year requirement under SDCL 23A-28B-25 , payment for mental health services may be made for up to 24 months from the date of the application.
source_title: ARSD 67:55:04:03, Mental health services

summary: Covered medical expense includes medical and dental services, mental health counseling, dental and prosthetic devices, and eyeglasses or other corrective lenses.
quote: "Medical expense," the cost of all medical and dental services, mental health counseling, dental and prosthetic devices, eyeglasses or other corrective lenses
source_title: SDCL chapter 23A-28B, Crime Victims' Compensation Program

summary: Payment for medical expenses is limited to medical services provided in the 12 months right after the crime. The department may extend this 12-month period for good cause.
quote: payment for medical expenses is limited to those medical services provided during the 12-month period immediately following the date the crime occurred. The department may extend this 12-month period if good cause is shown.
source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

summary: Medical services are paid only if given in the 12 months after the crime. The department may extend this for good cause. This 12-month limit does not apply to mental health care or to medicine for a mental condition.
quote: Except for mental health expenses covered under § 67:55:04:03 and the costs of medications related to the treatment of a mental condition, payment for medical expenses is limited to those medical services provided during the 12-month period immediately following the date the crime occurred. The department may extend this 12-month period if good cause is shown.
source_title: ARSD article 67:55, Crime victims' compensation

summary: A covered crime is conduct in South Dakota that is punishable as a felony or misdemeanor and causes personal injury or death.
quote: "Crime," conduct that occurs or is attempted in this state, including that arising from domestic violence, human trafficking, and acts of terrorism, as defined in 18 USC § 2331 as of January 1, 1997, which conduct results in personal injury or death and is punishable as a felony or misdemeanor
source_title: SDCL chapter 23A-28B, Crime Victims' Compensation Program

summary: Personal injury includes emotional distress, not only bodily harm.
quote: "Personal injury," actual bodily harm or emotional distress
source_title: SDCL chapter 23A-28B, Crime Victims' Compensation Program

summary: An award can be made whether or not anyone is prosecuted or convicted for the crime.
quote: An award of compensation may be made without regard to whether any person is prosecuted or convicted for the criminal conduct that is the basis of the award.
source_title: SDCL chapter 23A-28B, Crime Victims' Compensation Program

params: {"rule":"Crimes in South Dakota are covered. A South Dakota resident hurt by a crime outside the state may apply only if that place has no compensation law covering the injury (or, per ARSD 67:55:01:09, the person applied there and was found ineligible)."}

quote: If a resident of South Dakota is a victim of a crime as defined in § 23A-28B-1 , but the crime occurred outside the boundaries of this state, the resident has the same rights under the provisions of this chapter as if the crime had occurred within this state upon a showing that the state, territory, country, or political subdivision of a country in which the crime occurred does not have a crime victims' compensation law which covers the injury or death suffered by the resident.
source_title: SDCL chapter 23A-28B, Crime Victims' Compensation Program

source_title: SDCL chapter 23A-28B, Crime Victims' Compensation Program

summary: A victim of a covered sexually-oriented crime gets the forensic medical exam free. No bill may be sent to the victim and the facility may not hold the victim responsible for payment. The statute does not say whether the victim's insurance may be billed.
quote: shall be entitled to forensic medical examinations without charge to the victim. No bill for the examination shall be submitted to the victim, nor shall the medical facility hold the victim responsible for payment.
source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-118 (forensic medical examinations in sexual assault cases), 2025 via Justia

summary: A provider paid by the fund for a forensic exam may not bill the victim for any additional cost of the exam.
quote: No provider receiving compensation pursuant to this section shall bill the victim for any additional cost related to the forensic medical examination.
source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-118 (forensic medical examinations in sexual assault cases), 2025 via Justia

params: {"payer":"Tennessee Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund (claim filed by the health care provider)"}
summary: Forensic exam claims are paid from the state Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund.
quote: All claims for forensic medical examinations are eligible for payment from the criminal injuries compensation fund, created under § 40-24-107.
source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-118 (forensic medical examinations in sexual assault cases), 2025 via Justia

summary: A victim does not have to report to police or cooperate with prosecution for the forensic exam to be paid.
quote: the victims shall not be required to report the incident to law enforcement officers or to cooperate in the prosecution of the crime in order to be eligible for payment of forensic medical examinations
source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-118 (forensic medical examinations in sexual assault cases), 2025 via Justia

params: {"payer":"Tennessee Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund pays the health care provider directly; the payment is full compensation to the provider"}
summary: The fund pays the provider up to $1,000 for a forensic exam, and that payment counts as full payment, so the provider cannot bill the victim for the rest.
quote: The amount of compensation that may be awarded under this section shall not exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000), and shall constitute full compensation to the health care provider that provided the service.
source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-118 (forensic medical examinations in sexual assault cases), 2025 via Justia

quote: For crimes occurring on or after July 1, 2025: $34,100
pinpoint: Treasury Maximum Expense Amounts (June 2025); set under T.C.A. 29-13-106(h)
source_title: Tennessee Treasury, Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund Maximum Expense Amounts (June 2025)

quote: Compensation must not be awarded for any personal injury or loss alleged to have been incurred as a result of pain and suffering, except for victims of the crime of rape, victims of a human trafficking offense, and victims of a crime involving sexual deviancy
source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-106 (losses or expenses reimbursable; maximum award), 2025 via Justia

summary: A pain and suffering award for a victim of a sexually-oriented crime may not exceed $3,000.
quote: Any award based on the pain and suffering experienced by a claimant victimized by a sexually-oriented crime is to be made in an amount deemed necessary and appropriate, not to exceed three thousand dollars ($3,000)
source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-107 (standards for amount of compensation; sub-limits), 2025 via Justia

quote: In the case of a sexually-oriented crime committed against a victim who is under eighteen (18) years of age, where the compensation is for unreimbursed or unreimbursable mental health counseling or treatment made necessary by the sexually-oriented crime, any sibling or non-offending custodial parent of the victim, or both
source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-105 (persons eligible), 2025 via Justia

quote: Any counseling services must be necessary due to the injury and may be considered for the victim up to the maximum award.
pinpoint: Program page, Eligible (Covered) Expenses Explained: Medical Bills/Mental Health Counseling
source_title: Tennessee Treasury, Criminal Injuries Compensation program page (eligibility, Apply for Compensation, FAQ)

summary: Expenses actually and reasonably incurred because of the injury, including medical and hospital services, are covered.
quote: Expenses actually and reasonably incurred as a result of the personal injury or death of the victim, including, but not limited to, actual expenditures of moneys for or indebtedness resulting from medical services, hospital services, funeral and burial expenses
source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-106 (losses or expenses reimbursable; maximum award), 2025 via Justia

summary: Lost wages caused by the crime are paid on the workers' compensation temporary total disability schedule, but at 85 percent of the claimant's average weekly wage.
quote: Any award made for lost wages proximately caused by a violent crime is to be based upon those schedules of compensation for temporary total disability allowable by the workers' compensation statutes, found in § 50-6-207, in effect at the time of the commission of the crime giving rise to such claim; provided, however, that the sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66⅔%) rate prescribed in the workers' compensation statutes shall not be used in determining the amount of any award hereunder. Instead, such rate shall be eighty-five percent (85%) of the claimant's average weekly wage.
source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-107 (standards for amount of compensation; sub-limits), 2025 via Justia

params: {"expense":"relocation","count_limit":2,"scope":"moving costs, if the assault happened at your home, for up to 2 moves"}
summary: If you move because of an assault at your home, reasonable moving costs, storage fees, and fees to move your utilities are covered. This is for no more than 2 moves.
quote: The victim's reasonable moving expenses, storage fees and fees for transfer of utility service if the move is a direct result of an assault committed upon such victim at the victim's residence, provided that the victim shall not receive compensation for more than two (2) moves resulting from the assault
source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-106 (losses or expenses reimbursable; maximum award), 2025 via Justia

params: {"expense":"crime_scene_cleanup","scope":"cleaning the scene, if it was your home or a relative's home"}
summary: Reasonable costs to clean the scene of a sexual assault are covered when the scene was the home of the victim or a relative.
quote: Reasonable out-of-pocket expenses incurred for cleaning supplies, equipment rental and labor needed to clean the scene of a homicide, sexual assault or aggravated assault, if the scene was the residence of the victim or a relative of the victim
source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-106 (losses or expenses reimbursable; maximum award), 2025 via Justia

summary: Crime scene cleanup is capped at $3,000.
quote: Any award made for expenses under § 29-13-106(a)(4) shall not exceed three thousand dollars ($3,000)
source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-107 (standards for amount of compensation; sub-limits), 2025 via Justia

summary: Travel to and from the offender's trial and later appeals is paid up to a cumulative $1,250 for each claimant.
quote: Any award made under the preceding sentence to a claimant shall not exceed a cumulative total of one thousand two hundred fifty dollars ($1,250) for all such travel.
source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-106 (losses or expenses reimbursable; maximum award), 2025 via Justia

source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-107 (standards for amount of compensation; sub-limits), 2025 via Justia

source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-106 (losses or expenses reimbursable; maximum award), 2025 via Justia

quote: Reasonable costs of cleaning, repairing or replacing eyeglasses and hearing aids owned by the victim that were damaged or destroyed by the crime or the processing of the crime scene
source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-106 (losses or expenses reimbursable; maximum award), 2025 via Justia

params: {"expense":"property_replacement","scope":"repairing or replacing things damaged when police processed the scene at your home or a relative's home"}
summary: The program covers reasonable costs to repair or replace property of the victim or a relative that was damaged when police processed the scene. This is for a sexual assault, homicide, or aggravated assault at the home of the victim or of the relative who owned the property.
quote: the reasonable costs of repairing or replacing personal property owned by the victim or a relative of the victim as defined in § 29-13-102 that was damaged or destroyed in processing the scene of a homicide, sexual assault or aggravated assault if the scene was the residence of the victim or the relative of the victim who owned the property.
source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-106 (losses or expenses reimbursable; maximum award), 2025 via Justia

summary: A claim must be filed within 2 years after the crime. For listed sexual offenses against a minor, it can also be filed within 2 years after a resulting injury is diagnosed, and good cause can extend the time.
quote: A claim for compensation must be filed not later than two (2) years after the occurrence of the crime upon which the claim is based, two (2) years after the death of the victim, or two (2) years after any mental or physical manifestation or injury is diagnosed as a result of an act committed against a minor that would constitute a criminal offense under §§ 39-13-502 – 39-13-505, § 39-13-522, § 39-15-302, § 39-17-902, or §§ 39-17-1003 – 39-17-1005, or an attempt, conspiracy, or solicitation to commit such offenses; provided, that upon good cause shown, the time period for filing such claim may be extended either before or after the expiration of the filing period.
source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-108 (claims; filing period; reporting), 2025 via Justia

summary: Some sex crimes against a minor allow more time. A claim can also be filed within 2 years after a mental or physical injury from the crime is diagnosed.
quote: two (2) years after any mental or physical manifestation or injury is diagnosed as a result of an act committed against a minor that would constitute a criminal offense under §§ 39-13-502 – 39-13-505, § 39-13-522, § 39-15-302, § 39-17-902, or §§ 39-17-1003 – 39-17-1005, or an attempt, conspiracy, or solicitation to commit such offenses
source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-108 (claims; filing period; reporting), 2025 via Justia

params: {"required":true,"within_days":15,"alternatives":[],"exception":"or later if there is good cause, which can include sexual assault"}
summary: The crime must be reported to the proper authorities within 15 days, but a late report can be excused for good cause, and being a victim of sexual assault is a listed reason for good cause.
quote: A claim cannot be filed until the crime upon which the claim is based has been reported by the victim, or a member of the victim's family, to the proper authorities within fifteen (15) days after the occurrence of such crime unless, for good cause shown, it is found that the delay was justified. Good cause for the failure of a victim or a member of the victim's family to report a crime may be found if the victim is: (1) Physically unable; (2) A victim of sexual assault;
source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-108 (claims; filing period; reporting), 2025 via Justia

summary: Proof that the crime happened can come from documents other than a police report, such as medical records from a health care provider or a restraining order issued by a court. This is proof of the offense only; it does not replace the timely report to law enforcement that a compensation claim still needs.
quote: (vii) Medical records from a healthcare provider, as those terms are defined in § 9-8-408; (viii) A written communication from a prosecuting attorney or investigating law enforcement officer who has personal involvement in the prosecution or investigation of any criminal case relative to the claim filed; (ix) A report from child protective services or another government agency; (x) A restraining order issued by a court;
source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-103 (burden of proof; documentation; proof of offense), 2025 via Justia

summary: To qualify, the claimant needs at least $100 in out-of-pocket loss or at least 2 continuous weeks of lost earnings or support, unless the limit would not serve the interest of justice.
quote: no award shall be made unless the claimant has incurred a minimum out of pocket loss of one hundred dollars ($100) or has lost at least two (2) continuous weeks earnings or support, unless it is determined that the interest of justice would not be served by such a limitation
source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-106 (losses or expenses reimbursable; maximum award), 2025 via Justia

summary: Awards are reduced by money received or legally owed from the offender or any other public or private source, such as insurance.
quote: Any award shall be reduced by the amounts of payment already received or any amounts which claimant is legally entitled to receive as a result of the injury: (A) From or on behalf of the offender; (B) From any other public or private source;
source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-106 (losses or expenses reimbursable; maximum award), 2025 via Justia

summary: In deciding whether to award, or how much, the program may consider the victim's behavior that directly or indirectly contributed to the injury.
quote: In determining whether to make an award under this section, or the amount of the award, any circumstances reasonably relevant to the criminal act may be considered, including the behavior of the victim which directly or indirectly contributed to the victim's injury or death
source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-109 (claims requirements; awards; victim conduct; cooperation), 2025 via Justia

summary: An emergency award can be no more than $500.

summary: The division must make every effort to approve or deny a claim within 90 days of receiving it.
quote: the division shall investigate every claim for compensation and shall make every effort to honor or deny each claim within ninety (90) days of receipt of the claim
source_title: T.C.A. 29-13-108 (claims; filing period; reporting), 2025 via Justia
